Like those who circulate false and counterfeit coins, they would not want any touchstone [?] or index to exist by which they might be tested. This first usefulness, therefore, is very great.

units.la: Secunda est: quòd cùm venit Christus, Ecclesia habuit apertissimum certissimumque testimonium de completis in Christo omnibus, quæ de ipso erant vaticiniis, figuris, typis, atque ita certior facta, hunc Iesum esse Christum, eum amplexa est, & per eum est seruata: & ut alij etiam omnes seruentur iisdem scripturis demonstrat & euincit, hunc crucificrucifixum, verum esse Messiam, verumque seruatorem. Quanta haec est vtilitas?
units.tr: The second is this: that when Christ came, the Church had a most clear and most certain testimony of all the things fulfilled in Christ that had been prophesied, figured and typified concerning him; and so, being made more certain that this Jesus is the Christ, it embraced him and was preserved through him; and by the same Scriptures it demonstrates and proves to all others that this crucified man is the true Messiah and the true Saviour, so that they too may be saved. How great is this usefulness?

units.la: Atq; hic est vnus ex praecipuis finibus, cur Deus voluerit ante Christi aduentum, per Mosen & Prophetas in literas referri, quaecunq; de Messia ex spiritu Dei vaticinabantur: & omnes typi ac figurae, quae de ipso erant: vaticinia, inquam, & typi, tam de tempore aduentus Christi, & de familia, vnde, & de loco, vbi erat nasciturus: quàm de eius miraculis, de eius doctrina, de eius passionis & mortis genere: denique & de eius resurrectione & ascensione: vt cùm postea venisset, & quaecunq; fuerant de ipso praedicta, adimpleret: omnes Electi agnoscerent, hunc Iesum, verum esse Messiam, & per eum agnitum & fide receptum, seruarentur: Qui vero nollent agnoscere reprobi & infideles, inexcusabiles redderentur. Imò haec eadem est causa, cur non contentus Deus omnia haec in literas Hebraicas esse relata: voluit etiam, vt iis in linguam Graecam conuersis, eadem Mosis & Prophetarum vaticinia, cum tota salutis doctrina, apud Gentes extarent: vt cùm postea Apostoli ad ipsas venissent, praedicatum Christum: euincere possent testimoniis eorundem librorum, qui apud ipsos Gentiles essent, hunc quem praedicarent Iesum, verum esse Messiam & seruatorem Mundi, longè ante per Prophetas promissum: & hunc non solum pro Iudæis, verum etiam pro salute Gentium, mortuum esse: ac proinde salutem & gratiam, non tantùm ad Iudaeos, verùm etiam ad ipsos Gentiles pertinere, quandoquidem de ipsorum quoq; vocatione ad gratiam Euangelij, luculentissima haberent in Mose, & Prophetis testimonia. Quamobrem videmus primùm Christum ipsum iis vsum scripturis, ad demonstrandum se illum esse, qui venturus expectabatur salvator Mundi: & quem oportebat pati, & ita intrare in gloriam suam. Luc.24. Et exorsus à Mose & à Prophetis, interpretabatur in omnibus scripturis, quæ de ipso erant. Quomodo potuisset tam facile hoc demonstrari, nisi extitissent scripturæ? Ita reliquos omnes, ad has scripturas, tanquam ad certissimum de se testimonium ablegabat. Ioan.5. Scrutamini scripturas, quia illæ testimonium perhibent de me.
units.tr: And this is one of the chief purposes why God willed that, before the coming of Christ, through Moses and the Prophets, whatever the Spirit of God prophesied concerning the Messiah should be written down, and all the types and figures that concerned him: the prophecies and types, I say, both concerning the time of Christ's coming, and the family from which he would come, and the place where he was to be born, as well as concerning his miracles, his doctrine, the manner of his passion and death, and finally his resurrection and ascension; so that when he afterwards came and fulfilled whatever had been foretold of him, all the elect might recognise that this Jesus is the true Messiah, and that, being recognised through him and received by faith, they might be saved; but those who would not recognise him, the reprobate and unbelieving, would be made inexcusable. Indeed, this same is the reason why God, not content that all these things were related in Hebrew letters, willed also that, once translated into the Greek language, the same prophecies of Moses and the Prophets, together with the whole doctrine of salvation, should be available among the Gentiles; so that when the Apostles afterwards came to them and preached Christ, they might be able to prove, by the testimonies of those same books which were among the Gentiles themselves, that this Jesus whom they preached is the true Messiah and Saviour of the world, promised long before through the Prophets; and that he died not only for the Jews but also for the salvation of the Gentiles; and that therefore salvation and grace pertain not only to the Jews but also to the Gentiles themselves, since they had in Moses and the Prophets most clear testimonies concerning their own calling to the grace of the Gospel. Wherefore we see, first, that Christ himself used the Scriptures for this purpose, to demonstrate that he is the one who was expected to come as Saviour of the world, and who had to suffer and so enter into his glory. Luke 24: And beginning from Moses and from the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself. How could this have been demonstrated so easily, had the Scriptures not existed? Thus he referred all the rest to these Scriptures, as to the most certain testimony concerning himself. John 5: Search the Scriptures, for they testify of me.

units.la: Deinde videmus idem factum fuisse ab Euangelistis. Cùm enim narrant, aliquid ab ipso gestum fuisse, aut ipsum aliquid passum esse: mox citant scripturas, quæ de ea re prædixerant: vt ostendant in hoc Iesu impleta esse omnia, quæ de Messia prædicta fuerant à Prophetis. Exempla passim occurrunt in Euangelistis, Incipe ab ipsius conceptione in vtero virginis: & videbis ab Euangelistis confestim citari testimonia Prophetarum Matth.1. Posteaquam descripsit, quomodo Angelus venisset ad virginem Mariam, & annunciasset, in ipsius vtero, è Spiritu sancto, sine viri semine conceptum iri Filium'Dei, Messiam, & vocatum iri Iesum, id est, seruatorem: mox subdit testimonium Prophetæ Iesaiæ dicendo: Hoc autem totum factum est, vt impleretur quod dictum est, per Prophetam, dicentem, Ecce virgo concipiet, &c. & vocabis nomen eius Immanuel. Quid Apostoli in suis concionibus & epistolis, tam ad Iudæos, quàm ad Gentiles? Eandem sequuntur rationem: omnia in Iesu adimpleta esse demonstrant, eoque hunc verum esse Christum. Act.10. Huic (inquit Petrus) testimonium perhibent omnes Prophetæ, remissionem peccatorum accipere omnes qui credunt in eum. 2.Cor.1. Quotquot enim (sunt) promissiones Dei: in ipso (Christo Iesu) sunt. Etiam (id est complementum habent:) & in ipso (Christo) sunt Amen, hoc est, perfectum habent complementum. Quis non videat, quanta sit hæc altera vtilitas scripturarum? Ergo, vt suo tempore constaret omnibus, quæcunq; prædicta fuerunt de Christo, deq; eius Ecclesia & vocatione Gentium: adimpleta esse in Iesu Filio Mariæ, eoq; hunc verum esse Messiam, seruatoremque Mundi, non tam Iudæorum, quàm etiam Gentium: voluit Deus, vt illa omnia, cum tota salutis doctrina, scriptis committerentur, non tantum Hebraicis, sed etiam Græcis.
units.tr: Then we see that the same was done by the Evangelists. For when they relate that something was done by him, or that he suffered something, they straightway cite the Scriptures which had foretold that matter, to show that in this Jesus all things were fulfilled which had been foretold of the Messiah by the Prophets. Examples occur everywhere in the Evangelists. Begin from his conception in the womb of the Virgin, and you will see that the Evangelists at once cite the testimonies of the Prophets, Matthew 1. After he had described how the angel came to the Virgin Mary and announced that the Son of God, the Messiah, would be conceived in her womb by the Holy Spirit without the seed of a man, and that he would be called Jesus, that is, Saviour, he immediately adds the testimony of the Prophet Isaiah, saying: Now all this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall conceive, etc., and you shall call his name Immanuel. What do the Apostles do in their sermons and epistles, both to the Jews and to the Gentiles? They follow the same method: they demonstrate that all things were fulfilled in Jesus, and thereby that he is the true Christ. Acts 10: To him (says Peter) all the Prophets bear witness, that through his name everyone who believes in him receives remission of sins. 2 Cor. 1: For however many are the promises of God, in him (Christ Jesus) they are yes; and in him (Christ) they are Amen, that is, they have their complete fulfilment. Who does not see how great this second usefulness of the Scriptures is? Therefore, so that in its own time it might be evident to all that whatever had been prophesied about Christ, and about his Church and the calling of the Gentiles, was fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of Mary, and thereby that he is the true Messiah and Saviour of the world, not only of the Jews but also of the Gentiles, God willed that all those things, together with the whole doctrine of salvation, should be committed to writing, not only in Hebrew but also in Greek.

units.la: Tertia vtilitas fuit specialis Gentium vo-catio & salus. Idcirco enim voluit Domi-nus, vt per Mosen & Prophetas Hebraicis literis tota illa doctrina, quæ antea solita erat sola viua voce tradi, conscriberetur: vt ex ea lingua in Græcam, & deinde etiam in Latinam & in alias transferri posset: atq; itá ad omnes Gentes illa doctrina, & per doctrinam salus propagari commodè posset: aut si qui eam nollent amplecti, iis omnis tolleretur excusatio. Ioan.15. Si non venissem, & non locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non habe-rent (per concessionem & μιμητικῶς[?] dicitur:) nunc autem excusationem non habent de peccato suo. Ita dico de scripturis, Si Dominus non misisset scripturas ad omnes Gentes, ipsarumque linguas conuersas: potuissent & possent fortassis aliquid suæ iniquitati & improbitati prætexere: quòd scilicet Spiritus sancti illuminationibus destituantur: quòd non habeant Ministros, qui se doceant: quòd non etiam vacet, aut possint commodè eò se conferre, vbi prædicatur Verbum: sed cùm habeant scripturam in omnes fere linguas conuersam, è qua possint viam salutis cognoscere: nihil amplius illis relinquitur excusationis. Certè nos, quanta sit hæc vtilitas, quam ex Bibliorum versione capiunt fideles, re ipsa sentimus.
units.tr: The third benefit was the special calling and salvation of the Gentiles. For this reason the Lord willed that, through Moses and the Prophets, the whole of that teaching, which before had been handed down by the living voice alone, should be written down in Hebrew letters, so that it could be conveniently translated from that language into Greek, and then also into Latin and other languages; and thus that teaching, and salvation through that teaching, could be conveniently spread to all nations; or, if any were unwilling to embrace it, that every excuse might be taken away from them. John 15: "If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin" (this is said by way of concession and [μιμητικῶς?]); "but now they have no excuse for their sin." I say the same of the Scriptures: if the Lord had not sent the Scriptures to all nations, translated into their languages, they could perhaps have pleaded something in excuse of their iniquity and wickedness, namely that they lacked the illuminations of the Holy Spirit, that they had no ministers to teach them, that they had no leisure or could not conveniently betake themselves to where the Word is preached. But since they have Scripture translated into almost all languages, from which they can learn the way of salvation, no further excuse is left to them. Certainly we ourselves feel in fact how great this benefit is, which the faithful receive from the translation of the Bible.

units.la: Quarta vtilitas est, quòd hæc scriptura, Ecclesiæ Dei est instar fortissimæ & inexpu-gnabilis turris, in qua & ipsum cœlestis sa-pientiæ thesaurum sincerum, & seipsam mú-dam & saluam contra omnes hostes con-feruat. Id quod certè non posset facilè fieri, si doctrinam Dei scriptis comprehensam non haberehaberemus. Etenim nunquam defuerunt, nec desunt, nec defuturi sunt inimici & ho-stes, qui omnibus modis conentur verâ Dei & salutis cognitionem, aut penitus è Mundo tollere, aut saltem contaminare, eoq; & salu-tem nostram impedire. Quid non egit & agit Satan per tyrannos, vt totam funditus tol-lar veram religionem? aut curat, vt bellis, gladiis & ignibus omnes tollantur pij è me-dio. Sic egit per Athaliam, cùm omne semen Regium è tribu Iuda interficiendũ curauit. Sic per Romanos, Neronces, Valerianos, De-cios, Diocletianos. Sic per Antiochum; sic denique per Antichristum & impios tyran-nos: quantum in ipsis est, omnem mouent lapidem, vt in quibuscunque viget hæc do-ctrina salutis, ij tollantur è medio. Finis Sathanæ in iis tyrannis quis est? Vt iis interfe-ctis, tota tollatur pietatis doctrina. Si enim hæc doctrina in mentibus tantum esset fide-lium, & non etiam in scripturis conseruare-tur: profecto sublatis omnibus piis, tota etiam pietatis doctrina, foret extincta. Ergo, vt hæc seruetur, voluit Deus eam libris com-prehendi: & horum librorum numerum in-finitum vbiq; terrarum asseruari.
units.tr: The fourth benefit is that this Scripture is to the Church of God like a most strong and impregnable tower, in which it both preserves the pure treasure of heavenly wisdom and itself safe and unharmed against all enemies. This certainly could not easily be done if we did not have the doctrine of God comprehended in writings. For there never have been, nor are there now, nor will there ever be wanting enemies and foes, who by every means try either to remove the true knowledge of God and salvation utterly from the world, or at least to corrupt it, and thereby to hinder our salvation. What has Satan not done, and what does he not do through tyrants, so that the true religion may be utterly removed? Or he takes care that all the godly are removed from the midst by wars, swords and fires. So he acted through Athaliah, when she took care that all the royal seed of the tribe of Judah should be slain. So through the Romans: Nero, Valerian, Decius, Diocletian. So through Antiochus; so finally through the Antichrist and impious tyrants: as far as in them lies, they turn over every stone so that wherever this doctrine of salvation flourishes, those who hold it may be removed from the midst. What is Satan's end in those tyrants? That, when they have been slain, the whole doctrine of piety may be removed. For if this doctrine were in the minds of the faithful only, and were not also preserved in the Scriptures, then surely, with all the godly removed, the whole doctrine of piety would also be extinguished. Therefore, so that it may be preserved, God willed that it be comprehended in books; and that the number of these books be asserted to be unlimited everywhere on earth.

units.la: Si non possit omnes pios è medio tolle- re, curat ipsos saltem libros comburendos & abolendos, & ita totam veram religionem dissipandam. Sed Dominus tot horum libro-rum exemplaria voluit extare: vt semper vera doctrina in Mundo seruetur. Quoties in ipso etiam veteri Testamento hoc contigit? Melachim,id est 4.Reg.22. diu latuerant libri Legis, culpa & vitio impiorum Regum, Achabi & aliorum:atque ita corrupta & dissipata religio fuit. Sed quid Dominus? Effecit,vt tandem repertus sit liber,tempore losiæ quæ in templo abdiderant pij Pontifices: ita factum, vt religio sit instaurata ex lege & doctrina Dei. Quantum profuit tunc,doctrinā pietatis in libros fuisse relatam? & exemplar vnum in Templo fuisse repertum? Idem contigit sub Iosaphato,2.Paral.17. Item,post reditū populi è captiuitate Babylonica, quā de re Esdræ lib.2. qui inscribitur Nehemiæ, cap.8. Quoties exusti sacri libri, quotquot reperiri potuerunt? Vt sub Antiocho, sub Diocletiano. Sed Deus sæpe voluit aliquod exemplar asseruari. Quā de re 1. Mach.1. Et Euseb. Cæsar. histor. Ecclesiast. lib. g.cap.1. Quantum igitur profuit illis temporibus, cœlestem doctrinam in libris fuisse asserua- tam? Idem dico de nostris temporibus.
units.tr: If he cannot remove all the godly from the midst, he takes care that the books themselves be burned and destroyed, and so the whole true religion be scattered. But the Lord willed that many copies of these books should exist, so that true doctrine might always be preserved in the world. How often has this happened even in the Old Testament itself? In Melachim, that is, 4 Kings 22, the books of the Law lay hidden for a long time, through the fault and vice of impious kings, Ahab and others; and thus religion was corrupted and scattered. But what did the Lord do? He brought it about that at last a book was found, in the time of Josiah, which the godly high priests had hidden in the Temple; so it came about that religion was restored from the law and doctrine of God. How much did it then profit that the doctrine of piety had been committed to books, and that one copy had been found in the Temple? The same happened under Jehoshaphat, 2 Chronicles 17. Likewise, after the return of the people from the Babylonian captivity, concerning which see Esdras, book 2, which is entitled Nehemiah, chapter 8. How often were the sacred books burned, as many as could be found? As under Antiochus, under Diocletian. But God often willed that some copy be preserved. On this matter see 1 Maccabees 1, and Eusebius of Caesarea, Ecclesiastical History, book 9, chapter 1. How much, then, did it profit in those times that heavenly doctrine had been preserved in books? I say the same of our own times.

units.la: Aut si non possit Sathan vel pios, vel li- bros ipsos omnes per tyrannos tollere: cu- rat,vt per Antichristos & Hæreticos aut cor- rumpantur,aut falsis interpretationibus de- prauentur, & ita religionem inficiat. Addit deinde ipse, quippe qui se in Angelum lucis transfigurat,addit,inquam, vana omnia,falsa miracula, & infinitas imposturas, quibus falsas illas interpretationes, & religionis corruptelas confirmet, ac tanquam diuinas persuapersuadeat: ita vt si fieri possit, etiam electi in errorem inducantur. Quid hic ageret Ecclesia: nisi verbum Domini in scripturis purum & sincerum haberet? Sed bene est: ipsi Electi continent se in scripturis, & iis diiudicant reliquas omnes doctrinas & interpretationes. Ita non falluntur, nec falli possunt. Et huc spectat Apostoli adhortatio 2. Timoth. 3. Permane tu in iis, quae didicisti, & quae tibi credita sunt, sciens à quo didiceris, &c. Quanta est haec vtilitas sacrarum Literarum?
units.tr: Or if Satan cannot remove, through tyrants, either the godly or all the books themselves: he takes care that they be either corrupted through Antichrists and heretics, or depraved by false interpretations, and so infect religion. Then he himself adds, since he transforms himself into an angel of light, he adds, I say, all kinds of vain things, false miracles, and endless impostures, by which he may confirm those false interpretations and corruptions of religion, and persuade them as if they were divine; so that, if it were possible, even the elect would be led into error. What would the Church do here, unless it had the Word of the Lord pure and sincere in the Scriptures? But it is well: the elect themselves hold to the Scriptures, and by them they judge all the other doctrines and interpretations. Thus they are not deceived, nor can they be deceived. To this belongs the exhortation of the Apostle, 2 Timothy 3: "But continue in the things you have learned, and that have been entrusted to you, knowing from whom you learned them," etc. How great is this benefit of the Holy Scriptures?

units.la: Quid? quòd etiam Electi ac pij homines saepenumero aut curis huius seculi nimium occupati: aut à voluptatibus carnis abrepti; aut otio & negligentia audiendi Verbi à Pastoribus: obliuiscuntur doctrinam coelestem, si non totam: magna ex parte? Saepe etiam propter varias calamitates, bella, clades, pestilentias, publicum Verbi Ministerium intermittitur. Quid tum fideles, si non secum haberent libros sacros, quorum lectione pietatis doctrina in animis conseruetur? aut obliuioni tradita, in memoriâ renocetur? Est igitur scriptura ceu turris fortissima, in qua doctrina salutis in æternum conseruatur, & ex consequenti Electorum salus promouetur. Quamobrem recte à nobis responsum est ad quaestionem de principio: Cur Deus voluerit doctrinam salutis, post tot annos & secula, tandem per Mosen primum, deinde per Prophetas, postremo per Apostolos, in chartas & libros referri: hoc Deum voluisse propter Ecclesiæ suæ vtilitatem & salutem. Ergo & quando eam voluit sine scripto propagari: & quando in libris conseruari; vtrumque fecit DEVS propter salutem Electo-rum. Atque hæc de sexta quæstione satis.
units.tr: What then? Even the elect and godly men, very often either too much occupied with the cares of this age, or carried away by the pleasures of the flesh, or by idleness and neglect of hearing the Word from the ministers, forget the heavenly doctrine, if not wholly, then for the most part. Often too, because of various calamities, wars, slaughters and pestilences, the public ministry of the Word is interrupted. What then would the faithful do, if they did not have the sacred books with them, by whose reading the doctrine of piety is preserved in their souls, or, handed over to oblivion, is recalled to memory? Scripture is therefore like a most strong tower, in which the doctrine of salvation is preserved for ever, and as a consequence the salvation of the elect is advanced. Wherefore we have rightly answered the question at the beginning: why God willed that the doctrine of salvation, after so many years and ages, should at last be committed to paper and books, first through Moses, then through the Prophets, and lastly through the Apostles: that God willed this for the usefulness and salvation of his Church. Therefore, whether he willed it to be spread without writing, or to be preserved in books, God did both for the salvation of the elect. And that is enough on the sixth question.

units.la: QVÆSTIO VII.
units.tr: QUESTION VII.

units.la: De fine, propter quem data sunt scripturæ sanctæ, eoq; de illarum vtilitate.
units.tr: On the end for which the Holy Scriptures were given, and therefore on their usefulness.

units.la: Tractavimus hactenus duas, easque etiam absoluimus quæstiones: quarum prior fuit de origine, deque progressu verbi Dei in Ecclesia. Vbi præter alia vidimus, duabus in summa rationibus usum fuisse Deum in revelando, propagando, & conservando suo in Ecclesia verbo: nimirum viva voce, sine ulla externa scriptione: idque à condito orbe, usque ad Mosen, per annos circiter bis mille & quadringentos. Deinde usum fuisse etiam scriptionibus: idque primùm per Mosen, deinde etiam per Prophetas, postremò per Apostolos: post quos Apostolos, nulla unquam fuit [illegible, ~12 letters], neq; etiam expectanda est.
units.tr: Up to now we have treated two questions and have also finished them. The first was about the origin and progress of the Word of God in the Church. There we saw, among other things, that God used two main methods in revealing, spreading and preserving his Word in the Church: namely, by the living voice without any outward writing, and this from the creation of the world until Moses, a period of about two thousand four hundred years. Then he also used writings: first through Moses, then also through the Prophets, and finally through the Apostles. After those Apostles there was never, and is not to be expected, any [illegible, about 12 letters].

units.la: Altera quæstio fuit de causis, propter quas Deus voluit primùm viva voce, sine ullo scripto, verbum suum in Ecclesia propagari: deinde, illud etiam tandem in literas librosq; referri, & in varias trānsferri linguas. Et horum S. librorum plenum esse terrarum orbem: & eos in finem usque mundi asseruari. Vtrumque diximus factum fuisse propter bonum & vtilitatem Ecclesiæ. Ac quod ad primum, de sola viua voce attinet: ostendimus, vtilius & gratius fuisse primitiuç illi Ecclesiæ, quæ Mosen præcesserit: quòd Deus ea cum Patribus illis egerit ratione, nempe apparitionibus & colloquiis Filij sui, afflatibus Spiritus S. visionibus Angelorum, cum viuo efficacique sanctorum hominum ministerio coniunctis: quàm si illis cœlestibus agendi & docendi rationibus destituti, solum scriptum accepissent verbum. Longè enim vtilius es-se, Filium Dei præsentem audire, quàm solas eius literas legere.
units.tr: The second question was about the causes for which God wished first to spread his Word in the Church by the living voice alone, without any writing, and then also at last to have it recorded in letters and books and translated into various languages. We said that both of these have been done for the good and benefit of the Church, and that the whole world is full of these Holy Books and that they will be preserved until the end of the world. As for the first, concerning the living voice alone, we showed that it was more useful and more pleasing to that primitive Church which came before Moses, because God dealt with those Fathers in this way, namely by the appearances and conversations of his Son, by the breathings of the Holy Spirit, and by the visions of angels, joined with the living and effective ministry of holy men. This was better than if, lacking those heavenly ways of acting and teaching, they had received only the written Word. For it was far more useful to hear the Son of God present than merely to read his letters.

units.la: Insequenti etiam Ecclesiæ, eandem ratio-nem, cum prioribus Patribus seruatam, vti-lissimam fuisse: propterea quòd per eam di-dicerunt, quanto amore Deus suam prosequatur Ecclesiam: & quàm magnæ ea sibi sit curæ & cordi: quippe qui, vt eam erudiret de sua voluntate, subinde miserit Filium suum λόγον illum æternum, qui in specie humani corporis cum illis familiariter loqueretur: sæpe Angelos etiam cœlestes: semper autem spiritum in cordibus loquentem & persuadentem: Indè factū esse, vt persuasi de amore Dei erga humanum genus, cum postea dedit Scripturam sacram, maiori reuerentia, certiorique fide, eam amplexi sint: Ac proindè primam illam rationem ἄγραφον, per totum illud primum tempus cum Patribus, fuisse posteris ceu quandam παράδοσιν, ad scripturam porrò auidius & reuerentius accl-piendam, legendam, credendam: Et hucspe-stare illud Dei ad Mosen: Nunc ego veniam ad te in densa nube, vt populus audiat me loquen-tem ad te, & credant tibi in perpetuum. Eandem igitur etiam ob causam, Deum appa-ruisse Patribus, & viua voce sine scripto cum illis locutum esse: vt hoc cognito, posteri deinde plus fidei adhiberent Scripturis Dei, in quas eadem retulit, quæ etiam Patribus viua voce antea tradiderat. Quod verò dixi-mus de Ecclesia ante Mosen, & de illa, quæ Mosen insecuta est: idem de Ecclesia, quæ sub Christo, sine vllo eius aut Apostolorum scripto vixit: & de illa, quæ post Christum, Apostolorum scripta accepit, intelligendum esse ostendimus.
units.tr: Likewise, the same method was most useful to the Church that followed, which was kept with the earlier Fathers, because through it they learned how greatly God loves his Church and how great a concern it is to him and dear to his heart. For in order to instruct her about his will, he sent from time to time his Son, that eternal Word (λόγος), who spoke with them familiarly in the form of a human body; often also the heavenly angels; but always the Spirit speaking and persuading in their hearts. Hence it came about that, persuaded of God's love toward the human race, when afterwards he gave the holy Scripture, they embraced it with greater reverence and firmer faith. Accordingly, that first method, unwritten (ἄγραφον), which through the whole of that first time was kept with the Fathers, was for posterity a kind of tradition (παράδοσις), so that they would receive, read and believe Scripture more eagerly and reverently. To this looks that word of God to Moses: Now I will come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear me speaking with you, and may believe you forever. For this same reason, therefore, God appeared to the Fathers and spoke with them by the living voice without writing, so that, this being known, posterity would afterwards place more faith in the Scriptures of God, into which he has committed those same things which he had earlier delivered to the Fathers by the living voice. What we have said about the Church before Moses, and about the one that followed Moses, we have shown should be understood in the same way of the Church which lived under Christ without any writing of his or of the Apostles, and of the one which, after Christ, received the writings of the Apostles.

units.la: Quantum verò ad secundum attinet, de scriptionibus: quòd non contentus viua voce, voluerit etiam vti scriptionibus & libris: illud etiam factum fuisse propter maximam Ecclesiæ vtilitatem. Primùm vt semper haberet in promtu certum canonem, ad quem omnes de religione doctrinæ examinaren-tur: & quæ bonæ, quæ malæ, quæ diuinæ, quæ humanæ essent, facilè discernerentur. Hic autem canon, est Scriptura sacra, de quo canone Christus Iohan.7. Si quis voluerit facere voluntatem Patris mei (quæ erat, vt quisque legeret Scripturas, & ad illas omnem aliam examinaret doctrinam) cognoscet de doctrina, vtrum ex Deo sit, an ego à meipso loquar. Et 1.Iohan.4. Nolite omni spiritui credere, sed probate Spiritus (ad Scripturam scilicet) v-trum ex Deo sint.
units.tr: As for the second, concerning writings: that God, not content with the living voice, was willing also to use writings and books, this too was done for the very great benefit of the Church. First, so that he might always have at hand a certain canon, by which all doctrines of religion would be examined, and so that what is good and what is bad, what is divine and what is human, might be easily distinguished. This canon is the holy Scripture, concerning which Christ says in John 7: If anyone wishes to do the will of my Father (which is, that each one should read the Scriptures and test every other doctrine by them), he will know concerning the doctrine whether it is from God or whether I speak of myself. And in 1 John 4: Do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits (namely by Scripture) whether they are from God.

units.la: Secundo, vt in aduentu Christi, certum extaret testimonium, quo Ecclesia agnosceret, An ille Iesus, qui dicebat, se esse Messiam, hoc est, Christum, et sic etne verus ille Christus, de quo scripta extabant Prophetarum, nec ne:Quomodo? Ex collatione Scripturarum, quae de Messia erant, cum illis, quae in Iesu impleri videbant. Certe nisi extitissent oracula Prophetarum de Christo conscripta, non tam facile potuisset agnosci ille Iesus, an esset verus Christus, nec ne. Et huc spectare, quod Iesus, dum vult ostendere, se esse Messiam, subinde citat testimonia Scripturarum, & ad easdem inuestigandas, omnes ablegat & adhortatur. Iohan.5. Scrutamini Scripturas, quia illae de me testimonium perhibent. Idem facere Euangelistas: idem Apostolos, vt ostenderent, in Iesu impleri omnia, quae de Messia fuerant praedicta. Et huc illud Apostoli 2 Corinth.1. Quotquot promissiones Dei sunt, in ipso (Christo) sunt Etiam & Amen, id est, habent complementum.
units.tr: Second, so that at the coming of Christ there might stand a certain testimony by which the Church could recognise whether that Jesus, who said that he was the Messiah, that is the Christ, was indeed that true Christ of whom the writings of the Prophets stood as witnesses, or not. How? By comparing the Scriptures that were about the Messiah with those things which they saw fulfilled in Jesus. Certainly, unless the oracles of the Prophets concerning Christ had been written down, that Jesus could not so easily have been recognised as the true Christ or not. To this looks the fact that Jesus, when he wishes to show that he is the Messiah, repeatedly cites the testimonies of the Scriptures, and sends all to search them out and urges them to do so. John 5: Search the Scriptures, for they bear witness of me. The Evangelists did the same, and the Apostles likewise, to show that everything that had been foretold about the Messiah was fulfilled in Jesus. To this belongs also the word of the Apostle in 2 Corinthians 1: However many are the promises of God, in him (Christ) they are Yes, and in him Amen, that is, they have their fulfilment.

units.la: Tertio, voluisse verbum suum literis mandari Hebraicis per Mosen & Prophetas, & Graecis per Apostolos, vt inde tanquam ex Archetypo, doctrina coelestis, in alias etiam linguas converti: & ita salus ad omnes Gen-tes in perpetuum propagari posset: Et si qui nollent eam amplecti: iis omnis tollecetur[?] excuexcusatio. Et huc quadrare illud Christi, Iohan.1s.[?] Si non venissem, & locutus eis non fuisset, peccatum non haberent: nunc autem non habent, quod praetexant peccato suo. Christus venit ad omnes Gentes, partim per Apostolos, partim quotidie per suas scripturas, iam in omnes linguas conversas: Neminem igitur amplius posse se merito excusare, cum ubique locorum inveniantur Scripturae, in quibus loquitur Christus.
units.tr: Third, that he willed his Word to be committed to writing in Hebrew through Moses and the Prophets, and in Greek through the Apostles, so that from these as from an archetype the heavenly teaching could be translated also into other languages; and so salvation could be spread to all nations forever. And if some were unwilling to embrace it, every excuse would be taken away from them. To this fits that saying of Christ, John 15: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. Christ came to all nations, partly through the Apostles, partly daily through his Scriptures, now translated into all languages. No one, therefore, can any longer justly excuse himself, since Scriptures in which Christ speaks are found in every place.

units.la: Postremo, idcirco voluisse, ut verbum extaret scriptum, ut esset Ecclesiæ instar turris fortissimæ, in qua & thesaurum doctrinæ cœlestis, & se ipsam, contra omnes hostes con-servare posset. Futurum enim erat, ut Satan, modò per tyrānos conaretur aut pios, in quorum cordibus viget cœlestis doctri-na, è medio tollere, & cum illis ipsam etiam doctrinam extinguere: Voluit igitur Deus, ut saltem extaret in libris, propter posteros: Aut etiam libros curare comburendos, & variis rationibus perdendos: Voluit igitur Deus, ut innumeri & ubiq; essent sparsi libri sacri, ut in aliquibus saltem conservaretur: Modò per hæreticos & Antichristos nitere-tur falsis doctrinis multos seducere, aut et-iam falsis interpretationibus scripturarum, in ministerio corrũpere. Voluit igitur Deus extare Scripturam sacram in se puram & sin-ceram, ut semper haberent pij, quò confuge-rent, & ubi se tutos, tanquam in arce conser-varent. Et huc spectare Apostoli adhorta-tionem tionem ad Timoth.2. Tim.3. Mali homines, & seductores proficient in peius, errantes & in errorem inducentes. Tu autem permane in iis (tan-quam in tuta arce) quæ didicisti.
units.tr: Last, he willed that the Word should stand in writing, so that it might be for the Church like a very strong tower, in which it could preserve both the treasure of heavenly doctrine and itself against all enemies. For it was going to be that Satan would try, now through tyrants or through the pious, in whose hearts the heavenly doctrine flourishes, to remove them from the midst and with them to extinguish the doctrine itself. God therefore willed that it should at least stand in books for the sake of posterity; or even that books should be arranged to be burned and destroyed in various ways. God therefore willed that the holy books should be innumerable and scattered everywhere, so that it might be preserved at least in some. Now through heretics and Antichrists he would strive to lead many astray with false doctrines, or even to corrupt the ministry with false interpretations of the Scriptures. God therefore willed that the holy Scripture should stand in itself pure and sincere, so that the godly should always have a place to flee to, and where, as in a citadel, they might keep themselves safe. To this looks the Apostle's exhortation to Timothy, 2 Timothy 3: Evil men and seducers will advance to the worse, erring and leading others into error. But you remain in those things (as in a safe citadel) which you have learned.

units.la: Maximæ procul dubio, sunt hæ utilitates, quas accipimus à verbo Dei scripto: quibus omninò careremus, si verbum non fuisset scriptis mandatum. Has igitur ob causas ostendimus, Deum curasse, ut quam antea solitus erat sola voce tradere Patribus doctrinam, tandem illa libris comprehensa, nobis relinqueretur.
units.tr: Without doubt these are the greatest benefits which we receive from the written Word of God, and we would altogether lack them if the Word had not been committed to writings. For these reasons, therefore, we have shown that God took care that the doctrine which he was accustomed to deliver to the Fathers by the voice alone should at last be contained in books and be left to us.

units.la: Nunc ex iis quæ diximus, sese offert septi-ma quæstio, quæ est de fine eoque de utilita-te Scripturarum. Est autem hæc quæstio di-uersa à superiore: In ea enim disseruimus de causa, propter quam Deus in reuelanda sua cœlesti doctrina, usus sit illis duabus diuersis rationibus: primùm voce, deindè etiam scri-ptione: ac proindè, quàm utraque fuerit v-tilis, declarauimus. In hac autem quæstione quæritur causa finalis, propter quam Deus hoc suum verbum, tam voce, quàm scripto, reuelare, & in Ecclesia promoueri voluerit ac velit. Etsi verò rationes superius ad alte-ram quæstionem allatæ, ad hanc etiam accommodari possunt: tamen alias quoq; pro-prias habet hæc quæstio rationes & utilita-tes, quæ ad superiorem non pertinebant. Quare non immeritò hanc à superiore di-uersam facimus, quia latius hæc patet, quàm illa. Esto igitur hæc
units.tr: Now, from what we have said, the seventh question presents itself, which concerns the end, and therefore the usefulness, of the Scriptures. This question is different from the previous one. In that one we discussed the reason why God, in revealing his heavenly doctrine, used those two different means: first the voice, and then also writing; and we showed how useful each of them was. In this question, however, we ask about the final cause, for which God has wished, and still wishes, this his Word, both by voice and by writing, to be revealed and advanced in the Church. Although the reasons brought forward above for the other question can also be applied to this one, this question nonetheless has its own reasons and usefulness, which did not belong to the previous one. For this reason it is not without good ground that we treat it as distinct from the previous one, since it extends more widely than that one. Let this, then, be

units.la: PROPOSITIO.
units.tr: PROPOSITION.

units.la: Quòd Deus suum verbum, tam voce, quàm scripto, reuelari, & in Ecclesia conser- uari voluerit ac velit: hoc voluit ac vult, propter salutem multiplicemque vtilitatem omnium tam ex Gentibus, quàm ex Iudæis, Electorum.
units.tr: That God has wished, and still wishes, his Word to be revealed both by voice and by writing, and to be preserved in the Church: he has wished and still wishes this for the salvation and manifold usefulness of all the elect, both from the Gentiles and from the Jews.

units.la: Explicatio & Confirmatio.
units.tr: Explanation and Confirmation.

units.la: Principio, vtilitates, quas suprà attuli, huc etiam pertinent: Deinde aliæ etiam vtilitates explicantur ab Apostolo, in hoc contextu ad Timotheum. Cùm ait, Omnis doctrina θεόπνευστος vtilis est πρὸς διδασκαλίαν, &c. Quàm perfecta sit hæc partitio Apostolica, in nostris prolegomenis demonstratum à nobis fuit.
units.tr: First, the usefulnesses which I mentioned above also pertain here. Then, other usefulnesses are also set out by the Apostle in this context to Timothy, when he says: All Scripture, God-breathed [θεόπνευστος], is useful for teaching [πρὸς διδασκαλίαν], etc. How complete this Apostolic enumeration is has been shown by us in our prolegomena.

units.la: Nunc tantùm singula huius partitionis membra diligentius explicanda nobis sunt.
units.tr: Now only the individual members of this enumeration need to be explained more carefully.

units.la: Cùm ait, vtilem esse Scripturam πρὸς διδα-σκαλίαν, docet Apostolus, in hunc finem traditum nobis fuisse Dei verbum tam voce, quàm scripto: vt nihil nos lateret eorum, quæ ad veram pertinent pietatem, eoque ad vitam æternam. Quare si quid nosse velimus de Deo, Deique voluntate: de Mundi, rerumque omnium origine, progressu, finei de peccati etiam ortu, causis, effectis, consequentibus: de ratione eius abolendi, veramque iustitiam recuperandi: de Mediatore, per quem reconciliari possimus Deo, deque Mediatoris natura, officio, amore erga nos: de instituta ab ipso Ecclesia, Ecclesiæq; Sacramentis, Ministerio, felicitate: denique de iis, quæ post hanc vitam manent fideles in cœlo æterna bona: & quæ impios æterna mala: legamus Scripturam, quod hæc omnia abunde ibi tradantur.
units.tr: When he says that Scripture is useful for teaching [πρὸς διδασκαλίαν], the Apostle teaches that the Word of God was handed down to us, both by voice and by writing, for this end: that nothing of those things which pertain to true godliness, and thereby to eternal life, should be hidden from us. Therefore, if we wish to know anything about God and God's will; about the origin, progress and end of the world and of all things, and also about the origin, causes, effects and consequences of sin; about the way of abolishing it and of recovering true righteousness; about the Mediator, through whom we can be reconciled to God, and about the Mediator's nature, office and love towards us; about the Church instituted by him, and the Church's sacraments, ministry and happiness; and finally about those things which remain after this life, the eternal good things for the faithful in heaven, and the eternal evils for the impious: let us read Scripture, because all these things are abundantly set forth there.

units.la: Cùm verò ait, Eam etiam utilem esse πρὸς[?] ἔλεγχον[?]: ostendit, in hunc finem traditam esse Scripturam, vt per hanc omnia impia dogmata non tantùm agnoscere, sed etiam refutare possimus. Nullum enim inueniri posse impium de religione dogma, quod hac Scripturæ veritate & luce agnosci & convinci non possit. Quare si velimus aliena refutare, non opus esse, vt ad alios, sed ad solam Scripturam recurramus.
units.tr: But when he says, it is also useful for refutation [πρὸς ἔλεγχον], he shows that Scripture was handed down for this end: that through it we may not only recognise, but also refute, all impious doctrines. For no impious doctrine concerning religion can be found which cannot be recognised and convicted by this truth and light of Scripture. Therefore, if we wish to refute the views of others, we need not have recourse to others, but only to Scripture alone.

units.la: Cùm etiam ait, Eam utilem esse πρὸς ἐπανόρ-θωσιν[?]: docet, in hunc etiam finem esse tradi-tam, vt quicquid corruptum est in moribus & vita: illud per Scripturam reformare pos-simus. Nihil enim vitij in moribus & vita hominum esse posse, quod non queat per Scripturam agnosci & corrigi: quia quæcunque vitanda sunt, docet.
units.tr: When he also says, it is useful for correction [πρὸς ἐπανόρθωσιν], he teaches that it was handed down also for this end: that whatever is corrupt in morals and in life, we may be able to reform it through Scripture. For there can be no fault in the morals and life of men which cannot be recognised and corrected through Scripture, since it teaches what is to be avoided.

units.la: Ita cùm ait, utilem esse πρὸς παιδείαν[?], satis luculenter docet, in hunc quoque finem esse traditam & reuelatam, vt omnes, etiam pueros ipsos, in bonis moribus, disciplina, iustitia instituere valeamus. Nihil enim verè bonorum morum, veræque iustitiæ, nihil bonorum operum, nihil puerilis etiam insti-tutionis tutionis desiderari posse, quod non in S.lite-ris abunde tradatur.
units.tr: Thus, when he says that it is useful for instruction [πρὸς παιδείαν], he teaches quite clearly that it was also handed down and revealed for this end: that we may be able to train all, even children themselves, in good morals, discipline and righteousness. For nothing truly good in morals, nothing of true righteousness, nothing of good works, and nothing even of childhood education can be wanted which is not abundantly set forth in the Holy Scriptures.

units.la: Cùm verò subdit, ἵνα ἄρτιος[?] ἦ ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄνθρωπος[?], ὡς πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐξηρτισμένος[?], aperte docet, Scripturam in hunc finem inspirata, esse ad supradicta omnia vtilem, vt omni ex parte integer & perfectus esse homo possit, tam in iis, quae ad Deum, quàm in iis, quae ad proxi-mum, & ad nos ipsos spectant: ita vt nullum boni operis genus excogitari possit, ad quod per Scripturam (sed operante Spiritu S.) apparari non possit, quicunque velit homo esse Dei. En igitur fines & vtilitates, propter quas inspirata fuit Scriptura à Deo sanctis Patri-bus, & nobis in Ecclesia relicta.
units.tr: But when he adds, that the man of God may be complete [ἵνα ἄρτιος ἦ ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄνθρωπος], equipped for every good work [ὡς πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐξηρτισμένος], he plainly teaches that Scripture, inspired for this end, is useful for all the things mentioned above, so that a man may be whole and perfect in every respect, both in those things which concern God, and in those which concern his neighbour and ourselves: so that no kind of good work can be thought of for which a man who wishes to be a man of God cannot be prepared through Scripture (but with the Holy Spirit working). Here, then, are the ends and usefulnesses for which Scripture was inspired by God and handed down to the holy Fathers, and left to us in the Church.

units.la: Alium etiam finem & vtilitatem tradit A-postolus ad Rom.15.cùm ait:Omnia quaecunq; scripta sunt, ad nostram doctrinam scripta sunt, vt per patientiam & consolationem Scripturarum, spem habeamus.
units.tr: The Apostle also sets out another end and usefulness, in Romans 15, when he says: Whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the Scriptures we might have hope.

units.la: Docet iis verbis, in hunc etiam finem esse nobis traditam Scripturam S. vt si aliqua opus habeamus consolatione, tam in externis crucibus, quàm in internis animi aut con-scientiae cruciatibus, ad Scripturam recurra-mus. In ea enim omne consolationis genus nos reperturos: ita vt & praesentium malorum patientia ac tolerantia, & futurorum bono-rum spe fulciri ac sustentari possimus. Hunc eundem finem & vtilitatem tradit idem A-postolus 1.Thes.4. vbi cùm locutus esset de resurrectione nostra ad felicem aeternamq; vitam, subiunxit παράινεσιν: Itaque consolamini vos invicem in verbis istis.
units.tr: In these words he teaches that the Holy Scripture has also been handed down to us for this end: that if we have need of any consolation, whether in external crosses or in the inward torments of mind or conscience, we should have recourse to Scripture. For in it we shall find every kind of consolation, so that we may be supported and sustained both by patience and tolerance in present evils and by the hope of future goods. The same Apostle sets out this same end and usefulness in 1 Thessalonians 4, where, after speaking of our resurrection to a blessed and eternal life, he added an exhortation: Therefore comfort one another with these words.

units.la: Esse verò inspiratam & scriptam nobis; relictam propter nostram salutem, hoc est, vt assequamur vitam æternam, pulchrè docet Apostolus in hoc eodem contextu, cùm ait: Sciens à quo didiceris, & quòd S. literas nosti, quæ te possunt reddere sapientem ad vitam æternam. Docet igitur, Scripturas ideò nobis esse traditas, vt per eas ita instruamur in iis, quæ ad vitam pertinent æternam, vt eam etiam æternam vitam assequi tandem valea-mus.
units.tr: That Scripture is inspired and written and left to us for our salvation, that is, so that we may attain eternal life, the Apostle teaches beautifully in this same context, when he says: Knowing from whom you learned it, and that from childhood you have known the holy letters, which are able to make you wise unto eternal life. He therefore teaches that the Scriptures have been handed down to us so that we may be so instructed by them in those things which pertain to eternal life that we may at last be able to attain that eternal life also.

units.la: Cæterùm quas hîc vtilitates & fines paucissimis verbis complexus est Paulus, alibi fusiùs partim ipse, partim alij Apostoli, partim etiam Prophetæ, & Christus ipse explicant. Loca aliquot in gratiam studiosorum, vt habeant, vnde amplificent vtilissimos fines, propter quos traditæ nobis sunt Scripturæ, breuiter indicabo.
units.tr: But the usefulnesses and ends which Paul has comprised here in very few words are set out more fully elsewhere, partly by himself, partly by other Apostles, partly also by the Prophets, and by Christ himself. For the benefit of students, so that they may have from them the means of amplifying the most useful ends for which the Scriptures have been handed down to us, I shall briefly point out some passages.

units.la: Psal. 19. Lex Domini integra, &c. Præter alia sunt ibi 4, effecta verbi Dei. 1. quòd con-vertat Animas. 2. Quòd imperitis sapientiam suppeditet. 3. Quòd exhilaret cor. 4. Quòd illuminet oculos. Docet igitur in hos fines Scripturam esse reuelatam, & literis mandatam, vt per eam Animæ nostræ captiuæ Sathanæ conuertantur ad Deum, & seruentur: vt per eam nobis imperitis rerum diuinarum, sapientia cœlestis suppeditetur: vt per eam corda nostra afflicta, tum proptet peccata,tum propter varias cruces,consolatione afflciantur & exhilarentur: Deinque vt per eam oculi nostri in iis, quae ad Deum, & ad aliam vitam pertinent, suapte natura Talpis caeciores, illuminentur ad Deum cognoscendum. Quid iis finibus praestantius, quid vtilius excogitari potest? Ro-man.10. Fides ex auditu: auditus per verbum Dei. Ergo in hunc finem traditum est verbum Dei, vt ex illo audito, fides in nobis, opera Spiritus sancti excitetur. Psal.118. Memor esto verbi tui, seruo tuo, in quo mihi spem dedisti. Ergo scriptura tradita est, vt per hanc spes nobis donetur, & quoties videtur opprefla, sub-leuetur. Psal.118. Ignitum eloquium tuum vehementer, & seruus tuus diligit illud. Item Luc. 24. Nonne cor nostrum erat ardens in via, &c. Ergo datae scripturae, vt ex illarum auditu & interpretatione, corda nostra in amorem Dei & proximi accendantur. 1.Petr.1. Renati non ex semine corruptibili, sed ex semine immortali, per sermonem Dei viuentis, & manentis in aeternum. Ergo datus sermo Dei, vt per illum regeneremur, & fiamus nouae creaturae, id est, filij Dei. Ioh 15. Iam vos mundi estis per sermonem meum, quem locutus sum vobis.
units.tr: Psalm 19, The law of the Lord is perfect, etc. Besides other things, there are there four effects of the Word of God. (1) That it converts souls. (2) That it gives wisdom to the unlearned. (3) That it gladdens the heart. (4) That it enlightens the eyes. It teaches therefore that Scripture has been revealed and committed to writing for these ends: that through it our souls, held captive by Satan, may be converted to God and saved; that through it heavenly wisdom may be given to us, who are unskilled in divine things; that through it our hearts, afflicted both by sin and by various crosses, may be comforted and gladdened; and finally that through it our eyes, which by nature are blinder than moles in those things which pertain to God and to the other life, may be enlightened to know God. What more excellent or more useful end can be thought of than these? Romans 10: Faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the Word of God. Therefore the Word of God has been handed down for this end: that by hearing it, faith may be stirred up in us by the work of the Holy Spirit. Psalm 119: Remember your word to your servant, in which you have given me hope. Therefore Scripture has been handed down so that hope may be given to us through it, and whenever it seems to be oppressed, it may be raised up. Psalm 119: Your word is exceedingly fiery, and your servant loves it. Likewise Luke 24: Was not our heart burning within us on the way, etc.? Therefore the Scriptures were given so that by hearing and interpreting them our hearts may be kindled to the love of God and of our neighbour. 1 Peter 1: Born again not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible seed, through the word of the living God, which abides for ever. Therefore the word of God was given so that through it we may be regenerated and become new creatures, that is, children of God. John 15: Now you are clean through the word which I have spoken to you.

units.la: Ergo datur, vt per eum mundemur ab omni peccati labe, & mundi simus in conspectu Dei viuentis. Iohan.8. Si manseritis in sermone meo, veritas liberabit vos. Ergo datur sermo Dei, vt è seruis peccati & Sathanae, fiamus vere liberi. Iohan.15. Haec locutus sum voeis[?], ut gaudium meum in vobis sit. ¶Item. 1.Iohan. 1. Haec scripsi vobis, ut communionem habeatis nobiscum, & gaudium vestrum sit plenum. Ergo datae scripturae, ut vero gaudio & laetitia impleamur. Ief.1.[?] Si volueritis, & audieritis, bona terra comedetis: Quod si verbum meum nolueritis audire, gladius devorabit vos. Ergo datum verbum Dei, ut per eius observationem, à malis etiam praesentibus libe-remur, & benedictionibus etiam terrenis fruamur. Denique Iohan.15. Si manseritis in me, & verba mea in vobis manserint, quicquid volueritis, petetis, & fiet vobis. Ergo datae scrip-turae, & verba Christi, ut per ea in nobis retenta, impetremus à Deo, quicquid iuxta hoc verbum petimus.
units.tr: Therefore it is given that through it we may be cleansed from every stain of sin, and be clean in the sight of the living God. John 8. If you abide in my word, the truth will set you free. Therefore the word of God is given, so that from the slaves of sin and of Satan we may become truly free. John 15. I have spoken these things so that my joy may be in you. Likewise: 1 John 1. I write these things to you so that you may have fellowship with us, and that your joy may be full. Therefore the Scriptures are given so that we may be filled with true joy and gladness. Isaiah 1. If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land; but if you refuse to hear my word, the sword shall devour you. Therefore the word of God is given so that, by observing it, we may be freed even from present evils and may also enjoy earthly blessings. Finally, John 15. If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, you shall ask whatever you will, and it shall be done for you. Therefore the Scriptures and the words of Christ are given so that, when they are kept within us, we may obtain from God whatever we ask in accordance with this word.

units.la: His, quae ex sacris Literis hactenus adduxi-mus, satis perspicuum factum est, multas & maximas esse utilitates, propter quas doctrina coelestis, fuit S. Prophetis & Apostolis inspirata, & deinde etiam monumentis librisq; mandata.
units.tr: From what we have hitherto adduced from the sacred Writings, it has become sufficiently clear that there are many and very great benefits on account of which the heavenly teaching was inspired to the holy Prophets and Apostles, and then also committed to records and books.

units.la: Ex iisdem autem locis, colliguntur tria: Primum: Scripturam sacram in summa no bis esse traditam, propter salutem nostram, hoc est, ut ea sit nobis instrumentum, & potentia Dei ad salutem: id quod iis etiam insequentibus locis confirmatur. Rom.1. Evangelium virtus Dei est in salutem omni credenti. Evangelium igitur, & tota scriptura, revelata est propter salutem nostram. 1.Cor.1. Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis, salvos facere credentes. credentes. Stultitia autem prædicationis, est Euangelica doctrina. Doctrina igitur Euangelij, eoque scripturæ sacræ, propter salutem nostram, & omnium credentium reuelata est. 1. Timoth. 4. Dum venio, attende (inquit) lectioni, exhortationi, doctrinæ. Cui lectioni? cui doctrinæ? Proculdubio, sacrarum literarum. Postea subdit: Noli negligere donum, quod in te est, propter Prophetias, hoc est, ad interpretandum scripturas, & ad docendum. Postea concludit. Hoc enim si feceris: & teipsum seruabis, & eos, qui te audierint. Scriptura ergo sancta, doctrinaq; cœlestis, reuelata est propter nostram salutem.
units.tr: From the same passages, three things are gathered. (1) First, that the sacred Scripture has been handed down to us in sum for our salvation, that is, so that it may be to us an instrument and the power of God unto salvation; which is also confirmed in the passages that follow. Romans 1. The gospel is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes. The gospel, therefore, and the whole Scripture, has been revealed for our salvation. 1 Corinthians 1. It pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe. Now the foolishness of preaching is the evangelical doctrine. The doctrine of the gospel, and so of the sacred Scripture, has therefore been revealed for our salvation and for that of all believers. 1 Timothy 4. Until I come, he says, attend to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine. To what reading? To what doctrine? Without doubt, to the sacred letters. Afterwards he adds: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given through prophecies, that is, for interpreting the Scriptures and for teaching. Then he concludes: For if you do this, you will save both yourself and those who hear you. Therefore the holy Scripture and the heavenly doctrine has been revealed for our salvation.

units.la: Secundum: Scripturam S. non esse reuelatam propter salutem Iudæorum tantum: sed etiam Gentium omnium, quæ hanc velint fide amplecti. Hæc enim, quæ modò citauimus, scripsit ad Gentes, Romanos, Corinthios, Ephesinos: Et Christus aperte dixit. Matth.28 Prædicate Euangelium omni creaturæ: Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur. Luc.11. Beati, qui audiunt verbum Dei, & custodiunt illud. Ergo scriptura tota, reuelata est propter salutem omnium, qui eam velint fide amplecti, & custodire.
units.tr: (2) Secondly, that the holy Scripture has been revealed not for the salvation of the Jews alone, but of all the Gentiles too, who wish to embrace it in faith. For the passages just cited were written to the Gentiles, the Romans, the Corinthians, and the Ephesians; and Christ openly said: Matthew 28. Preach the gospel to every creature; whoever believes and is baptized will be saved. Luke 11. Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it. Therefore the whole Scripture has been revealed for the salvation of all who wish to embrace it in faith and keep it.

units.la: Tertium: Hoc etiam ex prædictis colligitur: totam scripturam ad nos pertinere: idq; contra quosdam fanaticos, qui sentiunt, vetus Testamentum nihil ad nos pertinere Christianos. Contra certè sunt omnes prædicti loci scripturarum, qui cumprimis loquuntur quuntur de scripturis Prophe:icis[?]. Si tota scriptura revelata est & scriptis comprehen-sa propter salutem nostram, hoc est, tam Gen-tium, quàm Judaeorum. Ergo tota, tam vetus, quàm Nouum Testamentum, ad nos per-i-net: & in gratiam nostram traditum est u-trumque Testamentum. Huc illa Apostoli testimonia Rom.4. Non est autem scriptum propter Abrahamum tantum, sed etiam propter nos. Item Rom.15. Omnia, quae scripta sunt, ad nostram doctrinam scripta sunt. De scripturis veteris Testamenti loquebatur. 1 Pet.1. Qui-bus etiam revelatum est, quòd non sibi, sed nobis administrarent, quae nunc annunciata sunt vobis.
units.tr: (3) Thirdly, this too is gathered from what has been said: that the whole Scripture pertains to us. This is against certain fanatics who think that the Old Testament pertains nothing to us Christians. Certainly all the aforesaid passages of Scripture are against them, which speak above all of the prophetic Scriptures. If the whole Scripture has been revealed and comprised in writings for our salvation, that is, for the salvation of Gentiles as much as of Jews, then the whole of it, the Old Testament as much as the New, pertains to us, and both Testaments have been handed down for our benefit. To this belong those testimonies of the Apostle: Romans 4. Now it was not written for Abraham's sake alone, but for ours also. Likewise Romans 15. Whatever things were written, were written for our instruction. He was speaking of the Scriptures of the Old Testament. 1 Peter 1. To whom it was also revealed that they were ministering not to themselves but to you, the things which have now been announced to you.

units.la: At (inquiunt) nihil ad nos pertinent illa Ce-remonia Judaica, Circumcisio, illa sacrificia. Respon. Verum: quatenus scilicet non tenemur illa seruare. Christus enim illa nobis abrogauit: quoniam omnia ceremonialia fuerunt ad tempus tantum Judaeis imposita. Usq; ad quod tempus? Hebr.9. ait, usque ad tempus correctionis. Quodnam hoc? Tempus adven-tus Christi in carnem. Ideo ipse omnia cor-rexit.
units.tr: But, they say, those Jewish ceremonies, circumcision and those sacrifices, pertain nothing to us. I reply: true, namely insofar as we are not bound to keep them. For Christ abrogated them for us, since all the ceremonial things were imposed on the Jews only for a time. Until what time? Hebrews 9. says, until the time of correction. What time is this? The time of Christ's coming in the flesh. Therefore he corrected all things.

units.la: Sed tria hic notanda sunt. Primum, Quaedam ibi fuerunt instituta in perpetuum, non ad tempus, ut fides in futurum Messiam, & alia quae ad fidem pertinent. Item praecepta ad vitam pertinentia, ut moralia. Haec certè, cũ aeterna sint, ad nos etiam pertinent, & pro-pter nostrā salutem sunt instituta & scripta.
units.tr: But three things are to be noted here. First, some things there were instituted in perpetuity, not for a time, such as faith in the future Messiah, and others which pertain to faith. Likewise precepts pertaining to life, such as the moral ones. These, since they are eternal, certainly pertain to us too, and were instituted and written for our salvation.

units.la: Secundum: sub ceremoniis carnalibus, & quæ usq; ad tempus correctionis erant institutæ, latebant spiritualia & æterna, tanquam nucleus sub cortice: verbi gratia, Circumci-sio cordis, sub circumcisione præputij: Sacrificium Christi æternum*, sub sacrificiis boum:purificatio conscientiæ, sub purifica-tionibus aquarum. Hic certè nucleus ad nos pertinet, & facit ad salutem nostram, corticem jam per Christum reiecto.
units.tr: Secondly, under the carnal ceremonies, which were instituted until the time of correction, lay hidden spiritual and eternal things, like the kernel under the husk: for example, circumcision of the heart under the circumcision of the foreskin; the eternal sacrifice of Christ under the sacrifices of oxen; purification of the conscience under the purifications with water. This kernel certainly pertains to us and serves our salvation, the husk having now been cast aside through Christ.

units.la: Tertium: Scripturæ etiam, quæ de illis sunt ceremoniis, ad nos pertinent, & relictæ sunt propter nostram salutem, ut scilicet videa-mus, sub quibus involucris exhibitus fuerit Christus Patribus, & inde confirmemur in fide, nucleumq; qui ad salutem est, inde erutum comedamus. Stat igitur propositio, totam scripturam inspiratam, & literis mandatam, propter nostram salutem.
units.tr: Thirdly, the Scriptures also which concern those ceremonies pertain to us, and have been left for our salvation, so that we may see under what coverings Christ was displayed to the Fathers, and be confirmed thereby in faith, and eat the kernel which is for salvation, drawn out from them. Thus the proposition stands: the whole Scripture, inspired and committed to writing, is for our salvation.

units.la: QUÆSTIO VIII. De perfectione Scripturarum.
units.tr: QUESTION VIII. On the perfection of the Scriptures.

units.la: Ex iis quæ diximus de fine, propter quem inspiratæ fuerunt scripturæ, hoc est, propter nostram salutem : liquidò apparet, quid re-spondendum sit ad quæstionem octauam, quæ est de perfectione scripturarum. Hac enim quæritur, An omnia quæ ad salutem nostram necessaria sunt, in sacris literis abundè & perspicuè continentur,nec ne.
units.tr: From what we have said about the end for which the Scriptures were inspired, that is, for our salvation, it is clear what must be answered to the eighth question, which concerns the perfection of the Scriptures. For this question asks: Whether or not all things that are necessary to our salvation are contained abundantly and perspicuously in the sacred letters.

units.la: Papistæ negant, idq; faciunt, quò possint suas putidas obtrudere traditiones, tanquam ad salutem necessarias, ac proinde suum augere quaestum. Nam pleraque omnes Papisticae traditiones, ad quaestum pertinent, & quaestus gratia excogitatae sunt. Ac si qui inter illos sint, qui efficacissimis rationibus, scripturarum testimoniis, & Patrum auctoritatibus convicti, concedant omnia ad salutem necessaria in scripturis contineri, addunt glossema, hoc esse intelligendum vel explicite, vel implicite. Hoc vero addunt, quo [?] suas ineptas & ἀσυλλόγιστους [?] sequelas quas faciunt e certis locis scripturarum, & quibus suas confirment idolomanias, aliquo possint modo tueri. Illorum rationibus respondebimus ad extremum. In praesentia iuxta nostram methodum respondebimus ad quaestionem: deinde confirmabimus. Respondemus igitur hac propositione.
units.tr: The Papists deny it, and they do so in order to be able to foist their foul traditions upon us as necessary to salvation, and thereby increase their profit. For almost all Papist traditions pertain to gain and were devised for the sake of gain. And if there are some among them who, convinced by the most effective arguments, by testimonies of Scripture and by the authority of the Fathers, concede that all things necessary to salvation are contained in the Scriptures, they add a gloss: that this must be understood either explicitly or implicitly. They add this so that they may in some way defend their absurd and illogical [?] inferences, which they draw from certain passages of Scripture, and by which they try to confirm their idolatries. We shall answer their arguments at the end. For the present, according to our method, we shall answer the question, and then confirm it. We therefore answer with this proposition.

units.la: PROPOSITIO I.
units.tr: PROPOSITION I.

units.la: Scriptura sancta continet omnia, quae ad salutem nostram necessaria sunt, idque perspicue: ac proinde nil citra apertum illius testimonium, admittendum est in religione, tanquam necessarium vel ad credendum, vel ad faciendum.
units.tr: Holy Scripture contains all things that are necessary to our salvation, and it does so perspicuously; and therefore nothing beyond its clear testimony is to be admitted in religion as necessary either to believe or to do.

units.la: Explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Primum, Cum dico, Necessarium ad salutem necessariarum genus: unum eorum, quae necessaria sunt per se, & semper: ut fidere Deo: credere quæcunque tradit Deus: timere & amare Deum: inuocare in omnibus necessitatibus Deum: deniq; eius causa paratum esse omnia perferre. Item, quoad proximum, amare proximum, & eum in omnibus, quibus possumus, iuuare. Item, quoad nos, sancte & caste viuere, noftraq; vasa custodire in sanctificatione: & bonam semper circumferre conscientiam. Hæc sunt per se & semper necessaria ad salutem, non tanquam causæ salutis: sed primo tanquam ita à Deo nobis mandata, vt nunquam vel minima in parte, aut vlla de causa liceat ea omittere, quin in indignationem Dei incurramus, & mortem nobis asciscamus: secundo tanquam effecta fidei iustificantis, & sine qua seruari nemo potest, ita coniuncta, vt separari ab illa non possint: Atque in iis internus cultus, veraq; s̈υσ consistit. Ac de iis Christus Matth. 23. Væ vobis Scribis & Pharisæis, qui decimatis mentam, &c. & reliquistis, quæ graviora sunt legis, misericordiam, iudicium, fidem. Testimonio Christi alia sunt in Lege graviora, alia minus gravia, hoc est, alia necessaria per se & semper: alia non item. Ideo subdit de illis gravioribus: Hæc oportuit facere: quasi dicat, hæc erant necessaria per se & semper, illa non ita.
units.tr: First, when I say, "necessary to salvation," I speak of a kind of necessary things: one class of those things which are necessary in themselves and always, such as: to trust in God; to believe whatever God delivers; to fear and love God; to call upon God in all necessities; and finally, for his sake, to be prepared to endure all things. Likewise, with regard to our neighbour: to love our neighbour and to help him in all the ways we can. Likewise, with regard to ourselves: to live holily and chastely, to keep our vessels in sanctification, and always to carry about a good conscience. These things are necessary to salvation in themselves and always, not as causes of salvation, but first, as commanded by God to us in such a way that it is never permitted to omit them in the least part, or for any cause, without incurring the wrath of God and bringing death upon ourselves; second, as effects of justifying faith, and so joined to it that they cannot be separated from it, and without which no one can be saved. In these the inward worship and true piety [?] consists. Concerning these Christ says, Matt. 23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, who tithe mint, etc., and have left aside the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. By the testimony of Christ, some things in the Law are weightier, others less weighty; that is, some are necessary in themselves and always, others are not so. Therefore he adds concerning those weightier things: These ought you to have done, as if he were saying: these were necessary in themselves and always, but those were not so.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Aliud genus rerum necessariarum ad salutem, est eorum, quæ non per se, nec semper, sed propter aliud, & ad certum tempus obseruanda sunt. In hoc genere sunt Sacramenta, menta,& ceremoniae omnes,ieiunia,& quæcunque ad externum & corporalem cultum pertinent. Hæc enim institituta sunt propter aliud, non propter se: ideò etiam necessaria sunt nō per se, sed propter aliud. Exemplum.
units.tr: Another kind of things necessary to salvation is that of those which are to be observed not in themselves nor always, but on account of something else and for a certain time. In this kind are the sacraments, and all ceremonies, fasts, and whatever pertains to external and bodily worship. For these were instituted on account of something else, not for themselves; therefore they too are necessary not in themselves but on account of something else. Example.

units.la: Vt Baptismus institutus est, propter fœderis confirmationem, hoc est, vt hoc ceu sigillo, & promissiones Dei erga nos, & nostra fides ac obedientia erga Deum, quæ sunt duæ fœderis partes, obsignentur & confirmentur.
units.tr: Just as Baptism was instituted for the confirmation of the covenant, that is, so that by it, as by a seal, God's promises toward us and our faith and obedience toward God, which are the two parts of the covenant, may be sealed and confirmed.

units.la: Et quod de Baptismo dico, idem de Cœna dictum volo. Idcirco etiam non semper est necess:, vt ea sumamus: sed Baptismum semel, Cœnam certis temporibus: & vtrumq; cùm adest facultas temporis, rerum, personarum. Nam etiamsi quis ex hac vita migraret sine Baptismi susceptione: idq; non aliam ob causam, nisi propterea quòd non potuit vel propter temporis breuitatem, vel propter aquæ aut ministri defectum, illum percipere: non idcirco tamen mortem incurrisse æternam, illum diceremus: modò non defuerint, quæ prioris sunt generis, fides, pœnitentia, bona conscientia. Talia quoq; erant Sacramenta & ceremoniæ veteris legis. Tenebantur Iudæi circumcidi, non propter se, sed propter fœderis, in quod recipiebantur, confirmationem & obsignationem: & non semper, sed semel, idque octauo die, non ante. Tenebantur offerre sacrificia, celebrare pascha, sed certis temporibus, & in certo loco. Hinc igitur apparet, quomodo hæc sint necessaria ad salutem, non per se, nec semper, ut superiora, quemadmodum declaratum est. Atque hæc secundi generis exercitia & opera, sunt pars altera divini cultus, nempe exterior. Ita habemus totum Dei cultum, interiorem, quem Apostolus 1. Tim.4. εὐσέβειαν [?] & exteriorem, quem vocat ibidem corporalem exercitationem.
units.tr: And what I say of Baptism, I wish to be said of the Supper as well. Therefore it is not always necessary for us to partake of it either; rather Baptism once, the Supper at certain times, and each when there is opportunity of time, things, and persons. For even if someone should depart this life without receiving Baptism, and for no other cause than that he could not receive it, either because of the shortness of time or because of a lack of water or of a minister, we would not on that account say that he had incurred eternal death, provided that the things of the first kind, faith, repentance, and a good conscience, were not lacking. Such also were the sacraments and ceremonies of the old law. The Jews were bound to be circumcised, not for themselves, but for the confirmation and sealing of the covenant into which they were received; and not always, but once, and that on the eighth day, not before. They were bound to offer sacrifices and to celebrate the Passover, but at certain times and in a certain place. From this, therefore, it is apparent how these are necessary to salvation, not in themselves nor always, unlike the former things, as has been declared. And these exercises and works of the second kind are the other part of divine worship, namely the external. Thus we have the whole worship of God, inward, which the Apostle calls piety [εὐσέβεια] in 1 Tim. 4, and outward, which he calls in the same place bodily exercise.

units.la: Cùm igitur dico in propositione, scriptu-ram omnia continere & tradere, quæ ad salutem sunt necessaria: intelligo non tantum de interno cultu, sed etiam de externo: quorum ille necessarius est per se & semper: iste verò propter aliud, & non semper, ut explicatum à nobis est. Nunc tenemus explicationem illius vocis, Necessaria ad salutem.
units.tr: Therefore, when I say in the proposition that Scripture contains and delivers all things that are necessary to salvation, I understand this not only of the inward worship but also of the outward; of which the former is necessary in itself and always, but the latter on account of something else and not always, as has been explained by us. Now we have the explanation of that expression, "necessary to salvation."

units.la: Secundo: Cùm dico perspicuè: intelligo vel in se, vel per se: vel in suis principiis & per aliud. In se & per se, ut cùm disertis & expressis verbis res explicatur, verbi gratia, ut credentes in Christum esse baptizandos: hoc enim disertis verbis præcepit Christus Matth.28. Et Actor.2. Qui receperunt sermonem, baptizati sunt. Et Actor.8. ait Philippus Eunucho, Si credis ex toto corde, licet, nempe baptizari. In suis autem principiis, & per aliud, ut baptizandos etiam esse infantes fidelium liberos. Etsi enim non extet expressum præceptum hac de re: colligitur tamen perspicuè ex suis principiis, hoc est, ex causis, propter quas conferendus sit alicui baptismus, ut scilicet obsignetur hoc sigillo ipsi Christo, quicunq; in fœdus nouum, cum Christo receptus est. Est enim hoc manifestum principium in scripturis: Quicunq; re- cepti sunt in fœdus Dei, eos etiam obsignandos esse eo signo, quo Deus iussit obsignari: vt in veteri Testamento, circumcisione: in Nouo, Baptismate. Est etiam hoc aliud principium perspicuum: fidelium infantes pertinere ad fœdus Dei, & in fœdus esse receptos: Genef.17. Ero Deus tuus, & seminis tui post te. Et Christus ait de infantibus, Horum esse regnum cœlorum, Matth. 19. Marc.10. Et 1. Corinth.7. Filios fidelium sanctos esse, nempe Deo. Perspicua igitur est doctrina, Baptizandos esse fidelium liberos: Si non in se & per se, saltem per aliud, hoc est, ex illis principiis de fœdere, de signo fœderis, deq; receptis in fœdus. Nunc etiam tenemus explicationem huius dictionis, perspicuè omnia tradi in scripturis, quæ ad salutem pertinent.
units.tr: Second: when I say perspicuously, I understand either in itself and through itself, or in its principles and through something else. In itself and through itself, as when a matter is explained in plain and express words, for example, that those who believe in Christ are to be baptized: for Christ commanded this in express words, Matt. 28; and Acts 2: Those who received the word were baptized. And Acts 8, Philip says to the eunuch: If you believe with your whole heart, it is lawful, namely, to be baptized. But in its principles, and through something else: as that the infants of believers too are to be baptized. For although there is no express precept on this matter, yet it is clearly gathered from its principles, that is, from the causes on account of which baptism is to be conferred on anyone, namely, that he may be sealed by this sign to Christ himself, whoever has been received into the new covenant with Christ. For this is a manifest principle in the Scriptures: Whoever have been received into the covenant of God are also to be sealed with that sign by which God has commanded them to be sealed: as in the Old Testament by circumcision, and in the New by baptism. There is also this other clear principle: the infants of believers belong to the covenant of God and have been received into the covenant: Gen. 17: I will be your God and the God of your seed after you. And Christ says of infants: Of such is the kingdom of heaven, Matt. 19; Mark 10. And 1 Cor. 7: the children of believers are holy, namely to God. The doctrine, therefore, that the children of believers are to be baptized is clear: if not in itself and through itself, at least through something else, that is, from those principles concerning the covenant, the sign of the covenant, and those received into the covenant. Now we also have the explanation of this phrase, that all things that pertain to salvation are delivered perspicuously in the Scriptures.

units.la: Tertio, Cùm verò addo ad finem, tanquam necessarium vel ad credendum, vel ad faciendum: complector omnia quæ ad religionem pertinent. Omnia enim aut ad fidè, aut ad opera & actiones pertinent: ad fidem, dogmata: ad actiones, præcepta legis. Hac igitur particula ostendo, nihil de religione tradi posse, quod non in scripturis continea-tur: ac proinde nemini hominum licere vel fidei dogmata, vel præcepta de sacramenti[?] & aliis actionibus conscientiam obligantia, in Ecclesia constituere. Nunc ad confirma-tionem venjamus,
units.tr: Third, when I add at the end, "as necessary either to believe or to do," I embrace all things that pertain to religion. For all things pertain either to faith or to works and actions: to faith, the doctrines; to actions, the precepts of the law.
