He was writing against Valentinus and his disciples, who did not acknowledge the one God only, the Creator of heaven, proclaimed by the Prophets.

units.la: Tertullianus lib. de præscriptionibus ad-versus Hæreticos, 1. statuit fidei regulam & summam, quæ habetur in symbolo Apostolico: hæc statuit unum Deum, & unum Filium Dei Christum. 2. Qui hanc non admit-tunt, hæretici sunt, & hos ad nullam de scri-pturis disputationem admittendos esse docet. Atque hæc præscriptio prima est contra Hęreticos: quia etiam ij (de quibus agit, Mar-cionitæ) non admittunt omnes scripturas, & quas admittunt, detractionibus & additio-nibus corrumpunt. Item, quia etiam illi dicunt, nos peruertere scripturas, ideo non esse ad scripturas prouocandum, nec in iis constituendum certamen.
units.tr: Tertullian, in his book On Prescription against Heretics, (1) lays down the rule of faith and summary, which is contained in the Apostles' Creed: this establishes one God and one Son of God, Christ. (2) He teaches that those who do not admit this are heretics, and that such persons are not to be admitted to any dispute from Scripture. And this is the first prescription against heretics: because those of whom he is speaking, the Marcionites, do not admit all the Scriptures, and those they do admit they corrupt by removals and additions. Likewise, because they also say that we pervert the Scriptures, therefore one must not appeal to the Scriptures, nor contend about them.

units.la: Secunda : Si Dominus Iesus Christus Apostolos misit ad prædicandum: non alios esse recipiendos prædicatores, quam quos Christus instituit: quia nemo novit Patrem, nisi Filius, & cui voluerit Filius revelare. Quid vero Apostoli prædicauerint, hoc est, quid illis Christus revelauerit, non aliter pro-bari debet (id est, per alios testes) quam per easdem Ecclesias, quas ipsi Apostoli condi-derunt, prædicando eis viva voce, deinde et-iam per Epistolas.
units.tr: Second: If the Lord Jesus Christ sent the Apostles to preach, then no preachers are to be received other than those whom Christ appointed, because no one knows the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal him. But what the Apostles preached, that is, what Christ revealed to them, ought not to be proved otherwise (that is, by other witnesses) than through the same Churches which the Apostles themselves founded, by preaching to them by the living voice, and then also through Epistles.

units.la: Tertia : Si hæc ita sunt, constat igitur omnem doctrinam, quæ cum illis Ecclesiis Apostolicis & originalibus fidei conspirat, veritati deputandam: id sine dubio tenete, quod Ecclesiæ ab Apostolis, Apostoli à Christo, Christus à Deo accepit: reliquam vero doctrinam omnem de mendacio prae-iudicandam, quæ sapit contra veritatem Ecclesiarum & Apostolorum, & Christi & Dei. Et quia hæretici dicebant, 1. Apostolos non omnia scivisse : 2. si sciverunt, non omnia prædicasse : 3. & si prædicarunt, Ecclesias aliter accepisse, quàm Apostoli docuerint: ideo aliam addit præscriptionem.
units.tr: Third: If these things are so, it is clear that every doctrine which agrees with those Apostolic and original Churches of the faith is to be counted as truth: hold without doubt that which the Churches received from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, and Christ from God; but all the remaining doctrine is to be judged false, which savours of opposition to the truth of the Churches and of the Apostles, and of Christ and of God. And because the heretics said, (1) that the Apostles did not know everything; (2) if they knew, that they did not preach everything; (3) and if they preached, that the Churches received it differently from what the Apostles taught: therefore he adds another prescription.

units.la: Quarta: Ecclesiæ ita ab Apostolis accepe-runt, sicut illi prædicarunt. Et quia hæretici addebant, Ecclesias etsi de principio bene acceperunt, tamen postea errasse, & defecisse à veritate, ut Ecclesiæ Galatiæ & Corinthiacæ: ideo obiicit illas, quas Apostolus laudat à constantia in fide, ut Philippenses, Ephesios, &c. Non est verisimile, omnes Ecclesias in unam fidem errasse. Apud omnes una & eadem semper fides. Ergo veritas, non error.
units.tr: Fourth: The Churches received from the Apostles exactly as they preached. And because the heretics added that the Churches, though they had received well at the beginning, afterwards went astray and fell from the truth, as the Churches of Galatia and Corinth did, therefore he objects to them those whom the Apostle praises for constancy in the faith, such as the Philippians, Ephesians, etc. It is not likely that all the Churches erred in one faith. Among all there is one and the same faith always. Therefore truth, not error.

units.la: Quinta : Illud est verum & Dominicum, quod prius fuit traditum: illud extraneum, & falsum, quod posterius immissum.
units.tr: Fifth: That is true and of the Lord which was first handed down; that is foreign and false which was introduced later.

units.la: Talis doctrina Ecclesiæ de uno Deo, id est prima: posterior fuit hæresis, Marcionis & Valentini.
units.tr: Such is the Church's doctrine of one God, which is the first; the later was the heresy of Marcion and Valentinus.

units.la: Sed quia potuissent forte hæretici dicere, se quoque fuisse tempore Apostolorum: ideo remittit ad successiones Episcoporum, & ait, ut ostendant origines suarum Ecclesiarum, evoluant ordinem suorum Episcoporum, ut tandem veniatur ad aliquem, qui Apostolos audiverit, sicut possunt nostræ Ecclesiæ Catholicæ.
units.tr: But because the heretics might perhaps say that they too existed in the time of the Apostles, therefore he refers them to the successions of bishops, and says that, to show the origins of their Churches, they should unroll the order of their bishops, so that at last one comes to someone who heard the Apostles, as our Catholic Churches can do.

units.la: Sed etsi hoc confingant : tamen nihil efficiunt, quia doctrina eorum cum Apostololica comparata: ex diuersitate & contrarie-tate sua pronunciabit, neque Apostoli ali-cuius autoritatis essent, neque Apostolici, pag.107. Et ideo subdit, Ecclesias quæ post Apostolorum tempora suerunt, post hac forma, id est, argumento à doctrina sumto, demonstrare, se esse Ecclesias Apostolicas: Hæreticas autem neque hac forma, scilicet à doctrina, neque altera forma, scilicet à suc-cessione Episcoporum vsque ad ipsos Apo-stolos resoluendo, se esse Apostolicas, pro-bare.
units.tr: But even if they were to invent this, they accomplish nothing, because their doctrine, compared with the Apostolic, will declare by its diversity and contrariety that neither were the Apostles of any authority, nor Apostolic, p. 107. And therefore he adds that the Churches which came after the times of the Apostles prove, by this form, that is, by the argument taken from doctrine, that they are Apostolic Churches; but heretics, neither by this form, namely from doctrine, nor by the other form, namely by resolving the succession of bishops back to the Apostles themselves, prove that they are Apostolic.

units.la: Sed contra addit aliam præscriptionem: illas non esse Apostolicas Ecclesias, quæ illas doctrinas, quas Apostoli deierarunt, ad-huc retinent, sive fuerint tempore Apostolorum, sive post. Vide locum, pag.107.
units.tr: But against this he adds another prescription: those are not Apostolic Churches which still retain those doctrines which the Apostles handed down, whether they existed in the time of the Apostles or after. See the passage, p. 107.

units.la: Summa: ostendit hanc regulam de doctrina, illam esse, qua præcipuè agnoscuntur quæ sint Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ, quæ non. Ideo ait pag.109. Unde autem extranei, & inimici Apostolis hæretici, nisi ex diuersitate doctrinæ, quam unusquisq; de suo arbitrio, aduersus Apostolos, aut protulit, aut recepit ?
units.tr: Summary: He shows that this rule concerning doctrine is the one by which, above all, it is recognised which Churches are Apostolic and which are not. Therefore he says at p. 109: But whence come strangers and enemies of the Apostles, the heretics, unless from the diversity of doctrine, which each one, by his own judgment, against the Apostles, either put forward or received?

units.la: Responsio ad argumenta tertiæ Classis.
units.tr: Response to the arguments of the third class.

units.la: Si hinc de sententia Patrum concludi-tur[?], non omnia esse in scripturis comprehensa, quæ ad salutem necessaria sunt: sequitur Patres istos secum pugnare. Nam, ut supra citavimus loca, ubique docent, in scripturis ita omnia contineri ad pietatem Christianam pertinentia, ut nihil admittendum sit, quod non habeat testimonium è scripturis. Et qui-dem Tertullianus ipse, lib. de carne Christi, sic reiicit hæreticorum dicta, Non recipio (inquit) quod extra scripturam de tuo in-fers. Concilient igitur illos inter se Papistæ, quia illorum autoritate nituntur. Neque dicendum est, Patres in illo primo axiomate errasse de scripturarum perfectione, quia illud consentaneum est cum scripturis ipsis, atque ita consentaneum, ut si Patres contrarium sentirent, omninò illi essent reiicien-di. Non est autem verisimile, Patres in iis duobus axiomatis secum pugnare. Non potest igitur ex iis, quæ scribunt de traditioni-bus, concludi, Non omnia ad salutem necessaria contineri in sacris Literis, etiam de Patrum sententia. Hoc postea faciam Ego planum, cùm explicabo dicta horum Patrum.
units.tr: If it is concluded from this, on the opinion of the Fathers, that not everything necessary for salvation is comprehended in Scripture, it follows that these Fathers contradict themselves. For, as we have cited above, they teach everywhere that Scripture contains all things pertaining to Christian piety, so that nothing is to be admitted which does not have testimony from Scripture. Indeed Tertullian himself, in his book on the flesh of Christ, thus rejects the sayings of the heretics: "I do not accept," he says, "what you infer from outside Scripture out of your own head." Let the Papists therefore reconcile these Fathers with one another, since they rest on their authority. Nor must it be said that the Fathers erred in that first axiom about the perfection of Scripture, for that is consistent with Scripture itself, and so consistent that, if the Fathers held the contrary, they would have to be entirely rejected. Nor is it likely that the Fathers contradict themselves in those two axioms. Therefore it cannot be concluded from what they write about traditions that not everything necessary for salvation is contained in the Sacred Letters, even on the Fathers' opinion. I will make this plain later, when I explain the sayings of these Fathers.

units.la: 2. Probent Patres isti, omnes has, quas commemorant, esse traditiones Apostolo-rum, & recipiemus.
units.tr: 2. Let these Fathers prove that all the traditions they mention are traditions of the Apostles, and we will accept them.

units.la: 3. Omnes traditiones, quæ vel in Patri-bus leguntur, vel ab aliis obtruduntur, exa-minandæ sunt ad lapidem lydium sacrarum scripturarum: sic etiam Patres docent esse faciendum. Legatur saltem Epistola Augu-stini 19. ad Hieronymum, Ego sentio, &c. & citatur in Decret. dist. 9. Tunc istas traditiones inueniemus aut cum scripturis Canonicis esse consentaneas, aut dissentaneas: aut ne-que consentaneas, neq; dissentaneas. Si fuerint consentaneæ, eas vt Apostolicas, pias & bonas admittemus: sed tunc constabit, eas non esse extra scripturas. Quicquid enim consentaneum est Scripturis sacris, testimo-nia vtique habet in scripturis. Proinde dici non poterit, aliquid ad salutem necessarium, extra scripturas reperiri. Et tales fuerunt o-mnes Apostolorum traditiones. Si fuerint dissentaneæ: nemo dicet, eas esse Apostoli-cas, & necessarias aut viles ad salutem, sed potius contra salutem. Quicquid enim pu-gnat cum sacris Literis, illud etiam repugnat saluti nostræ, eoque Apostolicum esse non potest: & ideo vt venenatum & pernicio-sum reiiciendum est. Et tales multæ sunt in Papatu traditiones. Quare neque de istis di-ci poterit, aliquid ad salutem necessarium, extra scripturam reperiri.
units.tr: 3. All traditions that are either read in the Fathers or thrust upon us by others must be examined by the touchstone of the Sacred Scriptures; the Fathers themselves teach that this must be done. At least let Augustine's nineteenth letter to Jerome be read, "I think, etc.," which is cited in Decretum, distinction 9. Then we shall find those traditions either consistent with the canonical Scriptures or inconsistent with them, or neither consistent nor inconsistent. If they are consistent, we will admit them as apostolic, pious and good; but then it will be clear that they are not outside Scripture. For whatever is consistent with the holy Scriptures certainly has testimony in the Scriptures. Therefore it cannot be said that anything necessary for salvation is found outside the Scriptures. And all the traditions of the Apostles were of this kind. If they are inconsistent, no one will say that they are apostolic and necessary, or even trivial for salvation, but rather contrary to salvation. For whatever fights against the sacred Letters also fights against our salvation, and so cannot be apostolic; and therefore it must be rejected as poisonous and destructive. And many traditions of this kind exist in the Papacy. Wherefore it cannot be said of these either that anything necessary for salvation is found outside Scripture.

units.la: Si fuerint neque consentaneæ, neque dis-sentaneæ: non erunt igitur ad salutem necef-sariæ. Quicquid enim cum scriptura neque dissentit, neque consentit, illud ἀδιάφορον est, & proinde neque necessarium ad salutem, neque contra salutem. Imò si hæc, quæ suapte natura ἀδιάφορα sunt, coniungantur cum superstitione aut obligatione conscien-tiæ, fiunt perniciosa & pugnantia cum sa-cris Literis. Ergo neque de iis poterit dici, aliquid ad salutem necessarium extra scri-pturas reperiri. Quare fiat sententia, Nihil extra scripturam reperiri posse, quod ad sa-lutem nostram necessarium sit vel creditu, vel factu:ac proinde quae tradunt Patres de traditionibus, minime pugnare cum hac nostra propositione: Quacunque ad salu-tem nostram necessaria sunt, ea omnia in scri-pturis Canonicis abunde & perspicue continèri.
units.tr: If they are neither consistent nor inconsistent, then they are not necessary for salvation. For whatever neither disagrees with Scripture nor agrees with it is ἀδιάφορον (indifferent), and therefore neither necessary for salvation nor contrary to it. Indeed, if these things, which are indifferent by their own nature, are joined with superstition or with an obligation of conscience, they become harmful and contrary to the sacred Letters. Therefore it cannot be said of these either that anything necessary for salvation is found outside the Scriptures. Let this then be the judgment: nothing necessary for our salvation, whether to be believed or to be done, can be found outside Scripture; and therefore what the Fathers hand down about traditions does not at all conflict with this proposition of ours: "Whatever things are necessary for our salvation, all of them are contained abundantly and clearly in the canonical Scriptures."

units.la: Atque haec esto brevis responsio ad omnia Patrum dicta & scripta de Traditionibus Apostolicis.
units.tr: And let this be a brief answer to all the sayings and writings of the Fathers about apostolic traditions.

units.la: Caeterum, quo melius intelligantur illa, quae Patres scribunt de traditionibus non scriptis: & quid de illis traditionibus sense-rit vetus Ecclesia, atque ita fructum aliquem ex illorum scriptis capiamus: tria nobis agenda sunt.
units.tr: Moreover, so that those things which the Fathers write about unwritten traditions may be better understood, and what the ancient Church thought about those traditions, and so that we may gain some profit from their writings, three things must be done by us.

units.la: Primum, explicandum nobis est, quot & quae traditionum species apud Patres legantur: & quas ut necessarias ad observandum, & quas non ut necessarias, fidelibus propo-fuerint.
units.tr: First, we must explain what and how many kinds of traditions are read of in the Fathers, and which they proposed to the faithful as necessary to observe, and which not as necessary.

units.la: Deinde tradendae regulae, quibus possimus fieri certiores, quaenam illarum sint verae Apostolicae traditiones, quae minus: sed aut humanae, aut diabolicae.
units.tr: Next, rules must be laid down by which we may be made more certain which of them are true apostolic traditions, and which less so, but are either human or diabolical.

units.la: Postremo, ad quaedam Patrum praecipua dicta, maxime Irenaei & Tertulliani, respon-dendum fuerit: ut quomodo illa sint intelligenda, & qui verus sit illo-rum sensus, appareat.
units.tr: Last, we must respond to certain chief sayings of the Fathers, especially of Irenaeus and Tertullian, so that it may appear how those sayings are to be understood and what their true sense is.

units.la: DE PRIMO.
units.tr: ON THE FIRST.

units.la: Si Patrum loca, vbi de traditionibus loquuntur, diligenter inspiciantur, luculenter videbimus has distinctiones, quarum pri-ma est.
units.tr: If the passages of the Fathers where they speak of traditions are carefully examined, we shall clearly see these distinctions, the first of which is this.

units.la: 1. Traditionum quæ apud Patres leguntur, aliæ sunt de doctrina fidei, aliæ de ritibus & ceremoniis Ecclesiasticis: aliæ de mo-ribus & præceptis vitæ.
units.tr: 1. Of the traditions that are read in the Fathers, some concern the doctrine of faith, others concern the rites and ceremonies of the Church, and others concern morals and precepts of life.

units.la: 2. Harum traditionum aliæ proponuntur vt necessariæ ad credendum & agendum, aliæ non vt necessariæ.
units.tr: 2. Of these traditions, some are put forward as necessary to believe and to do, others not as necessary.

units.la: Nunc explico subiectis exemplis: ac pri-mùm de traditionibus quæ sunt de doctrina.
units.tr: Now I explain with the examples subjoined; and first, concerning the traditions that concern doctrine.

units.la: Inter traditiones de doctrina, quæ vt necessariæ proponuntur à Patribus, sunt etiam hæ:
units.tr: Among the traditions of doctrine which the Fathers put forward as necessary, these also are included:

units.la: Prima, de libris Canonicis & Apocryphis, tam noui quàm veteris Testamenti: Quinam sint Canonici, & qui non Canonici. Sentiunt Patres omnes, hoc nos habere ex sola veterum traditione, Apostolorum scilicet & Apostolicorum virorum: nempe (interpretor) quoad nomina autorum, & quoad principium fidei.
units.tr: First, concerning the canonical and apocryphal books, both of the New and of the Old Testament: which are canonical and which are not canonical. All the Fathers hold that we have this only from the ancient tradition of the Apostles and apostolic men; namely (I interpret) as regards the names of the authors, and as regards the principle of faith.

units.la: Secunda de summa Canonicorum librorum & regula fidei: Summam doctrinæ Christianæ, & regulam fidei nostræ, esse symbolum, quod Apostolorum vocatur. Hoc enim fuisse ab Apostolis compositum, nos non habere è scripturis, sed tantùm ex traditione. Hanc autem summam fideique regulam, vti traditiotraditionem Apostolicam omnibus Eccle-siis communicatam, vtique vrgent Patres, praesertim cum disputant contra haereticos: atque ita hanc traditionem vrgent, vt qui nolunt eam admittere, dicant cum iis non esse veniendum in disputationem, etiamsi velint scripturas vrgere. Vide Tertull. de praescriptionibus.
units.tr: Second, concerning the summary of the canonical books and the rule of faith: the Fathers hold that the summary of Christian doctrine and the rule of our faith is the creed that is called the Apostles'. For that this was composed by the Apostles we do not have from Scripture, but only from tradition. Moreover, this summary and rule of faith, as an apostolic tradition communicated to all the churches, the Fathers certainly press, especially when they dispute against heretics; and they press this tradition so strongly that those who are unwilling to admit it are said not to be worth disputing with, even if they wish to press the Scriptures. See Tertullian, On Prescription.

units.la: Tertia de sensu scriptura S. Scripturam sanctam iuxta eum sensum, quem in communi symbolo confitemur, esse intelligendam & explicandam, vt nihil cum sensu, quem simpliciter habemus in symbolo, pugnet. Hanc etiam esse traditionem Apostolicam.
units.tr: Third, concerning the sense of Holy Scripture. That Holy Scripture is to be understood and explained according to that sense which we confess in the common creed, so that nothing conflicts with the sense which we simply hold in the creed. This too is an apostolic tradition.

units.la: Hæ tres generales traditiones de doctrina sunt observatu necessariæ. Sunt enim consentaneæ sacris Literis. Agnoscimus enim nos, primum, ex ipsis sacris Literis, per Spiritum sanctum nobis apertis & explicatis, eas vere esse θεοπνευστ[?]ως. Secundo, agnoscimus doctrinam, quæ est in symbolo, vere esse Apostolicam, & è Scripturis sacris desumtam, eoque veram esse fidei regulam. Tertio, agnoscimus scripturas esse interpretandas & intelligendas iuxta simplicem sensum, quem habemus in hoc symbolo, quod est regula fidei. Sic enim Roman. 12. docet etiam Apostolus.
units.tr: These three general traditions concerning doctrine must be observed, since they agree with the sacred Letters. For we acknowledge, first, from the sacred Letters themselves, opened and explained to us by the Holy Spirit, that they are truly God-breathed [θεοπνευστῶς]. Second, we acknowledge that the doctrine which is in the creed is truly apostolic and drawn from the holy Scriptures, and therefore a true rule of faith. Third, we acknowledge that the Scriptures are to be interpreted and understood according to the plain sense which we have in this creed, which is the rule of faith. For thus the Apostle also teaches in Romans 12.

units.la: Ex iis tribus generalibus, postea colligunt Patres alias traditiones particulares, de singulis articulis fidei: Vt
units.tr: From these three general traditions, the Fathers afterwards gather other particular traditions concerning the individual articles of faith, as follows.

units.la: Irenæus & Tertullianus contra Hæreticos in libr. de præscriptionibus, & alibi, urget hanc doctrinam tanquam traditionem Apostolicam apud omnes Ecclesias depositam, unum tantùm esse Deum, & hunc esse illum, qui creauit Cœlum & Terram : Et unum Mediatorem Iesum Christum. Hæc doctrina apud omnes Ecclesias retinebatur firmissima. Ideo non immeritò Patres urgebant hanc traditionem, & provocabant ad Ecclesias Apostolicas ipsos hæreticos, Marcionem, Valentinum, & alios: qui cum evincerentur per scripturas, aut illas negabant, aut pervertebant, addendo, diminuendo: vel non omnia in illis contineri, vel non omnia bene esse expressa contendebant, ut docet Tertullianus.
units.tr: Irenaeus and Tertullian, against the heretics, in the book On Prescription and elsewhere, press this doctrine as an apostolic tradition deposited in all the churches: that there is only one God, and that he is the one who created heaven and earth; and one Mediator, Jesus Christ. This doctrine was held most firmly in all the churches. Therefore the Fathers not unjustly pressed this tradition and challenged the heretics themselves, Marcion, Valentinus and others, to the apostolic churches; and when these were refuted by the Scriptures, they either denied them or perverted them, by adding and subtracting, or they contended that not everything is contained in them, or that not everything is well expressed, as Tertullian teaches.

units.la: Sunt præterea aliæ traditiones ad doctri-nam pertinentes, & de interpretatione scri-pturarum apud Patres: sed quæ non proponuntur tanquam necessariæ: Et si ab aliquibus proponuntur ut necessariæ, non sunt tamen admittendæ. Nam neque ab omnibus proponuntur ut Apostolicæ, neq; verè sunt Apostolicæ. Exempla, ut quòd Epiphanius scribit, cùm Lazarus moreretur primùm, fuisse eum 30.annorum.
units.tr: There are besides other traditions pertaining to doctrine and to the interpretation of Scripture among the Fathers, but which are not put forward as necessary; and if some do put them forward as necessary, they are nevertheless not to be admitted. For they are neither proposed by all as apostolic, nor are they truly apostolic. Examples are such as what Epiphanius writes, that when Lazarus first died he was thirty years old.

units.la: E scripturis hoc non habemus: volebat ex traditione esse: sed non ut necessarium. Item, quòd Basilius voluit, Zachariam qui occisus fuit inter templum & altare, fuisse Patrem Iohannis Baptistæ, & similia. Hæc certè non habuerunt ab Apostolis: sed opiniones antiquorum hominum fuerunt.Ideo Patres,si hæc obtrudebant ut traditiones A-postolicas,hallucinabantur.
units.tr: We do not have this from Scripture: he wished it to come from tradition, but not as something necessary. Likewise what Basil wished, that Zechariah who was killed between the temple and the altar was the father of John the Baptist, and similar things. These certainly did not come from the Apostles; they were opinions of ancient men. Therefore the Fathers, if they pressed these things as Apostolic traditions, were mistaken.

units.la: De traditionibus vero, quæ sunt de cere- moniis Ecclesiasticis , illud notandum est: Patres antiquos nunquam alia sacramenta præter Baptismum & Cœnam proposuisse Ecclesiis, nec in scriptis suis reliquisse, tanquam ex traditionibus Apostolorum aut aliorum antiquorum. Et hoc obseruandum est contra Papistas. Quod vero attinet ad alios ritus & Cæremonias Ecclesiasticas, multos tradunt: sed horum alios proponunt ut universales & necessarios ad obseruandum, alios non ita. Exempla priorum.
units.tr: Concerning those traditions which concern ecclesiastical ceremonies, this must be noted: the ancient Fathers never proposed to the Churches any sacraments besides Baptism and the Lord's Supper, nor left them in their writings as if from the traditions of the Apostles or of other ancients. This must be observed against the Papists. As for the other rites and ecclesiastical ceremonies, they hand down many, but of these some they propose as universal and necessary to be observed, and others not so. Examples of the former.

units.la: Vniuersales & necessarij sunt, ut de conuocanda Ecclesia in certum locum.
units.tr: They are universal and necessary, such as concerning the calling of the Church to a certain place.

units.la: 1. Quòd fideles celebrent conuentus Ecclesiasticos, & in iis scripturas legant, sacramenta solenniter administrent, habeant publicas preces,etiam pro impiis Regibus.
units.tr: 1. That the faithful hold ecclesiastical assemblies, and in them read the Scriptures, administer the sacraments solemnly, and offer public prayers, even for impious kings.

units.la: 2. Item ut in Baptismate baptizandus renunciet Mundo & Diabolo, & suâ in Christum profiteatur fidem: Item ut nemo admittatur ad Cœnam, nisi suam profiteatur fidem Et aliæ id genus.
units.tr: 2. Likewise that in Baptism the one to be baptized renounce the World and the Devil, and profess his faith in Christ; likewise that no one be admitted to the Supper unless he professes his faith; and others of that kind.

units.la: Hæ traditiones, quia & universales erant, & consentaneæ sacris literis, idcirco proponebantur ut necessariæ ad obseruandum: & reuera obseruandæ sunt.
units.tr: These traditions, since they were both universal and consonant with the sacred letters, were therefore proposed as necessary to be observed; and indeed they are to be observed.

units.la: Exemplum secundarum, hoc est, illarum, quæ de ritibus Ecclesiasticis erant, sed non vniuersales, & proinde neque necessariæ ad obseruandum, quales multæ apud Tertull. de corona militis: Vt
units.tr: Example of the second kind, that is, of those which concerned ecclesiastical rites but were not universal, and therefore neither necessary to be observed, of which there are many in Tertullian, On the Soldier's Crown, such as:

units.la: 1. Quòd baptizati olim çonsueuerint[?] post acceptum baptismum lac & mel comedere, Quòd Christianus, ad quæcunque agitat, si-gno crucis frontem munire : Quòd diebus Mercurij & Veneris iciunare debeat: Et aliæ id genus permultæ, de quibus copiosè Basi-lius lib.de Spiritu S.cap.27.
units.tr: 1. That the baptized were formerly accustomed, after receiving baptism, to eat milk and honey; that a Christian, whenever he goes out anywhere, should fortify his forehead with the sign of the cross; that he ought to fast on Wednesdays and Fridays; and very many others of that kind, of which Basil speaks at length in his book On the Holy Spirit, chapter 27.

units.la: Cæterùm non omnes, quas ibi recitat, fuerunt vniuersales: deinde non omnes con-sentaneæ sunt verbo Dei. Ideo non erant nec sunt necessariæ ad obseruandum.
units.tr: But not all that he recites there were universal; and further, not all are consonant with the Word of God. Therefore they were not, nor are, necessary to be observed.

units.la: Quod ad traditiones de moribus & legi-bus vitæ atti[?] ęt[?], sunt illæ feré cum lege Dei consentaneæ, exceptis quibusdam de con-uersatione & vita clericorum: quarum aliæ humanæ sunt, & nullo nituntur fundamen-to in verbo Dei: aliæ sunt pugnantes, & ideo impiæ, vt quæ de votis & Cœlibatu. Epi-phanius in refutatione Apostolicorum ait, hanc esse traditionem Apostolicam, Qui vo-uerunt cœlibatum, si postea vxores ducant, illos peccare & χρίμα[?] sibi accersere. Sed pu-gnat cum Pauli doctrina 1. Corinth. 7. Cùm de omnibus ait, Qui non potest se continere nu-bat. Imò etiam ipse Epiphanius in eodem loco ostendit, multò melius esse, vt etiam huiuscemodi homines, qui votum fecerunt cœlibatus, contra votum faciant, vxores du-cendo, quàm perpetuò in tot criminibus vstionibus[?] versari. Quomodo hoc melius, si illud primum damnatur, & contra Deum est? Quo testimonio niititur? Utique illo Apostoli 1. Corinth. 7. Melius est nubere, quàm uri. Ergo etiam in traditionibus de vitæ legi-bus, quædam sunt pugnantes cum verbo Dei. Atq; hæc de primo capite satis.
units.tr: As for the traditions concerning morals and laws of life, these are for the most part consonant with the law of God, except some concerning the conduct and life of the clergy: of these some are human and rest on no foundation in the Word of God, and others are contrary and therefore impious, such as those concerning vows and celibacy. Epiphanius, in his refutation of the Apostolics, says this is an Apostolic tradition: that those who have vowed celibacy, if afterwards they take wives, sin and draw condemnation upon themselves. But this conflicts with the teaching of Paul, 1 Corinthians 7, where he says of all, "Let him who cannot contain marry." Indeed Epiphanius himself, in the same place, shows that it is far better that such men, who have made a vow of celibacy, act against their vow by taking wives, than to live constantly in so many crimes and burnings. How is this better, if the first is condemned and is against God? On what testimony does it rest? Surely on that of the Apostle, 1 Corinthians 7: "It is better to marry than to burn." Therefore also among the traditions about the laws of life, some are contrary to the Word of God. And so much on the first head.

units.la: Veniamus nunc ad secundum caput, quibus-nam regulis agnoscere possimus, qua traditiones sint Apostolica, & qua non Apostolica.
units.tr: Let us now come to the second head: by what rules we can recognise which traditions are Apostolic and which are not Apostolic.

units.la: Augustinus Tom. 7. contra Donatistas, lib. 4. cap. 24. hanc tradit regulam: 'Quod universa tenet Ecclesia, nec Concilijs institutum, sed semper retentum est: non nisi auctoritate Apostolica traditum, restissimè creditur. Idem ferè repetit in epistola ad Ianuarium 118. Hanc regulam ego non reiicio, sed amplector: nempe si aliquid in Ecclesia (id est, tota, & in omnibus) & semper (hoc est, jam inde ab Apostolorum temporibus, sine ulla intermissione) retentum fuit: illud venire de traditione Apostolica. Sed ut hoc probetur, hoc opus, hic labor est.
units.tr: Augustine, in volume 7, against the Donatists, book 4, chapter 24, hands down this rule: "What the whole Church holds, not instituted by Councils but always retained, is most rightly believed to have been handed down by no other authority than the Apostolic." He repeats almost the same in his letter to Januarius, 118. I do not reject this rule but embrace it: namely, if something has been retained in the Church (that is, throughout, and in all) and always (that is, from the very times of the Apostles, without any interruption), that comes from Apostolic tradition. But to prove this, this is the work, here is the labour.

units.la: Ergo certiorem nos adferemus regulam: Ea autem hæc est: Si hæ traditiones una ex parte fundamentum habeant aliquod in scripturis, hoc est, si possint è scripturis necessario concludi: & ex altera faciant ad pietatem promouendam, hoc est, tam ad internum cultum, qui consistit in fide, spe, charitate & bona conscientia, excitandum, conseruandum, promouendum: quam ad externum, qui consistit in sacrasacramentorum perceptione & precibus publicis reverentius exercendum: has dicimus esse Apo-stolicas, eoq; ut pias & salutares esse recipiendas & observandas. Ratio huiusce regulae est, quòd omnes Apostolorum traditiones, de quibus nemo dubitat, quin Apostolorum fuerint, hæc duo habuerunt, primum fundamentum in verbo Dei: deinde utilitatem ad pietatem promouendam & ædificationem.
units.tr: Therefore we will offer a more certain rule, and it is this: If these traditions have, on the one hand, some foundation in the Scriptures, that is, if they can be necessarily concluded from the Scriptures; and on the other hand they serve to promote piety, that is, both to arouse, preserve and advance the inner worship, which consists in faith, hope, charity and a good conscience, and the outer worship, which consists in reverently exercising the reception of the sacraments and public prayers: these we say are Apostolic, and are therefore to be received and observed as pious and salutary. The reason for this rule is that all the traditions of the Apostles, about which no one doubts that they are the Apostles', had these two things: first a foundation in the Word of God, and then usefulness for promoting piety and edification.

units.la: Id quod manifestum fit 1. ex generali regula, quam Apostolus præscribit de iis rebus 1. Corinth. 14. Omnia ad ædificationem fiant. Item infra, Omnia autem decenter, & secundum ordinem fiant. Ergo hanc quoque servarunt regulam Apostoli in suis traditionibus.
units.tr: This becomes evident, first, from the general rule which the Apostle prescribes concerning such matters, 1 Corinthians 14: "Let all things be done for edification." Likewise below: "But let all things be done decently and in order." Therefore the Apostles also observed this rule in their traditions.

units.la: 2. Ex locis, ubi legimus constitutiones Apostolorum. In omnibus illis locis hęc duo videbis, primum, omnes illas Apostolicas institutiones, habere fundamentum in verbo Dei, hoc est, in doctrina Prophetica & Christi. 2. finem habere ædificationem Ecclesiæ, ut serviant cultui divino, vel spirituali & interno, vel corporali & externo, qui tamen etiam propter internum est institutus. Exempla aliquot.
units.tr: Second, from the places where we read the constitutions of the Apostles. In all those places you will see these two things: first, that all those Apostolic institutions have a foundation in the Word of God, that is, in the prophetic and Christian teaching; second, that they have as their end the edification of the Church, so that they serve divine worship, whether inward and spiritual, or outward and bodily, which nevertheless is also instituted for the sake of the inward. A few examples.

units.la: 1. Corinth. 11. instituit, ut in Ecclesia mulie-res orent capite tecto, viri detecto. Primum vide, quot utatur rationibus e scripturis deductis, ut ostendat, hanc constitutionem esse recipiendam, & esse secundum voluntatem Dei. Imò præmittit, dicendo, Imitatores mei estote, sicut & ego Christi. Secundò, vide finem huius constitutionis: esse honestatem, decorum in Ecclesia seruandum, eoque ædificationem Ecclesiæ, hoc est, ut externus cultus, ut est auditio verbi, & preces, & sacramentorum perceptio, maiori cum honestate & decoro exerceatur. Item alium finem, ut quisque ea cæremonia moneatur sui officij, hoc est, ut agnoscat vir, se caput esse mulieris: mulier suæ subiectionis, qua subiecta est viro. Hæc autem sunt utilia ad cultum internum.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 11 establishes that in the Church "women should pray with the head covered, men uncovered." First, see how many reasons he uses, drawn from the Scriptures, to show that this constitution is to be received and is according to the will of God. Indeed he prefaces it by saying, "Be imitators of me, as I also am of Christ." Second, see the end of this constitution: that decency and seemliness are to be kept in the Church, and thereby the edification of the Church, that is, that the outward worship, such as the hearing of the Word, the prayers and the reception of the sacraments, be exercised with greater honour and decorum. Likewise another end: that each one be reminded by that ceremony of his office, that is, that the man acknowledge that he is the head of the woman, and the woman her subjection, by which she is subject to the man. These things, moreover, are useful for the inward worship.

units.la: Item ibidem statuit, modum celebrandi Cœnam Domini: nimirum, ut omnes simul conueniant, & alter alterum exspectet. Primò ostendit hoc ex verbo Dei, id est, ex institutione Christi, esse faciendum. 2. Finis est ipsorum salus, ut ne fiant rei corporis Christi: Item, ut cœna maiori cum reuerentia sumatur: Et ut hæc externa cæremonia conueniendi simul, seruiat interno cultui, fidei, scil-licet & charitati, vnionique animorum.
units.tr: Likewise in the same place he lays down the manner of celebrating the Lord's Supper: namely, that all come together at once and wait for one another. First, he shows that this is to be done from the Word of God, that is, from the institution of Christ. Second, the end is their own salvation, so that they do not become guilty of the body of Christ; likewise, that the Supper be received with greater reverence; and that this outward ceremony of assembling together serve the inward worship, namely faith and charity, and the union of souls.

units.la: 1.Corinth.14.Instituit, quomodo debeant in Ecclesia uti linguis: nimirum, ut non loquantur linguis sine explicatione & interpretatione. 1. Quot rationibus utitur e scripturis etiam deductis, ut probet, hoc esse iuxta voluntatem Dei, bonum & honestum. Nam post multas rationes, attulit etiam scripturam, dicendo: In lege scriptum est, variis linguis, & labiis variis loquar populo huic (infideli) & ne sic quidem audient me: quasi dicat Apostolus, Ne sinatis huiuscemodi homines loqui in Ecclesia, qui peregrinis loquuntur linguis sine explicatione. Nam hoc signum esset[?], Deum vos non amare, quòd tales solet mittere Prophetas populo infideli, quem non vult veritatem intelligere, & sacras Literas noscere. 2. Finem huius institutionis aperte dicit esse aedificationem Ecclesiae, vt habeant consolationem, exhortationem, &c. hoc est, vt seruiat cultui interno, fidei, charitati, consolationi spiritus.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 14. He lays down how they ought to use tongues in the Church: namely, that they not speak in tongues without explanation and interpretation. First, with how many reasons, also drawn from the Scriptures, he uses to prove that this is according to the will of God, good and honourable. For after many reasons he also brought in Scripture, saying: "In the law it is written, 'With other tongues and other lips I will speak to this people (the unbelieving), and even so they will not hear me.'" As if the Apostle were saying, "Do not allow people of this kind to speak in the Church, who speak in foreign tongues without explanation. For this would be a sign that God does not love you, since he is accustomed to send such Prophets to an unbelieving people, which does not want to understand the truth and to know the sacred Letters." Second, he openly says the end of this institution is the edification of the Church, so that they may have consolation, exhortation, etc., that is, that it serve the inward worship, faith, charity, and comfort of the spirit.

units.la: Ephes.4. Cùm verba facit de fine, propter quem Christus in Ecclesia instituit Ministe-rium: docet esse aedificationem corporis Christi. Hinc colligimus finem omnium ceremoniarum, & quæcunque in cœtu fidelium instituuntur & fiunt, debere esse aedificationem Ecclesiae. Si hic absit, nullae sunt bonae, & ex Christi voluntate institutiones traditionesve Ecclesiasticae.
units.tr: Ephesians 4. When he speaks of the purpose for which Christ instituted the ministry in the Church, he teaches that it is the edification of the body of Christ. From this we conclude that the purpose of all ceremonies, and of whatever is instituted and done in the assembly of the faithful, must be the edification of the Church. If this is lacking, no institutions or ecclesiastical traditions are good, nor are they from the will of Christ.

units.la: 2.Thess.2. Ubi dicit, Tenete traditiones quas didicistis, praemisit haec verba: Nos autem gratias agere debemus Deo semper pro vobis, dilecti à Deo, quod elegerit nos Deus ab initio in salutem, in sanctificatione spiritus. Vide reliqua.
units.tr: 2 Thessalonians 2. Where he says, Hold the traditions which you have been taught, he has first set down these words: But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning to salvation, in sanctification of the Spirit. See the rest.

units.la: Docet illis verbis, quales illis traditiones commendet, quasque ab Apostolo accepe-rint illi: nempe tales, per quas commoveri potuissent ad plenius obtemperandum Deo, ad proficiendum in sanctificatione spiritus, in fide veritatis, & in acquisitione gloriæ Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Finis igitur tra-ditionum ditionum est,ut seruiant ad proficiendum in sanctificatione spiritus, in fide veritatis, & in acquisitione gloriæ Christi.
units.tr: By these words he shows what sort of traditions he commends, and which ones they had received from the Apostle: namely, such as could move them to obey God more fully, to advance in sanctification of the Spirit, in faith of the truth, and in the attainment of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. The purpose of traditions, therefore, is that they serve to advance in sanctification of the Spirit, in faith of the truth, and in the attainment of the glory of Christ.

units.la: 1. Corinth. s. ubi instituit, quomodo excommunicatio exerceri debeat in illum incestum, mox ostendit causam finalem, ut scilicet ille pudefactus in carne, prouocetur fortius ad pœnitentiam, & ita spiritus saluus fiat. Illæ igitur traditiones, quibus homines magis ad pœnitentiam veram prouocantur, Apostolicæ sunt & bonæ.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 5. Where he lays down how excommunication ought to be exercised against that incestuous man, he immediately shows the final cause: namely, that he, shamed in the flesh, might be provoked more strongly to repentance, and so his spirit be saved. Those traditions, therefore, by which men are more stirred to true repentance, are apostolic and good.

units.la: Idem in 2. Cor. 7. probat illas contristationes, quæ excitant ad pœnitentiam. Nam etiamsi (inquit) vos contristaui per Epistolam, non me pœnitet. Nam gaudeo, quòd contristati estis ad pœnitentiam.
units.tr: In 2 Corinthians 7 he likewise approves those sorrows which stir people to repentance. For even if (he says) I made you sorry by my letter, I do not regret it. For I rejoice that you were made sorry unto repentance.

units.la: 1. Timoth. 5. Illa traditio, ne iuniores viduæ admittantur ad illud Ministerium Ecclesiæ, quo seruiebatur sanctis ægrotis, & alia pietatis exercitia præstabantur: sumtibus autem Ecclesiæ hoc hominum genus sustentabatur: fuit ideò instituta ab Apostolo, quia utilis erat Ecclesiæ, & etiam illis viduis ad ædificationem cedebat, ut liquet ex contextu.
units.tr: 1 Timothy 5. The tradition that younger widows should not be admitted to that ministry of the Church by which the holy sick were served, and other works of piety were performed, (and this class of people was supported at the expense of the Church), was therefore instituted by the Apostle, because it was useful to the Church, and also turned to the edification of those widows themselves, as is clear from the context.

units.la: Item quæ scribit Ephes. 5. & 6. de officio parentum erga liberos, liberorum erga parentes: seruorum erga dominos, dominorum erga seruos. Item 1. Timoth. 6. de seruorum officio erga dominos. Item 1. Timoth. 5. de modo, quo admonendi & corrigendi sint senes, mulieres, &c. Et quæ 1. Pet. 2. de officio subditorum erga suos Magistratus etiam impios. pios.Item, quæ de ornatu & vestimentis mulierum,1.Tim.2.&1.Pet.3.Et si quæ aliæ reperiuntur traditiones in scriptis Apostolicis, videbis in eis hæc duo: primùm, fundamentum eas habere in verbo Dei, in lege Domini: secundò, illarum finem esse ædificationem, & vt quisque diligentius incumbat suæ vocationi, & spiritualem promoueat cultum.
units.tr: Likewise what he writes in Ephesians 5 and 6 about the duty of parents toward children and of children toward parents, of servants toward masters and of masters toward servants. Likewise 1 Timothy 6 about the duty of servants toward masters. Likewise 1 Timothy 5 about the manner in which old men, women, and so on are to be admonished and corrected. And what 1 Peter 2 says about the duty of subjects toward their magistrates, even impious ones. Likewise what concerns the adornment and clothing of women, 1 Timothy 2 and 1 Peter 3. And if any other traditions are found in the Apostolic writings, you will see in them these two things: first, that they have their foundation in the Word of God, in the law of the Lord; second, that their purpose is edification, and that each person may apply himself more diligently to his own calling and promote spiritual worship.

units.la: Hinc igitur colligitur regula de omnibus aliis traditionibus, quæ in scripturis non continentur. Quomodo poterunt agnosci an sint Apostolicæ, nec ne? 1. Si fundamentum habeant in verbo Dei. 2. Si faciant ad promouendam pietatem, ad excitädam pœnitentiam & fidem: deniq; si ad id seruiant, vt fideles maiori studio, & maiori cum fructu, tam doctrinam, quàm sacramenta, & mandata Dei audiant percipiantq;, plenius credant,& in tota vita obseruent. Quæ illud non habent, neque ad hunc finem tendunt, inutiles & vanæ sunt: ideo non Apostolicæ sed meræ humanæ. Si verò aut pugnent cum verbo Dei, aut eò faciant, vt homines in iis & suis operibus ponant fiduciam& spem remissionis peccatorum ac salutis,sunt Diabolicæ. Atq; hæc de secundo satis.
units.tr: Hence, then, a rule is drawn concerning all other traditions which are not contained in the Scriptures. How can it be recognised whether they are apostolic or not? (1) If they have a foundation in the Word of God. (2) If they serve to promote piety, to stir up repentance and faith; finally, if they serve so that the faithful may hear and receive, with greater zeal and greater fruit, the doctrine, the sacraments and the commandments of God, believe them more fully, and observe them throughout their lives. Those which do not have this, nor tend to this end, are useless and vain, and so not apostolic but merely human. But if they either conflict with the Word of God, or have the effect that men place their trust and hope in them, and in their own works, for the remission of sins and salvation, they are diabolical. And this is enough concerning the second point.

units.la: Cùm hæc ita habeant: nunc singulæ traditiones, quæ apud Patres leguntur, ad has regulas examinandæ essent, & videndum, quænam fundamentum habeant in scripturis,quæ non habeant: Item quæ seruiant pietati promouendæ, & sacramentis reuerenter participandis,& quæ non seruiant:atque ita concludendum, quæ sint Apostolicæ, ac proinde recipiendæ, & quæ non,ac proinde reiiciendç[?]:Sed quia hæc res nimiæ esset prolixitatis,idcirco sufficiat in præsentia, si breuibus aliquot propositionibus complectar ea, quæ fusius aliàs de iis omnibus traditionibus explicabuntur.
units.tr: Since these things stand thus, the individual traditions which are read among the Fathers ought now to be examined by these rules, and it should be seen which have a foundation in the Scriptures and which do not; likewise which serve to promote piety and to receive the sacraments reverently, and which do not serve; and thus it should be concluded which are apostolic, and therefore to be received, and which are not, and therefore to be rejected. But since this matter would be of excessive length, it will suffice for the present if I embrace them in a few brief propositions, the rest of which will be explained at greater length elsewhere concerning all those traditions.

units.la: In genere igitur& in vniuersum de tradi-tionibus,quæ apud Patres leguntur,retinendæ sunt hæ propositiones.
units.tr: In general, therefore, and as a whole, concerning the traditions which are read among the Fathers, the following propositions are to be maintained.

units.la: Prima: Quædam sunt,quæ non solùm habent fundamentum in verbo Dei,verùm etiam semper efficaciter faciunt ad pietatem exercendam, promouendam, conseruandam,ac proinde Apostolicæ sunt,& omnibus Christianis seruandæ, & quæ bona conscientia omitti non possunt: vt, de summa doctrinæ Christianæ, quæ in symbolo continetur: vt de habendis publicis precibus inEcclesia, certis diebus, pro omnibus hominibus: vt de administratione sacramentorum publica,non priuata,ram[?] Baptismi, quàm Cœnæ: vt de solenni exercitio disciplinæ & excommunicationis.Hæ enim omnes,&aliæ etiam similes, testimonium habent in verbo Dei apertum, & plurimum conducunt ad pietatem & ad ædificationem Ecclesiæ: & ab omnibus Ecclesiis fuerunt receptæ: & proinde etiam Catholicæ & Apostolicæ appellatæ.
units.tr: First: There are some which not only have a foundation in the Word of God, but also always effectively serve to exercise, promote and preserve piety, and therefore are apostolic, and are to be observed by all Christians, and cannot be omitted with a good conscience: such as the sum of Christian doctrine, which is contained in the creed; such as the holding of public prayers in the Church on set days for all men; such as the public, not private, administration of the sacraments, both of Baptism and of the Supper; such as the solemn exercise of discipline and excommunication. For all these, and others also of a similar kind, have clear testimony in the Word of God, and contribute greatly to piety and to the edification of the Church; and they have been received by all the churches, and therefore are also called catholic and apostolic.

units.la: Secunda: Aliæ sunt, quæ fundamentū quidem habent in verbo Dei, & aliquando et-iam profuerunt ad pietatem: sed iam non amplius prosunt:ac proinde Apostolicæ quidem sunt, sed quia non amplius utiles, idcirco non est necesse, ut observentur. Ut illa traditio de abstinendo ab idolothytis, sanguine, & suffocato: Ac proinde etiamsi hæ fuerunt Apostolicæ, non sunt tamen Catholicæ.
units.tr: Second: Others are those which indeed have a foundation in the Word of God, and sometimes also profited piety, but now no longer profit; and therefore they are indeed apostolic, but since they are no longer useful, it is not necessary that they be observed. Such is that tradition of abstaining from things offered to idols, from blood, and from what is strangled. And therefore, although these were apostolic, they are nevertheless not catholic.

units.la: Tertia: Quædam non habent fundamentum in verbo Dei, sed tamen possent ad pie-tatem facere & ad ædificationem, si sine super-stitione exercerentur. Ideo non Apostolicæ quidem sunt, sed Ecclesiasticæ. Et harum Ecclesiasticarum quædam sunt universales, & ab omnibus Ecclesiis & semper admissæ, ac proinde Catholicæ dictæ: ut, quòd celebretur dies Natalis Domini, Pascharis, Ascen-sionis, Pentecostes, & id genus alia. Ideo hæ contemnendæ non sunt, sed servandæ, modò absit omnis superstitio.
units.tr: Third: Some have no foundation in the Word of God, but yet could serve piety and edification if they were practised without superstition. Therefore they are indeed not apostolic, but ecclesiastical. And of these ecclesiastical traditions some are universal, admitted by all the churches and always, and therefore called catholic: such as that the birthday of the Lord, Easter, the Ascension, Pentecost, and other things of this kind are celebrated. These, therefore, are not to be despised, but to be kept, provided that all superstition is absent.

units.la: Quarta: quædam vero sunt particulares, à particularibus Episcopis in suis Ecclesiis institutæ, & hac de causa Episcopales appellatæ: atque hæ proinde liberæ sunt & esse debent omnibus Ecclesiis: ut, de tempore ce-lebrandi Pascha: aliud fuit tempus Ecclesiis in Asia, aliud Ecclesiis in occidente. Ita de traditionibus celebrandi Cœnam, alibi fre-quentius, alibi rarius.
units.tr: Fourth: But some are particular, instituted by particular bishops in their own churches, and for this reason called episcopal; and these are therefore free and ought to be free for all churches: such as the time of celebrating Easter. One time was observed by the churches in Asia, another by the churches in the West. So too with the traditions of celebrating the Supper: in one place more often, in another more rarely.

units.la: Quinta: Quædam vero sunt, quæ nullum habent in scripturis fundamentum, & nihil faciunt ad pietatem, neq; ad ædificationem: sed neq; pugnant cum verbo Dei, neq; sunt contra pietatem suapte natura. Ideo Apostolicæ esse non possunt, sed merè humanæ. Et tales permultæ retinentur in Papatu, inanes & leues: vt, quòd in Cœna Domini aliquid aquæ imponatur in vinum.
units.tr: Fifth: But some are such that they have no foundation in the Scriptures, and contribute nothing to piety or edification; yet they neither conflict with the Word of God nor are contrary to piety by their own nature. Therefore they cannot be apostolic, but are merely human. And very many such are retained in Papacy, empty and light: such as that something of water is put into the wine in the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Sexta: Quædam autem sunt, quæ pugnant cum verbo Dei, eóque etiam obsunt pietati: ac proinde nec Apostolicæ sunt, nec Ecclesiasticæ, nec merè humanæ, sed diabolicæ: eóq; nec liberæ, sed damnandæ & vitandæ: Vt, quod tradit Epiphanius, Eos qui post votum virginitatis vel cœlibatus vxores ducunt, peccare: Vt, traditio de retinendis imaginibus, de inuocandis mortuis. At sancti sunt, qui hæc scripta reliquerunt. Resp. Fuerunt etiam homines, ideo & falli & fallere potuerunt.
units.tr: Sixth: But some are those which conflict with the Word of God, and by that also harm piety; and therefore they are neither apostolic, nor ecclesiastical, nor merely human, but diabolical; and therefore not free, but to be condemned and avoided: such as what Epiphanius hands down, that those who marry wives after a vow of virginity or celibacy sin; such as the tradition of retaining images and of invoking the dead. But they are holy men who left these writings. Answer: there were also men, and therefore they could both be deceived and deceive.

units.la: Cæterùm ex iis omnibus, quæ de traditionibus istis diximus, non potest colligi, aliquid ad salutem esse necessarium, & ad pietatem pertinere, quod non continetur in sacris literis. Nam omnes bonæ traditiones, vt Apostolicæ, fundamentum habent in verbo Dei: Quæ autem sunt tantùm Ecclesiasticæ, liberæ sunt omnibus Ecclesiis.
units.tr: Moreover, from all those things which we have said about these traditions, it cannot be concluded that anything is necessary to salvation and pertains to piety which is not contained in the sacred letters. For all good traditions, as apostolic, have their foundation in the Word of God; but those which are only ecclesiastical are free for all churches.

units.la: Ex iis propositionibus generalibus liquet, quid ad quædam specialia Patrum de Traditionibus dicta, respondendum sit.
units.tr: From these general propositions it is clear how the particular sayings of the Fathers about traditions are to be answered.

units.la: Et primùm ad illud, quòd scribunt Ecclesiam accepisse ab Apostolis non solùm ἐγγραφα[?], sed etiam ἀγραφα[?], Basilius de Spiritu sancto, Epiphanius.
units.tr: And first, to what they write, that the Church received from the Apostles not only written things [ἐγγραφα] but also unwritten things [ἀγραφα]: Basil, On the Holy Spirit, and Epiphanius.

units.la: Resp. Hoc facile damus, ut liquet de symbolo Apostolico, quod tamen in scripturis iuxta illam verborum formam & ordinem non continetur: Et hanc dicimus esse primam ac praecipuam Apostolorum traditionem ἀγραφον[?]: Et ut est traditio de libris Canonicis & Apocryphis. Item multa, quae ad disciplinam & ritus Ecclesiasticos pertinent: de synodis etiam habendis: de ieiuniis tempore calamitoso indicendis: Et multa alia id genus, fatemur Ecclesiam accepisse ab Apostolis: sine scripto: Sed addimus, haec omnia fundamentum habere in scripturis: & deinde nihil ab Apostolis fuisse institutum, quod non faceret ad pietatem, & aedificationem Ecclesiae. Nihil etiam leve, nihil ludicrum, nihil superstitiosum. Item, addimus, quoad doctrinam, nihil diversum ore docuisse ab eo, quod scriptum reliquerunt. Quoad sacramenta, eos nullum sacramentis duobus à Christo institutis, adiecisse.
units.tr: Answer: We readily grant this, as is clear in the case of the Apostles' Creed, which nevertheless is not contained in Scripture in that particular form of words and order. We call this the first and chief tradition of the Apostles, unwritten [ἀγραφον]. So too is the tradition concerning the canonical and apocryphal books. Likewise, we admit that the Church received from the Apostles, without writing, many things which pertain to church discipline and ecclesiastical rites, such as the holding of synods, and the proclaiming of fasts in times of calamity, and many other things of this kind. But we add that all these have their foundation in the Scriptures; and further, that the Apostles instituted nothing that did not serve piety and the edification of the Church, nothing trivial, nothing frivolous, nothing superstitious. We add also that, as regards doctrine, they taught nothing orally that differed from what they left in writing; and as regards the sacraments, they added nothing to the two sacraments instituted by Christ.

units.la: Secundum dictum Patrum est: Quae Ecclesia accepit per traditionem & ἀγραφα[?]: parem habere vim ad pietatem, & pares esse autoritatis, cum iis, quae accepit ἐγγραφα[?], Basil. de Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: The second saying of the Fathers is: What the Church received through tradition and unwritten [ἀγραφα] things has equal force for piety, and equal authority, with those things which it received in writing: Basil, On the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Resp. Hoc admittimus in illis traditionibus, quae aperta habent in scripturis testimonia, & ad pietatem non solum utiles sunt, sed etiam necessariae, & ideo ab omnibus Ecclesiis semper admissæ, eoque Apostolicæ & Catholicæ: vt, traditio de symbolo, de-libris Canonicis, & aliis quibusdam: Sed non admittimus, nec admittendum est in omnibus.
units.tr: Answer: We admit this of those traditions which have clear testimonies in Scripture, and which are not only useful but also necessary for piety, and therefore have always been admitted by all churches, and are thus apostolic and catholic: such as the tradition concerning the creed, concerning the canonical books, and certain others. But we do not admit, nor is it to be admitted, that this holds of all.

units.la: Tertium dictum: Traditiones esse pari religione seruandas, qua & illa, quæ habemus in scripturis.
units.tr: The third saying: That traditions are to be kept with the same reverence as those things which we have in Scripture.

units.la: Resp. Damus de illis Catholicis, de quibus antea dictum est: non de omnibus, etiamsi habeant testimonium in scripturis, & aliquando fecerunt ad pietatem: vt traditio de abstinendo à suffocato & sanguine, habebat testimonium in scripturis: item faciebat ad pietatem per aliquod tempus, sed iam non facit. Ideo non est pari religione seruanda. Proinde dicimus, illas esse obseruatu neces-sarias, quas primò constat esse conformes sacris Literis, & secundò obseruatas semper fuisse, & in omnibus Ecclesiis, iam inde à tempore Apostolorum. Ideo quæ non sunt huiusmodi, non cogimur admittere: Sed sequenda est regula Apostoli 1. Thess. 5. Omnia probate, quod bonum est tenete.
units.tr: Answer: We grant this of those catholic traditions of which we spoke above, but not of all, even if they have testimony in Scripture and at some time served piety. For example, the tradition of abstaining from what is strangled and from blood had testimony in Scripture, and for some time served piety, but no longer does. Therefore it is not to be kept with the same reverence. Accordingly we say that those are necessary to observe which, first, it is evident conform to the sacred Scriptures, and second, have always been observed, and in all churches, from the time of the Apostles onward. Therefore we are not compelled to admit those which are not of this kind; but the rule of the Apostle must be followed, 1 Thess. 5: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

units.la: Quartum dictum apud Epiphan. in refutatione Apostolic. Vbi existit traditio Eccle-sia, nihil inquirendum. Item illud Augustini ad Ianuarium: Disputare de eo, quod Ecclesia per totum terrarum orbem seruat, insolentissima est insania.
units.tr: The fourth saying is in Epiphanius, in his refutation of the Apostolics: Where the tradition of the Church exists, nothing is to be inquired into. Likewise that saying of Augustine to Januarius: To dispute about what the Church keeps throughout the whole world is the most insolent madness.

units.la: Resp. Hæc dicta intelliguntur de traditionibus Catholicis & Apostolicis, fundatis in verbo Dei, & ad obseruandum necessa-riis, de quibus supra. Multi autem abusus in-troducti sunt in Ecclesiam, de quibus Augu-stinus ad Ianuar. 118. De iis certe non loqui-tur Augustinus, necalij Patres.
units.tr: Answer: These sayings are to be understood of the catholic and apostolic traditions, grounded in the Word of God and necessary to be observed, of which we spoke above. But many abuses have been introduced into the Church, of which Augustine speaks in letter 118 to Januarius. Certainly Augustine, and the other Fathers, do not speak of these.

units.la: Quintum dictum est speciale Irenæi & Ter-tulliani, veritatem religionis Christianæ requirendam esse apud Ecclesias Apostolicas, inter quas speciatim collocat Romanam. Item, quòd de harum Ecclesiarum fide & authoritate præscribendum sit hæreticis: ita vt cum iis, qui harum Ecclesiarum authoritatem reiiciunt, non sit per scripturas agendum.
units.tr: The fifth saying is the particular one of Irenaeus and Tertullian, that the truth of the Christian religion is to be sought among the apostolic churches, among which they especially place the Roman. Likewise, that judgment is to be pronounced on heretics from the faith and authority of these churches, so that with those who reject the authority of these churches one should not deal by means of the Scriptures.

units.la: Resp. Vt cum fructu hæc Patrum dicta ex-plicentur ac intelligantur, notanda sunt qua-tuor in iis dictis.
units.tr: Answer: So that these sayings of the Fathers may be explained and understood with profit, four things are to be noted in them.

units.la: 1. Quales nam essent illæ Ecclesiæ, ad quas volebant recurri, & quarum authoritatem ita [?] magnificiebant, vt si quis eas, & quæ apud ipsas erant traditiones reiiceret, cum hoc negarent esse è scripturis disputandum.
units.tr: 1. What manner of churches these were to which they wished recourse to be had, and whose authority they so magnified that, if anyone rejected them, and the traditions which were among them, they declared that one should not dispute from Scripture with him.

units.la: 2. De quánam veritate loquerentur ij Pa-tres, cùm scribebant inquirendam esse veri-tatem apud Ecclesias Apostolicas.
units.tr: 2. Of what truth those Fathers were speaking when they wrote that the truth is to be sought among the apostolic churches.

units.la: 3. Quando tandem provocarint ad illas Ecclesias.
units.tr: 3. When, at length, they appealed to those churches.

units.la: 4. Quam ob causam.
units.tr: 4. For what cause.

units.la: Quod ad primum attinet: Ecclesiæ illæ, atque inprimis Romana, erant veræ Apostolicæ & Christianæ, non nomine tantùm, sed re ipsa, puritate doctrinæ, sinceritate sacramentorum, seueritate disciplinæ, constantia in fide, fortitudine animi in perferendis pro Christo omne genus tormentis, charitate in fratres[?], mortificatione carnis, honestate vitæ, contemtu Mundi, denique sanctificatione, & Christianis Apostolicisq; moribus. Ecclesiæ erant recens ab Apostolis plantatæ, in purissima doctrina, & seueta[?] disciplina instituta, à nemine adhuc adulteratæ, à nemine vitiatæ, ceu castissimæ & incontaminatæ virgines, in quarum ore recens adhuc lac Apostolicum hærebat, suauissimeque olebat. Atque in primis, ut dixi, Romana, quemadmodum Patres omnes illi vetustissimi testificantur: cui nihil vel ab ipsis hæreticis obiici poterat merito. Ergo ad hanc, & huius similes Ecclesias, tanquam ad illas, apud quas purissima manebat doctrina, provocabant Patres, & volebant eas esse controuersiarum iudi-ces, urgebántque illarum autoritatem, & contendebant, cum iis, qui harum reiicerent autoritatem, non esse amplius è scripturis disputandum. Sed quæ dissimilitudo est inter illam & hanc? Quæ inter castam virginem, & impudentissimum scortum. Ac pto-inde quæ etiam est impudentia, quæ Patres scribunt de illa sanctissima & castissima virgine, ea retorquere ad hoc putidissimum, impudicissimum, & impudentissimum scortum? ad præsentem scilicet Romanam Babylonem? quæ nihil vel parum retinet amplius Apostolicæ vel doctrinæ, vel pietatis, vel disciplinæ: sed in qua diabolus regnat, in qua sedet patefactus iam totiOrbi Antichri-stus. Legantur obsecro, quæ apud Ezechielem scribuntur de Ecclesia Israel, cap.16.
units.tr: As to the first: Those churches, and above all the Roman, were truly apostolic and Christian, not in name only but in fact: in purity of doctrine, sincerity of the sacraments, strictness of discipline, constancy in the faith, courage of spirit in enduring every kind of torment for Christ, love toward the brethren, mortification of the flesh, honesty of life, contempt of the world, and in short sanctification and Christian and apostolic manners. They were churches recently planted by the Apostles, established in the purest doctrine and strict discipline, not yet corrupted by anyone, not yet defiled by anyone, like most chaste and undefiled virgins, in whose mouths the apostolic milk still clung and smelled most sweetly. And above all, as I have said, the Roman, as all those most ancient Fathers testify; of which nothing could justly be objected even by the heretics themselves. Therefore it was to this church, and churches like it, as to those in which the purest doctrine remained, that the Fathers appealed; they wanted these to be the judges of controversies, and they urged their authority, and they contended that with those who rejected their authority there was no longer any need to dispute from Scripture. But what a difference there is between that church and this! What difference between a chaste virgin and the most shameless harlot! And so, what impudence is it to turn back upon this most foul, most unchaste and most shameless harlot, the present Roman Babylon, those things which the Fathers write of that most holy and chaste virgin? Who now retains little or nothing of apostolic doctrine, piety or discipline, but in which the devil reigns, in which sits Antichrist, now revealed to the whole world. Let there be read, I beg you, what is written in Ezekiel concerning the Church of Israel, chapter 16.

units.la: Principiò, posteaquam illi ostendit suam originem, unde sit educta, explicat, quanta diligentia fuerit à Deo mundata omni labe, lota, purgata, bene nutrita, sanctissimè educata, bene colorata, pulcherrimè vestita, & omni ornamentorum genere ornata: & ita eam comparat castissimæ & formosissimæ sponsæ. Deinde explicat, quid porrò facta sit, confisa suâ pulchritudine. Factam esse dicit scortum obscœnissimum, impudentis-simum. Legatur locus.
units.tr: First, after he has shown her origin, whence she was brought forth, he explains with what great care she was cleansed by God from every stain, washed, purified, well nourished, most delicately brought up, well coloured, most beautifully clothed, and adorned with every kind of ornament; and so he makes her out as a most chaste and most beautiful bride. Then he explains what she afterwards became, trusting in her own beauty. He says she became a most obscene and most shameless harlot. Let the passage be read.

units.la: Hic interrogo Romanenses: si, quæ ibi prædicat Propheta de illa Ecclesia, antequam scortaretur, vellet quis ad eandem etiam accommodare, posteaquam facta fuit scortum, an non esset impudens? Tales estis vos, dum quæ prædicant Patres de Ecclesia illa prima Romana, deque illius auctoritate, de præsen-ti quoque interpretamini. Nam quæ scribit Ezechiel de duplici statu Ecclesiæ Israeliticæ, vaticinia fuerunt de duplici statu Romanæ Ecclesiæ. Fuit speciosa virgo: nunc est fœdissimum scortum. Ergo nihil ad vos pertinent ea, quæ Irenæus & Tertullianus de prima illa Romana Ecclesia, deque illius auctoritate scripta reliquerunt. Sed si detur nobis talis Ecclesia, qualis illa prima fuit: nos etiam libenter dabimus vobis hanc auctoritatem.
units.tr: Here I ask the Romanists: if someone wished to apply to that church what the prophet there proclaims about her before she played the harlot, would he not be shameless, after she had become a harlot? You are such people, when you interpret what the Fathers proclaim about that first Roman church, and about its authority, as applying to the present. For what Ezekiel writes of the twofold state of the Israelite Church was a prophecy of the twofold state of the Roman Church. She was once a beautiful virgin; now she is a most foul harlot. Therefore those things which Irenaeus and Tertullian wrote about that first Roman church, and about its authority, have nothing to do with you. But if we are given such a church as that first one was, we too will gladly grant you this authority.

units.la: Quod ad secundum attinet: Quanam erat illa veritas, quam inquirendam esse dicebant Patres apud Ecclesias Apostolicas, & cumprimis apud Romanam? Veritas erat primorum & praecipuorum Christianæ religionis articulorum, de Deo creatore rerum omnium & gubernatore: de Christo Filio Dei, & vero Deo: de vera eius morte & resurrectione.
units.tr: As to the second: what was that truth which the Fathers said was to be sought among the apostolic churches, and especially among the Roman? It was the truth of the first and chief articles of the Christian religion: concerning God, creator and governor of all things; concerning Christ, the Son of God and true God; concerning his true death and resurrection.

units.la: Fuerat hæc veritas primum prædicata per Apostolos, deinde scriptis consignata: ita apud omnes Ecclesias partim per traditionem, partim in scriptis deposita. Erat igitur veritas, de qua nullæ Ecclesiæ dubitabant, certa, cognita, perspecta, quæ quotidie prædicabatur, in scripturis legebatur, in scholis explicabatur. Quis igitur non merito ad illas Ecclesias, pro hac veritate tam fideliter conseruata tamque certa, prouocasset? Sed quid hæc ad illa, quæ iam inter nos & Romanam Ecclesiam controuertuntur? Nam hæc nunquam fuerunt apud omnes Ecclesias recepta, in scripturis non sunt expressa, neque e scripturis erui possunt: sed ab ipsa Ecclesia Romana contra scripturas excogitata: de primatu Papæ? hunc Ecclesiæ Orientales nunquam vobis permiserunt. De purgatorio igne, de hoc etiam altercatio fuit inter Orientales & Occidentales Ecclesias: De imaginibus in templis, quot dissidia & etiam bella inter Orientales & Occidentales? imo & inter ipsosmet Orientales, dum alij eas damnabat, alij probabant? Idem de aliis controuersiis possem demonstrare. Sed quis hæc novit? Non fuisse hanc de iis controuersiis doctri-nam, quam nunc tenet & profitetur Ecclesia Romana, apud omnes Ecclesias receptam: imò neque semper in Ecclesia Romana lo-cum habuisse: constat, hanc non contineri in symbolo: constat non probari posse apertis scripturarum testimoniis, ac proinde con-fugiunt ad traditiones. Constat etiam, has quas de hac doctrina urgent traditiones, non reperiri apud antiquos Patres. Quid igitur illa veritas, de qua Irenæus & Tertullianus, quæ & in scripturis erat & est expressa, & in symbolo Apostolico aliisque omnibus explicata, & apud omnes, nulla excepta, Christianas Ecclesias recepta, conseruata, verissi-ma, certissima, & extra omnem controuer-siam posita: quid, inquam, hæc veritas ad hæc præsentis Ecclesiæ Romanæ mendacia? Imò de illa veritate, de qua disputabant Irenæus & Tertullianus cum illis Hæreticis, de uno Deo creatore omnium, qui est pater Domini Iesu Christi, volumus adhuc cum illis Patribus provocare ad Ecclesiam Romanam. Vide quantum illi tribuamus? Quid igitur conqueruntur? Quæ igitur scribunt Patres illi, de inquirenda illa veritate, nihil perti-nent ad præsentes nostras controuersias.
units.tr: This truth was first preached by the Apostles, then consigned to writing; thus it was deposited among all churches, partly by tradition, partly in writings. It was therefore a truth about which no churches doubted: certain, known, well understood, which was preached daily, read in the Scriptures, explained in the schools. Who, then, would not justly have appealed to those churches for this truth, so faithfully and so certainly preserved? But what has this to do with those matters which are now in dispute between us and the Roman Church? For these were never received by all churches, are not expressed in the Scriptures, and cannot be drawn out of the Scriptures, but were devised by the Roman Church itself against the Scriptures: the primacy of the Pope? The Eastern churches never allowed you this. Concerning purgatorial fire, there was also controversy on this between the Eastern and Western churches. Concerning images in temples, how many dissensions and even wars between the Eastern and Western churches? Indeed, even among the Eastern themselves, while some condemned them and others approved them? I could demonstrate the same for other controversies. But who knows these things? That the doctrine on these controversies which the Roman Church now holds and professes was not received among all churches; indeed that it did not always have a place even in the Roman Church: it is established that this is not contained in the creed; it is established that it cannot be proved by clear testimonies of Scripture, and therefore they flee to tradition. It is also established that the traditions which they press concerning this doctrine are not to be found among the ancient Fathers. What then has that truth, about which Irenaeus and Tertullian spoke, which was both in the Scriptures and is expressed in them, and is explained in the Apostles' Creed and in all others, and was received, preserved, most true, most certain, and placed beyond all controversy among all Christian churches without exception, what, I say, has this truth to do with the lies of the present Roman Church? Indeed, to that truth about which Irenaeus and Tertullian disputed with those heretics, concerning the one God, creator of all, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, we are still willing to appeal, with those Fathers, to the Roman Church. See how much we attribute to them? Why then do they complain? Therefore those writings of the Fathers about inquiring after that truth have nothing to do with our present controversies.

units.la: Quod ad tertium: Quando illi Patres provo-cabant ad Ecclesias pro illa veritate? Postea-quam illam probassent primùm scripturis, deinde etiam traditione, hoc est, symbolo: Illi vero Hæretici aut scripturas reiecissent, aut aliarum negassent sensum, quem Patres afferebant: traditionem etiam, id est, symbolum non admisissent: Tum demum Patres, cum viderent, nihil sibi amplius superesse armorum, quibus illos hæreticos confoderent, & veritatem defenderent, nisi te-stimonia Ecclesiarum, prouocabant ad Ecclesias, non ad unam, sed ad omnes: ad Ecclesias, inquam, tales, quales ante descripsimus: Illas enim daturas testimonium, primùm, An hi libri, quos reiiciebant Hæretici tanquam Apocryphos, essent Canonici nec ne: Dein-de, an quem ex simplicibus verbis, simplicem afferebant sensum scripturarum, esset verus & genuinus, nec ne: & tertiò, an quam ur-ge-bant traditionem symboli, esset vera Apostolorum traditio, nec ne: ac proinde, an quam de uno Deo, déq; uno Filio Dei Chri-sto, defendebant doctrinam, vera esset nec ne: posse tantum illas Ecclesias, certum de iis rebus dare testimonium, propterea quòd ab Apostolis non ita multò ante institutæ in omni doctrina, non tam scriptis, quàm etiam voce, eam hucusque retineant doctrinam, & scripturarum intelligentiam, quam ab A-postolis viva voce acceperunt: id quod pro-babant illi Patres, quia ab eo tempore, quo fuerunt illæ Ecclesiæ ab Apostolis plantatæ & edoctæ, nunquam variarunt in doctrina: debere igitur illarum testimonium, ut cer-tissimum & verissimum admitti. Quòd si quis hoc etiam reiiciat, & hanc Ecclesiarum au-toritatem contemnat, se non amplius posse cum huiusce modi hominibus disputare. An non tunc merito provocabant ad Ecclesias, & ad tales Ecclesias? Annon tum merito di-cebant, non esse amplius cum his hominibus haereticis, solis scripturis disputandum?
units.tr: On the third point: when did those Fathers call the churches to witness to that truth? After they had first proved it from the Scriptures, and then also from tradition, that is, the creed: but those heretics had either rejected the Scriptures, or denied the sense which the Fathers gave them, and they had not admitted the tradition, that is, the creed. Then at last the Fathers, seeing that no weapons were left to them with which to strike down those heretics and defend the truth, except the testimony of the churches, called upon the churches, not one only but all of them: churches, I say, of the kind we described earlier. For these were to give testimony on three points: first, whether those books which the heretics rejected as apocryphal were canonical or not; then, whether the simple sense they drew from the plain words of Scripture was true and genuine or not; and third, whether the tradition of the creed which they pressed was the true tradition of the Apostles or not, and consequently whether the doctrine they defended concerning the one God and the one Son of God, Jesus Christ, was true or not.
