He only says that the Epistle to the Hebrews is placed outside the number by most, but he himself admits it. Vol. 3 [?], in the letter to Dardanus, p. 86. Likewise in the commentary on Galatians, ch. 1, p. 159. Athanasius, in the synopsis, translated by the most learned Musculus. See above, p. 35.

units.la: De epistola ad Hebr.
units.tr: On the Epistle to the Hebrews.

units.la: De hac epistola à multis fuit disputatum, sit ne Canonica, nec ne.
units.tr: Concerning this epistle, it has been disputed by many whether it is canonical or not.

units.la: Hieronymus ad Paulinum. Item in Catal. Ecclesiasticorum scriptorum, alij Clementi, alij Lucæ eam asscribunt.
units.tr: Jerome, to Paulinus. Likewise in the Catalogue of Ecclesiastical Writers, some ascribe it to Clement, others to Luke.

units.la: Tert. lib. de pudicitia p.766. ait fuisse Barnabæ, discipuli & comitis Apostoli Pauli.
units.tr: Tertullian, in the book On Modesty, p. 766, says that it is by Barnabas, the disciple and companion of the Apostle Paul.

units.la: Resp. Sed à pluribus & grauioribus pro epistola Pauli & Canonica fuit agnita.
units.tr: Reply: But it was acknowledged by many and weightier authorities as the epistle of Paul and as canonical.

units.la: 1. Clemens in Epistola ad Corinth. quæ pro indubitata est habita, sed quæ non extat, teste Eufeb. Cæsar. lib 3.c.37. vetus esse Apostoli scriptum in Ecclesia. Multos autem suspicatos, esse vel Clementis, vel Lucæ, propterea quod ex Hebr. in Græcam linguam conuerterit vel ille, vel iste, hominum iudicio.
units.tr: 1. Clement, in his Epistle to the Corinthians, which was held to be undoubted, but which is not extant, according to Eusebius of Caesarea, book 3, ch. 37, was an ancient writing of the Apostle in the Church. However, many suspected that it was by either Clement or Luke, because, in the judgment of men, one or the other translated it from Hebrew into the Greek language.

units.la: 2. Origenes idem sensit quod Clemens: Eufeb. teste lib.6.c.25.
units.tr: 2. Origen thought the same as Clement, according to the testimony of Eusebius, book 6, ch. 25.

units.la: 3. Clemens etiam Alexandrinus in ead. fuit sententia. Eufeb.lib.6.c.14. sed ait à Luca conuersam.
units.tr: 3. Clement of Alexandria also held the same opinion, Eusebius, book 6, ch. 14, but he said it was translated by Luke.

units.la: Hieronymus ad Gal.c.1.p.159. Item To.3. in Epistola ad Dardanum.p.68.
units.tr: Jerome, on Galatians, ch. 1, p. 159. Likewise Vol. 3, in the letter to Dardanus, p. 68.

units.la: 5. Concilium Laodicenum can.59.
units.tr: 5. The Council of Laodicea, Canon 59.

units.la: 6. Epiphanius lib. 2. T. contra Arioma-nitas hæres[?].69. pag.364. adducit ut Canoni-cam, & ait, Arianos eam negare.
units.tr: 6. Epiphanius, book 2, Vol., against the Arianites, heresy [?] 69, p. 364, adduces it as canonical, and says that the Arians deny it.

units.la: 7. Theodoretus in argumento in hanc epistolam: & refutat argumenta eorum, qui contendunt non esse Pauli.
units.tr: 7. Theodoret, in the argument on this epistle, refutes the arguments of those who contend that it is not Paul's.

units.la: 8. Chrysost,in hanc epistolā idem sensit.
units.tr: 8. Chrysostom also thought the same about this epistle.

units.la: 9. August.restatur apud Orientales sem-per fuisse habitam pro Epistola Pauli.
units.tr: 9. Augustine testifies that among the Easterners it was always held to be an Epistle of Paul.

units.la: Quidam hoc utuntur argumento 2. Pet.3.
units.tr: Some use this argument from 2 Peter 3.

units.la: Petrus ad fratres ex Iudaismo scribit de pa-tientia in afflictionibus: & ait de hac re et-iam Paulum ad eos scripsisse. Atqui non est alia epistola Pauli ad Hebr.nisi hæc, quæ et-iam est de eodem argumento patientiæ in ferenda cruce propter Christum.
units.tr: Peter writes to the brothers from Judaism about patience in afflictions, and says that Paul also wrote to them about this matter. Yet there is no other epistle of Paul to the Hebrews except this one, which is also on the same subject of patience in bearing the cross for Christ.

units.la: Alia argumenta non contemnenda vide in commentario Iohan. Pisc.in illam epistolam, ubi & Argumenta pro contraria parte refutantur.
units.tr: Other arguments, not to be despised, see in the commentary of John Piscator on that epistle, where the arguments for the opposite side are also refuted.

units.la: Obiectiones contra epistolam ad Hebr. non esse Apostoli.
units.tr: Objections against the epistle to the Hebrews not being by the Apostle.

units.la: I. Non præponit nomen suum: ergo non est Apostoli.
units.tr: I. It does not place its author's name at the head; therefore it is not by an Apostle.

units.la: Respondet Hieron.ergo nullius, quia nullius nomen præponitur. Sunt causæ, cur tacuerit honestè, quæ ab aliis citantur. Vid. Theodor.in epistolam hanc: Fallac. est non causæ,&c.
units.tr: Jerome replies: then it is by no one, since no one's name is placed at its head. There are reasons why he honorably kept silent, which are cited by others. See Theodore on this epistle: the fallacy is not the reason, etc.

units.la: II. Stylus elegantior solito stylo Pauli,
units.tr: II. The style is more elegant than the usual style of Paul,

units.la: Resp. Quasi verò idem homo nonnunquam non varium habeat stylum. Hebrai-cè scripsit, ideo elegantius. Vertit autem Clemens Romanus eleganter. Eufeb. lib. 3. cap.37.
units.tr: Reply: As if the same man does not sometimes have a varied style! He wrote in Hebrew, therefore more elegantly. Clement of Rome, moreover, translated it elegantly. Eusebius, book 3, ch. 37.

units.la: III. Fauet Nouato in c.6.& 10.
units.tr: III. It favors Novatian in chapters 6 and 10.

units.la: Refp. Fallac. ex ignoratione figurae di-ctionis.
units.tr: Reply: A fallacy arising from ignorance of the figure of speech.

units.la: IV. Torquet scripturas, vt illud. 2.Sam. 7.verf.14. Ego ero illi in Patrem, torquet. ad Christum.
units.tr: IV. It twists the Scriptures, as in that passage of 2 Samuel 7:14, "I will be his Father," which it twists to Christ.

units.la: Refpond. Non torquet. Proprie enim de Christo intelligitur: non de Salomone. 1. promittitur filius post mortem ipsi Dauid. 2. promittit regnum æternum huic filio. Vid. Auguft.de Ciuitate Dei, lib.18. cap.10. Ambrosium in Lucam,l.3.de genealogia Christi.
units.tr: Reply: It does not twist them. For it is properly understood of Christ, not of Solomon. 1. A son is promised after David's own death. 2. An eternal kingdom is promised to this son. See Augustine, On the City of God, book 18, ch. 10, and Ambrose on Luke, book 3, on the genealogy of Christ.

units.la: Instant. At ibi 2.Sam.7. ait Deus de hoc filio. Cùm peccauerit,&c. Christus autem non peccauit.
units.tr: Objection: But there, in 2 Samuel 7, God speaks of this son: "When he commits iniquity," etc. But Christ did not sin.

units.la: Refp. Christus in sua persona non peccauit, sed primo peccata nostra in fe recepit, Ief.53. Secundo peccare dicitur in membris, ideo in eis etiam punitur.
units.tr: Reply: Christ in his own person did not sin, but firstly he received our sins in himself, Isaiah 53. Secondly, he is said to sin in his members, and therefore is also punished in them.

units.la: V. Heb.2.v.3. ait, Si tantam neglexerimus salutem, quæ ab iis, qui audierunt, fuit in nos confirmata. Paulus autem ab hominibus non accepit, Gal.1.
units.tr: V. Hebrews 2:3 says, "If we neglect so great a salvation, which was confirmed to us by those who heard it." But Paul did not receive it from men, Galatians 1.

units.la: Refp. 1. Non ait, Ad me allata, sed ad nos. Ponit se in locum aliorum. 2. Si de fe loquitur, non ait allata, sed confirmata. Hoc indicat Gal.2. Sed tertiò, non ait doctrina, verum salus confirmata. Liquet Actor.9. per Ananiam confirmatus fuit : instructione & Baptismo.
units.tr: Reply: 1. It does not say "brought to me" but "to us." He places himself in the place of others. 2. If it speaks of faith, it does not say "brought," but "confirmed." This is shown in Galatians 2. But thirdly, it does not say "doctrine," but "salvation was confirmed." It is clear from Acts 9 that he was confirmed through Ananias, by instruction and Baptism.

units.la: VI. Heb.9. ait, in Arca fuisse vrnam auream, Manna, virgam Aaronis. Scriptura tamen 1.Reg.8. ait non fuisse in Arca, nisi duas tabulas Testamenti.
units.tr: VI. Hebrews 9 says that in the Ark there was a golden urn, the manna, and Aaron's rod. Yet Scripture, 1 Kings 8, says that there was nothing in the Ark except the two tablets of the Covenant.

units.la: Resp.1. Tunc 1.Reg.8.non erant intus nisi duæ tabulæ : sed tempore Mosis erat etiam vrna, &c. Et de hoc tempore loquitur Apostolus.2.Erant circa Arcam, perinde ac si intus essent.Sic autem loquitur Apostolus. Vi-de Martyrem in 1. Melachim cap.8.vers.9.
units.tr: Reply: 1. At the time of 1 Kings 8 there were only the two tablets inside; but at the time of Moses there was also the urn, etc. And the Apostle speaks of this time. 2. They were around the Ark, just as if they were inside. Thus the Apostle speaks. See Martyr on 1 Kings, ch. 8, verse 9.

units.la: VII. Cap.12. Exemplo Esau videtur negare Respiscentibus veniam.
units.tr: VII. Chapter 12. By the example of Esau it seems to deny pardon to those who repent.

units.la: Resp. Minime : sed exemplo Esau terret, ne inebrientur delitiis Mundi. Deinde nomine pœnitentiæ Esau non intellexit respi-scentiam, sed terrorem, quo impij percel-luntur, sero cùm sapiunt Phryges.
units.tr: Reply: Not at all: by the example of Esau it terrifies, lest they be intoxicated by the pleasures of the world. Moreover, by the name of repentance Esau did not understand a turning back, but the terror by which the impious are struck, too late when they grow wise, like the Phrygians.

units.la: De EPISTOLA IACOBI.
units.tr: On the Epistle of James.

units.la: Iacobus iste, non fuit filius Zebedæi, fra-ter Iohannis: is enim ab Herode fuerat in-terfectus Hierosolymis. Act.12. Patres:suis-se discipulum & consanguineum Christi, cognomine Obliam, qui Ecclesiæ Hierofo-lymitanæ præfuerit.
units.tr: This James was not the son of Zebedee, the brother of John, for he had been put to death by Herod at Jerusalem (Acts 12). The Fathers say that he was a disciple and kinsman of Christ, surnamed Oblias, who presided over the church of Jerusalem.

units.la: Alij:filium fuisse Alphæi, eoque Apostolum, de quo Matth.10. Act.1. Huic frater Iu-das, Matth.13 55.De hoc Iacobo Act.15.
units.tr: Others say he was the son of Alphaeus, and therefore an apostle (Matt. 10; Acts 1). His brother was Jude (Matt. 13:55). Concerning this James see Acts 15.

units.la: Hieronymus probat in prolog.Biblior.ad Paulinum.
units.tr: Jerome proves this in the prologue to the Bible addressed to Paulinus.

units.la: Item de viris Illustribus seu scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis. Laodicenum Concilium. Ruffinus in Symb. Eusebius lib.2,c.23. ait, in plurimis Ecclesiis legi publicè.
units.tr: Likewise in his book On Illustrious Men, or Ecclesiastical Writers. The Council of Laodicea. Rufinus in his commentary on the Creed. Eusebius (Book 2, chapter 23) says that it was read publicly in most churches.

units.la: Anacletus primus, qui fuit tertius Pontifex Romanus in prima Decretal. citat dictū ex hac epistola, & ait: sicut dicit beatus Iacobus Apostolus. Sed fallitur. Ita Alexander primus in prima Decretali.
units.tr: Anacletus, the first, who was the third Roman pontiff, in the first Decretal quotes words from this epistle and says: "as the blessed apostle James says." But he is mistaken. So too Alexander the first, in his first Decretal.

units.la: Contra Epistolam Iacobi Ob- iecta.
units.tr: Objections Against the Epistle of James.

units.la: I. Doctrinam de iustificatione habet pugnantem cum doctrina Apostolica.
units.tr: I. It has a doctrine of justification that conflicts with the apostolic doctrine.

units.la: Resp. Optime conuenit, si rectè intelligatur. Paulus de iustificatione coram Deo: Iacobus de iustificatione etiam coram hominibus. Illa, fide: haec operibus comparatur.
units.tr: Reply: It agrees very well, if it is rightly understood. Paul speaks of justification before God; James speaks of justification also before men. The former is set against faith, the latter against works.

units.la: Ar ait cap. 2. ad calcem: Sicut corpus Spiritu (id est, anima) mortuum est: ita fides sine operibus mortua est. Vt igitur anima est causa vitae corpori: ita facit opera causam vitae, fidei. Annon haec pugnant.
units.tr: Ar says in chapter 2, at the end: "As the body without the spirit (that is, the soul) is dead, so faith without works is dead." Therefore, as the soul is the cause of life for the body, so works make faith live. Do not these things conflict?

units.la: Resp. Homonymia est in vocabulo Spiritus, Spiritus enim accipitur hic pro Spiritu, quo per os spiramus. Vt hic non est causa vitae, sed πνευματικόν[?]: ita opera bona.
units.tr: Reply: There is an ambiguity in the word "spirit": here "spirit" is taken for the breath by which we breathe through the mouth. As that breath is not the cause of life but [spiritual], so good works are not the cause of faith.

units.la: II. Item ait: Qui offenderit in uno, factus est omnium reus?
units.tr: II. Likewise he says: "Whoever offends in one point has become guilty of all"?

units.la: Resp. Non respectu materiae, sed formae, hoc dictum intelligendum est. Haec est offensio in DEUM, ideo dixit,offendit. Item subdit: Qui enim dixit: Non moechaberis, &c. quasi dicat, sicut in eo, quod peccasti non curasti legislatorem: sic nec in alio pec-cato curasses, si occasio peccandi oblata fuisset. Ideo quoad offensam in Deum,Qui offendit in uno,factus est reus omnium.
units.tr: Reply: This saying is to be understood not with respect to the matter but to the form. This is an offence against God, and therefore he said "offends." Next he adds: "For he who said, 'You shall not commit adultery,' etc." As if to say: just as you did not care about the lawgiver in the sin you committed, so you would not have cared in another sin, if the opportunity to sin had been offered. Therefore, as regards the offence against God, "whoever offends in one point has become guilty of all."

units.la: III. Statuit Chrisma seu extremam un-ctionem papisticam cap. 5.[?]
units.tr: III. He establishes the Papistical chrism or extreme unction in chapter 5?

units.la: Resp. Minimè:sed alludit ad unctionem, qua Apostoli ex mandato Domini ungebant ægrotos,&curabantur.Donum erat miracu-lorum,de qua re Marc 6.v.13.
units.tr: Reply: Not at all; he alludes to the anointing by which the apostles, on the Lord's command, anointed the sick and they were healed. It was a gift of miracles, concerning which see Mark 6:13.

units.la: At attribuit huic non solum sanitatem corporis,sed etiam Animæ v.15.[?]
units.tr: But he attributes to this not only bodily health but also that of the soul (v. 15)?

units.la: Resp. Imò fidei attribuit,hoc est,fideli orationi utrunque. Oleum symbolum tum erat,nec pro alia re agnoscit Iacobus. Con-firmatur. Nam mox alia exempla adfert effi-cacitatis orationis fidelis.
units.tr: Reply: Rather, he attributes both to faith, that is, to the prayer of faith. The oil was then a sign, and James recognizes it for no other purpose. This is confirmed, for he immediately brings forward other examples of the efficacy of the prayer of faith.

units.la: IV. Non utitur salutatione Apostolica, Gratia vobis,sed profana, Salutem.
units.tr: IV. He does not use the apostolic greeting, "Grace to you," but a profane one, "Greetings."

units.la: Resp. Etiam Apostoli Act.15. sic salutant fratres inter Gentes. Iohannes autem in sua prima epistola nulla utitur salutatione.
units.tr: Reply: The apostles too in Acts 15 greet the brothers among the Gentiles in this way. But John, in his first epistle, uses no greeting at all.

units.la: V. Eusebius ait esse adulterinam l.2. c.23.[?]
units.tr: V. Eusebius says it is spurious (Book 2, chapter 23)?

units.la: Resp. Ait tamen legi publicè in Ecclesiis: Non omnes igitur habebant illam pro ad-ulterina.
units.tr: Reply: He says, however, that it was read publicly in the churches. Therefore not all held it to be spurious.

units.la: VI. Non facit officium Apostoli. Non enim meminit passionis,resurrectionis,&c. Christi,&eius officij.
units.tr: VI. It does not fulfil the office of an apostle. For it makes no mention of the passion, resurrection, etc. of Christ, and of his office.

units.la: Resp.Quasi vero debeat singuli de iisdem scribere. Neqj Matthaeus & alij disseruerunt de Christi Deitate ,ut Iohannes. Scribebat Iacobus de moribus & vita Christiana.
units.tr: Reply: As if each one ought to write about the same things! Nor did Matthew and the others discourse on the deity of Christ as John did. James wrote about morals and the Christian life.

units.la: VII. Ex Petri & Pauli Epistolis recitat aliquot dicta,ut, charitas operit multitudinem peccatorum, est Petri. Item, Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei. Item Gal 5. Spiritus concupiscit aduersus carnem.
units.tr: VII. He quotes several sayings from the epistles of Peter and Paul, such as "charity covers a multitude of sins," which is from Peter; likewise "Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God"; likewise Gal. 5: "The Spirit lusts against the flesh."

units.la: Resp. Quid mirum:Deinde cur non idem reuelare potuit Spiritus S. Iacobo, ut & illis duobus.
units.tr: Reply: What is strange about that? Furthermore, why could the Holy Spirit not have revealed the same things to James as to those two?

units.la: DE 2. PETRI EPISTOLA.
units.tr: DE 2. PETRI EPISTOLA.

units.la: Est Petri. Ait enim se fuisse vnum ex iis, qui in monte sancto vidit gloriam Christi. Si non est Petrus iste. Ergo magnus nebulo, & impudens qui haec falso scribat.
units.tr: It is Peter's. For he says that he was one of those who on the holy mountain saw the glory of Christ. If this is not Peter, then he is a great rascal and a shameless man who writes these things falsely.

units.la: DE 1. ET 3. IOANNIS.
units.tr: Concerning 1 and 3 John.

units.la: Sunt Ioannis. Irenaeus citat dictum ex 2. Epistola: Et ait, Ioannem Apostolum hoc scripsisse in epistola sua 2. Hieronymus T.2. ad Euagrium pag.329.
units.tr: They are by John. Irenaeus quotes a saying from the second Epistle, and says that the Apostle John wrote this in his epistle. Jerome, vol. 2, to Evagrius, p. 329.

units.la: Obiecta.
units.tr: Objections.

units.la: At vocatur Presbyter,non Apostolus.
units.tr: But he is called an elder, not an apostle.

units.la: Resp. Quasi vero non etiam Petrus in 1. epistola non se vocet compresbyterum. c. 5. v.1. Sic autem se vocabant Apostoli, quando in aliqua Ecclesia residebant.
units.tr: Answer: As if Peter did not also call himself a fellow-elder in his first epistle, 1 Pet. 5:1. The apostles also called themselves this when they were residing in some church.

units.la: DE IVDAE EPISTOLA.
units.tr: ON THE EPISTLE OF JUDE.

units.la: Est.Hieron.in prolog.ad Paulinum.Idem ad Marcellam sub nomine Paulæ & Eusto-chij, p.125. In Epistola, inquit Canonica Iudas Apostoli frater Iacobi, scribit, dicens: Commonere autem vos volo, &c. Idem T.1.de Ecclesiasticis scriptoribus ait, propter testimonium ex libro Apocrypho Enoch reiectum esse à multis, sed vsu & vetustate, autoritatem obtinuisse.
units.tr: Jerome, in the prologue to the letter to Paulinus; the same author, in the letter to Marcella under the name of Paula and Eustochium, p. 125: "In the canonical Epistle, he says, Jude, the apostle, brother of James, writes, saying: 'I want to remind you,' etc." The same Jerome, in his book On Ecclesiastical Writers, says that because of its testimony from the apocryphal book of Enoch it was rejected by many, but through use and antiquity it gained authority.

units.la: Nota Iacobi Apostoli duo. Primus frater Iohannis Zebedæi filius, hic gladio cæditur Act.12. secundus Alphæi filij, de quo Mat.10. Huic fuit frater Iudas: ambo fratres, id est, consanguinei Christi. Matth.13.v.55. De hoc etiam Ioh.14.v.22.
units.tr: Note that there are two apostles named James. The first is the brother of John, son of Zebedee; he was put to death by the sword, Acts 12. The second is the son of Alphaeus, of whom Matthew 10. Jude was the brother of this one; both were brothers, that is, cousins of Christ, Matthew 13:55. Of him also John 14:22.

units.la: Hunc volunt multi, vt Beza quoq;,esse autorem Epistolæ huius. Inter Apostolos autem Matth.10. non connumeratur. De hoc etiam Act.1.v.13. Quanquam Pareus vult sub nomine Taddæi vel Lebæi intelligi.
units.tr: Many, Beza among them, hold that this man is the author of this epistle. But he is not counted among the apostles in Matthew 10. Of him also Acts 1:13. Although Pareus wants him to be understood under the name Thaddaeus or Lebbaeus.

units.la: I. Allegat prophetiâ Enochi Apocrypham.
units.tr: I. He cites the prophecy of the apocryphal Enoch.

units.la: Respondet 1. Caluinus Ἀγάφον[?] potius fuit memorabile dictum propagatum & vulgatū inter Iudæos, quam ex libro desumtum. 2. Etiamsi ex apocrypho libro: dictum tamen hoc probando authenticum fecit: sicut & dicta Poëtarum Apostolus Paulus.
units.tr: Reply: 1. Calvin answers that the saying was rather a memorable remark spread and made common among the Jews, not taken from the book. 2. Even if it came from the apocryphal book, Paul the Apostol nonetheless made this saying authoritative by approving it, just as he did with the sayings of the poets.

units.la: II. Adhibet historiam apocryphā de certamine Michaelis cum Sathana pro corpore Mosis.
units.tr: II. He adduces the apocryphal story of the contest between Michael and Satan over the body of Moses.

units.la: Resp. Etsi in scriptura historia hæc nō habetur: non sequitur tamen esse falsam aut incertam. Multa enim habuerunt Iudæi per traditionem, eaq; vera. Certè quod narrat nihil pugnat cum scripturis, aut absurdi in se cōtinet; sed valde verisimile est. Sathan enim semper quærit Sanctorū corpora producere ad idololatriam & superstitionem: Angeli autem Dei resistunt.
units.tr: Reply: Although this story is not found in Scripture, it does not follow that it is false or uncertain. The Jews had many things by tradition, and these were true. Certainly what it relates conflicts with nothing in the Scriptures, nor does it contain anything absurd in itself; rather it is very probable. For Satan always seeks to bring forth the bodies of the saints for idolatry and superstition, but the angels of God resist him.

units.la: III. Item, est consarcinata epistola ex 2. Petri. Non ergo inspirata. Item, ergo discipulus fuit Apostolorum.
units.tr: III. Likewise, the epistle is patched together from 2 Peter. It is therefore not inspired. Likewise, then, he was a disciple of the apostles.

units.la: Resp. Fallacia est non causæ vt causæ. Non est legitima causa, & sufficiens, qua probes non fuisse inspiratam à Deo. Etiam Prophetæ acceperunt à Mose: & Apostoli à Prophetis: sed omnes inspirati à Deo ad hæc dicta sumenda,{1}
units.tr: Reply: This is a fallacy of mistaking a non-cause for a cause. It is not a legitimate and sufficient reason by which you could prove that it was not inspired by God. The prophets also received from Moses, and the apostles from the prophets; but all were inspired by God to take up these sayings.

units.la: Deinde à parte aliqua ad totam Epistolam, non valet consequentia.
units.tr: Then, from some part to the whole epistle, the inference does not hold.

units.la: Fuisse etiam Discipulum Apostolorum, nō hinc euincitur. Deinde quid tum? Non enim contendimus fuisse Apostolum: sed discipulum Christi, fratrem illius Iacobi, cuius est prima Catholica. Act.15.v.32. legimus, Iudam & Silam fuisse Prophetas.
units.tr: That he was also a disciple of the apostles is not proved by this. Moreover, so what? For we do not contend that he was an apostle, but a disciple of Christ, the brother of that James to whom the first catholic epistle belongs. In Acts 15:32 we read that Judas and Silas were prophets.

units.la: III. Iudas Apostolus venit non in Græciam, sed in Persidem: Non igitur Græcè, sed persicè scripsit.
units.tr: III. The apostle Jude came not into Greece but into Persia. Therefore he wrote not in Greek but in Persian.

units.la: Resp. 1. Iudam Apostolum non lego, nisi Iscariotem: sed Prophetam lego Act.15. v.32. 2. Potuit verti è Persica in Græcam.
units.tr: Reply: 1. I read of no apostle Jude except Iscariot; but I read of a prophet in Acts 15:32. 2. It could have been translated from Persian into Greek.

units.la: DE APOCALYPSI.
units.tr: ON THE APOCALYPSE.

units.la: Est Iohannis. Testes. Iustinus Martyr. Irenæus: Apollonius: Theophyl. Eusebii. Eufeb.lib.3.ca. 25. Item l.4.ca.18. verba Justini ex Dialogo citat. Item, de Irenæo, lib.5.c.8. Item, de Appol-lonio lib 5.cap.18. Item de Theophil.lib.4.c. 24. Idem Euseb. scribit suaætate non fuisse dubitatum : sedante à nonnullis. Origenes in Psal.1. teste etiam Eusebio lib.6.c. 25. Hieronymus in prologo.
units.tr: It is by John. Witnesses: Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, Apollonius, Theophilus; Eusebius. Eusebius, book 3, chapter 25; also book 4, chapter 18, where he cites the words of Justin from the Dialogue. Likewise, concerning Irenaeus, book 5, chapter 8; likewise, concerning Apollonius, book 5, chapter 18; likewise, concerning Theophilus, book 4, chapter 24. The same Eusebius writes that in his time it was not doubted, though by some it was. Origen on Psalm 1, also witnessed by Eusebius, book 6, chapter 25. Jerome in the prologue.

units.la: Obiectiones contra Apocaly-psin.
units.tr: Objections against the Apocalypse.

units.la: 1. Ab autoritate antiquorum Patrum, qui non agnouerunt pro Johannis Apostoli li-bro : horum nomina vide in prolegomenis Bezæ in Apocalyp.
units.tr: 1. From the authority of the ancient Fathers, who did not acknowledge this book as the book of the apostle John. Their names see in Beza's prolegomena to the Apocalypse.

units.la: Resp. 1. Alii plures & antiquiores Patres probarunt, & commentariis illustrarunt. 2. Rationes, quibus permoti illi reiecerunt librum, nullæ sunt.
units.tr: Reply: 1. Many other and more ancient Fathers approved it and illustrated it with commentaries. 2. The reasons by which those men were moved to reject the book are none.

units.la: II. Non habet grauitatem Apostolicam.
units.tr: II. It lacks apostolic weight.

units.la: Resp. Est falsum vt liquet: plenus est sententiis Prophetarum : & res futuras prædicit.
units.tr: Reply: This is false, as is clear: it is full of the sayings of the prophets, and it foretells future events.

units.la: III. Inculcat suum nomen propter Apostoli consuetudinem in Euangelio.
units.tr: III. It inculcates its own name, on account of the apostle's custom in the Gospel.

units.la: Resp. Aliud est scribere historiam, aliud Prophetiam. Ibi non est opus nominis autoris inculcatione, quia autoritas historiæ non pendet ab authore, sed à rebus. In prophetia scribenda est opus: Sic Jeremias suum inculcat: sic Daniel, vt sciatur, per quos & quo ordine futura hæc prædicantur. 2. O-ctics[?] tantum, nisi fallor, repetitur.
units.tr: Reply: Writing history is one thing, writing prophecy another. There it is not necessary to inculcate the author's name, because the authority of a history does not depend on the author but on the facts. In writing prophecy it is necessary: thus Jeremiah inculcates his name; thus Daniel, so that it may be known through whom and in what order these things are foretold. 2. Only the eighth [?] is repeated, unless I am mistaken.

units.la: IV. In Græcis exemplaribus est Iohannis Theologi.
units.tr: IV. In the Greek copies it is "of John the Theologian."

units.la: Resp. Atq; hic est titulus Iohannis Euangelistæ. κατ' ἐξοχὴν [?] enim sic vocatus est, quia nemo diuinius disseruit de Deitate Christi.
units.tr: Reply: And this is the title of John the Evangelist. For he was called so by preeminence, because no one spoke more divinely about the Deity of Christ.

units.la: V. Stylus diuersus à Stylo Euangelistæ & & Epistolarum.
units.tr: V. The style is different from the style of the Evangelist and of the Epistles.

units.la: Resp. Hoc postulabat argumen tum ab-illis diuersum. 2. Hic simpliciter dictata à Christo scripsit. Item verba Prophetarum, pura, dictata etiam à Christo, adiecit, nihil mutans.
units.tr: Reply: This argument demanded a different style. 2. Here he simply wrote what was dictated by Christ. Likewise, he added the words of the prophets, pure, also dictated by Christ, changing nothing.

units.la: VI. Fauere videtur Chiliastis.
units.tr: VI. It seems to favor the Chiliasts.

units.la: Resp. Fallacia est ex ignoratione figuræ dictionis.
units.tr: Reply: It is a fallacy arising from ignorance of the figure of speech.

units.la: SEQVVNTVR REGVLÆ QVÆDAM GENERALES, AD DE-monstrandam tum autoritatem & perfectionem sacrarum Literarum, tum etiam veram earum intelligentiam, unde ea sit petenda, & quaraitone acquirenda: ad diluenda Adversariorum, inprimis verò Pontificiorum argumenta, apprime utiles & necessa-ria.
units.tr: THE FOLLOWING ARE CERTAIN GENERAL RULES, USEFUL AND NECESSARY ABOVE ALL FOR DEMONSTRATING BOTH THE AUTHORITY AND PERFECTION OF THE HOLY LETTERS, AND ALSO THEIR TRUE UNDERSTANDING: WHENCE IT IS TO BE SOUGHT, AND BY WHAT MEANS IT IS TO BE ACQUIRED; AND FOR REFUTING THE ARGUMENTS OF THE ADVERSARIES, ESPECIALLY THE PAPISTS.

units.la: Tres sunt gradus librorum, qui in volumine Biblico continentur. Primus continet eos, de quibus nunquam in Ecclesia à piis doctisque & in scripturis exercitatis hominibus dubitatum fuit, quin essent θεόπνευστοι [?]. Hi sunt etiam indubitatæ autho-ritatis.
units.tr: There are three grades of the books contained in the biblical volume. The first contains those about which it was never doubted in the Church by pious and learned men, practised in the Scriptures, that they were θεόπνευστοι [?] [God-breathed]. These are also of indubitable authority.

units.la: Secundus continet eos, de quibus, non ab omnibus, neque semper, sed à multis & & aliquando dubitatum fuit. Et horum qui-dam sunt, 1. de quorum dignitate, eoque de primario autore Spiritu sancto non ita du-bitatum: sed tantùm de secundariis, seu de scriptoribus, vt est Epistola ad Hebraeos. Item Epistola Petri altera: Duae Iohannis, & Apocalypsis. Quanquam etiam, de aliis ho-rum minùs, de aliis magis dubitatum fuit. Nam de autore Epistolae alterius Petri, & de autore Apocalyp. minùs dubitatum fuit, quàm de secunda Iohannis. 2. Alij sunt de quorum non solùm autoribus, sed etiam di-gnitate, primarioque autore dubitatum fuit ad tempus, vt Epistola Iacobi & Iudae: Sed tamen non ita multò post, & ipsi fuerunt a-gniti esse à Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: The second contains those about which doubt was raised, not by all, nor always, but by many and at times. Some of these are: (1) those whose dignity, and therefore whose primary author, the Holy Spirit, was not so much doubted, but only their secondary authors, or writers; such is the Epistle to the Hebrews, likewise the second Epistle of Peter, the two Epistles of John, and the Apocalypse. Although, of these too, some were doubted less and some more: for doubt about the author of the second Epistle of Peter and about the author of the Apocalypse was less than about the second Epistle of John. (2) Others are those about which doubt was raised for a time, not only concerning their authors but also concerning their dignity and primary author, such as the Epistle of James and of Jude; but yet not long after, they too were acknowledged to be from the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Tertius continet eos, quos vetus Ecclesia, eoq; purior, semper pro adulterinis & Apo-cryphis habuit.
units.tr: The third contains those which the ancient Church, and the purer for that, always held to be spurious and Apocryphal.

units.la: Distinctio hæc certa est, & ex Patribus sumta.
units.tr: This distinction is certain, and is taken from the Fathers.

units.la: Exempla primi ordinis in veteri Testa-mento, vide apud Euseb. lib. 3. cap. 10. ex Io-sepho.
units.tr: Examples of the first order in the Old Testament, see in Eusebius, book 3, chapter 10, drawn from Josephus.

units.la: In nouo Testamento, Euseb. lib. 3. c. 25. Et hæc quidem scripta, pro indubitatis habentur, inquit Eusebius.
units.tr: In the New Testament, Eusebius, book 3, chapter 25. "These writings, indeed, are held as indubitable," says Eusebius.

units.la: Exempli secundi generis, in veteri Testamento, nullus est. In nouo Eusebius lib. 3. cap. 25.
units.tr: There is no example of the second kind in the Old Testament. In the New, Eusebius, book 3, chapter 25.

units.la: Quibus verò contradicitur, tametsi multis sint cognita, sunt hæc: Epistola Iacobi, Iudæ, & secunda Petri, secunda item & tertia Iohannis. De Apocalypsi subdit: Hanc nonnulli reprobant: alij verò certis & indubitatis scripturis adiudicant. Hæc sunt (inquit) quibus contradicitur. Verùm non ait Eusebius, ab omnibus: imò ait, multis esse cognita.
units.tr: Those which are contradicted, although they are known to many, are these: the Epistle of James, of Jude, and the second of Peter, likewise the second and third of John. Concerning the Apocalypse he adds: "Some reject this; others, however, ascribe it to certain and indubitable Scriptures." These, he says, are the ones which are contradicted. But Eusebius does not say "by all"; rather he says they are known to many.

units.la: Isti igitur multi, quibus cognita sunt, præferendi sunt illis, qui tantùm dubitabant: sicut præferenda scientia dubitationi.
units.tr: Those many, therefore, to whom they are known, are to be preferred to those who only doubted; just as knowledge is to be preferred to doubt.

units.la: Horum enim dubitatio, non tollit aliorum scientiam. Nam neq; simpliciter illi negarunt, sed tantùm dubitarunt. Verè igitur dici potest, hos libros secundi ordinis, ab Ecclesia fuisse agnitos pro Canonicis: quia à paucis de eorum dignitate fuit dubitatum.
units.tr: For the doubt of these does not destroy the knowledge of others. For neither did they simply deny them, but only doubted. It can therefore truly be said that these books of the second order were acknowledged by the Church as canonical, because by few was their dignity doubted.

units.la: II. Reg. Scriptura sacra Canonica, perfectus est canon fidei, operū & Ceremoniarum in religione, omniumque ad salutem necessariorum, ad quem omnia debent examinari. Ergo extra scripturam nihil tanquam vel creditu, vel obseruatu in religione necessarium, admittere debet Ecclesia Dei: Et contrà nihil omittere eorum, quæ in scripturis vel credenda, vel obseruanda traduntur, nisi per Christum abolita sint. Proinde, quæ vel vtrumq; vel altervtrum facit, Ecclesia Christi ea in re non est.
units.tr: II. Reg. Holy Scripture, being canonical, is the perfect canon of faith, of works and of ceremonies in religion, and of all things necessary to salvation, by which all things ought to be examined. Therefore the Church of God ought to admit nothing outside Scripture as necessary to be believed or observed in religion; and, on the contrary, to omit nothing of those things which are handed down in the Scriptures to be believed or observed, unless they have been abolished through Christ. Accordingly, whoever does either of these, or one of the two, is not in that matter the Church of Christ.

units.la: Deut 4. Non addetis ad verbum, nec minuetis ex eo. Idem cap.5.&12.Si nihil addendum:Ergo perfecta. Si nihil adimendum. Ergo nihil habet superuacaneum.
units.tr: Deut. 4. "You shall not add to the word, nor take away from it." The same, chapters 5 and 12. If nothing is to be added, then it is perfect; if nothing is to be taken away, then it contains nothing superfluous.

units.la: Psal.1. Beatus qui in lege Domini meditatur die & nocte: Et erit sicut arbor plantata secus riuos aquarum, quae fructum suum dat in tempore, & folium eius non decidit, & omne quod facit, prospere cadet. Lex igitur Domini facit ad beatitudinem consequendam.
units.tr: Ps. 1. "Blessed is the man who meditates in the law of the Lord day and night; and he shall be like a tree planted by the streams of waters, which gives its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not fall, and whatever he does shall prosper." The law of the Lord therefore serves to attain blessedness.

units.la: Prouerb.30. Omnis sermo Dei purgatus est, scutum iis, qui eo niituntur. Ne addas sermonibus eius, ne te redarguat, & mendax inueniaris. Is igitur sufficit aduersus omnes hostes, proinde ad salutem.
units.tr: Prov. 30. "Every word of God is purified; he is a shield to those who trust in it. Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar." It therefore suffices against all enemies, and so for salvation.

units.la: Ezech.10.[?] Dedi eis Statuta mea, atque judicia mea indicaui eis, in quibus homo, si ea fecerit, viuet. Item: In praeceptis Patrum vestrorum nolite incedere, &c. In praeceptis meis ambulate.
units.tr: Ezek. 20. [?] "I gave them my statutes, and showed them my judgments, by which a man, if he does them, shall live." Likewise: "Do not walk in the ordinances of your fathers, etc." "Walk in my ordinances."

units.la: Matth.22. Erratis nescientes scripturas. Primum igitur causa omnium errorum in religione, est ignorantia scripturarum. Secundo, qui igitur tenent scripturas, errare non possunt, quatenus eas sequuntur.
units.tr: Matt. 22. "You err, not knowing the Scriptures." Therefore the first cause of all errors in religion is ignorance of the Scriptures. Second, those who hold to the Scriptures cannot err, insofar as they follow them.

units.la: 2. Tim.3. Literas S. didicisti, quae possunt te sapientem reddere ad salutem. Sufficiunt igitur ad salutem.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3. "You have learned the holy letters, which can make you wise unto salvation." They therefore suffice for salvation.

units.la: Item, omnis scriptura diuinitus inspirata, utilis est ad docendum, &c. Sunt enim quatuor necessaria in doctrina Ecclesiastica. 1,ut doceamus vera: 2. ut refellamus falsa. 3. ut instituamus ad virtutes, & vitam Christianam. 4. vt arguamus vitia, & malam vitam. Ad hæc (sufficit sacra Scriptura. Sufficit igitur ad salutem.
units.tr: Likewise, "All Scripture is divinely inspired and profitable for teaching," etc. For there are four things necessary in ecclesiastical teaching: (1) that we teach the truth; (2) that we refute falsehoods; (3) that we instruct in virtues and the Christian life; (4) that we rebuke vices and a wicked life. Holy Scripture suffices for these. Therefore it suffices for salvation.

units.la: 1. Tim.1. Denuncies μὴ ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν[?].
units.tr: 1 Tim. 1. Charge them not to teach other doctrine [μὴ ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν].

units.la: 1. Iohan.1. Quod audiuimus, quod vidi-mus oculis nostris, quod spectauimus, & manus nostræ contrectarunt de sermone vitæ: hæc annunciamus vobis, vt & vos communionem habeatis nobiscum, & communio nostra sit cum Patre, & cum Filio eius Iesu Christo. Scripta igitur Apostolorum sufficiunt nobis ad habendum cum illis communionem, & perfectum capiendum gaudium, id est, vitam æternam.
units.tr: 1 John 1. That which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, concerning the word of life: this we declare to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship may be with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ. The writings of the Apostles therefore suffice for us to have fellowship with them, and to possess the full joy, that is, eternal life.

units.la: 1.Cor.11.In hoc (quòd scilicet conveniatis non in melius, sed in deteriùs) non laudo vos: quasi dicat, laudo quidé vos in eo, quòd retinetis instituta mea (vt est in principio cap.11.) sed in iis, (de quibus iam dixi) non laudo vos. Quare? Quoniam ego accepi à Domino, quod & tradidi vobis: quasi dicat, quoniam hoc non tradidi vobis, neq; etiam accepi à Domino.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11. In this (namely that you come together not for the better but for the worse) I do not praise you: as if he were saying, I do indeed praise you in this, that you keep my ordinances (as is said at the beginning of chapter 11), but in those matters of which I have already spoken I do not praise you. Why? Because I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you: as if he were saying, because I did not deliver this to you, nor did I receive it from the Lord.

units.la: 1.Cor.15. Tradidi vobis inprimis quod & accepi.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15. I delivered to you first of all what I also received.

units.la: Gal.1. Licet nos aut Angelus Euangeliza-verit vobis præterquam quod Euangeliza-tum est, anathema sit.
units.tr: Gal. 1. Even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you anything other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed.

units.la: Ioh.15.[?] Si feceritis quod mando, non dicam vos seruos, sed amicos. Si quis igitur ea tanùm[?] doceat facienda, & ipse etiam curet ea facere, amicus est Christi.
units.tr: John 15. If you do what I command, I will not call you servants but friends. Whoever therefore teaches only those things to be done, and himself also takes care to do them, is a friend of Christ.

units.la: Apoc. 22. Si quis adiecerit ad hæc, adii-ciet illi Dominus plagas multas.
units.tr: Rev. 22. If anyone adds to these things, the Lord will add to him the many plagues.

units.la: Contra hoc mandatum sæpius in sacris Literis inculcatum, fecerunt Iudæi cum aliâs, tum cùm introduxerunt, & à Romanis confirmari curarunt, ut unus facinorolo dimitteretur in Paschate. In quem finem? ut esset testimonium & memoria, se etiam pec-catores, liberatos fuisse ex Ægypto. Quasi verò Deus non satis prudenter instituerit, quibus rebus deberent memoriam suæ libe-rationis excitare, esu scilicet agni Paschatis, & aliis quæ in festo Paschæ ex instituto Domini fiebant. Fuit autem hæc traditio, & consuetudo contra mandatum Dei in eo et-iam, quia Dominus nolebat, ut cuiquam facinoroso parceretur. Deut.19. Exod.13. Pro-verb.17. Qui impium absoluit, & qui conde-mnat iustum, uterque abominatio est coram Domino.
units.tr: Against this command, which is repeated more often in the Holy Scriptures, the Jews acted, both in other ways and when they introduced, and took care to have confirmed by the Romans, that one criminal be released at Passover. For what purpose? That it might be a testimony and a memorial that they too, as sinners, had been freed from Egypt. As if God had not prudently enough appointed by what means they should awaken the memory of their liberation, namely by eating the Passover lamb and the other things that were done at the Passover feast by the Lord's ordinance. This tradition and custom was, moreover, contrary to God's command also in this respect, that the Lord did not want any criminal to be spared. Deut. 19; Exod. 13; Prov. 17: He who acquits the wicked and he who condemns the righteous are both an abomination before the Lord.

units.la: 1. Reg. 20. Quia dimisisti virum dignum morte, erit anima tua pro anima illius.
units.tr: 1 Kings 20. Because you have let go a man worthy of death, your life shall be for his life.

units.la: III. Regula, Tametsi S. Scriptura per se fa-tis est clara: tamen expositionem piam & religiosam non recusat: imò addit ornamentum verbo Dei, & auditori fructum adfert, Exponendæ igitur sunt sacræ Scripturæ. Pa-tet hoc.
units.tr: III. Rule. Although Holy Scripture is of itself clear enough, it nevertheless does not refuse a pious and religious exposition; indeed it adds ornament to the word of God and brings fruit to the hearer. The Scriptures must therefore be expounded. This is evident.

units.la: Deus legem suam datam in monte Sina ad totam Israelis Ecclesiam, exponit ipse Ecclesiæ per Mosen, quippe qui nobis Deute-ronomium & alios quosdam libros, ceu di-vinæ legis Commentarios reliquit.
units.tr: God expounded his law given on Mount Sinai to the whole Church of Israel, expounding it himself through Moses, who left us Deuteronomy and certain other books, as commentaries on the divine law.

units.la: Prophetæ quid suis concionibus facie-bant? Legem Mosis interpretabantur, suis temporibus & hominibus applicantes illum, & sermones suos veluti enarrationes divinæ legis scriptas reliquerunt posteris.
units.tr: What did the prophets do in their sermons? They interpreted the law of Moses, applying it to their own times and people, and they left their sermons, written out as explanations of the divine law, to posterity.

units.la: Neh. 8. Attulit sacerdos Esdra legem li-brum Mosis, & stetit super turriculam li-gneam, nimirum in S. Cathedra, & aperuit Esdra librum coram Ecclesia, & legerunt in libro legis Dei luculenter, explicantes sen-sum & erudientes inter legendum. Ecce, quod non tantum legerunt Leuitæ, sed etiam exposuerunt legem Dei.
units.tr: Neh. 8. The priest Ezra brought the book of the law of Moses and stood upon a wooden pulpit, namely the holy chair, and Ezra opened the book before the Church, and they read in the book of the law of God clearly, explaining the sense and instructing while reading. See, they not only read but also expounded the law of God, not only the Levites.

units.la: Christus ipse ingressus Synagogam Na-zarethanam, expoluit locum illum Ies. 61. Spiritus Domini super me, &c. Luc. 4.
units.tr: Christ himself, entering the synagogue of Nazareth, expounded that passage of Isaiah 61: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, etc. Luke 4.

units.la: Luc. 24. Incipiens a Mose & a Prophetis, interpretabatur illis scripturas.
units.tr: Luke 24. Beginning from Moses and the Prophets, he interpreted to them the Scriptures.

units.la: Actor. 2. Petrus interpretabatur Psalmum 16. de Christo resurgente, & alibi alias scri-pturas.
units.tr: Acts 2. Peter interpreted Psalm 16 concerning the resurrected Christ, and other Scriptures elsewhere.

units.la: Actor. 8. Philippus interpretatur vaticinium Iesaiæ Tanquam ouis ad occisionem, &c. Eunucho illi, atque ea interpretatione il-lum ad fidem Christi convertit.
units.tr: Acts 8. Philip interprets the prophecy of Isaiah, "As a sheep to the slaughter," etc., to that eunuch, and by that interpretation converts him to faith in Christ.

units.la: Paulus Apostolus semper interpretatur scrip-turas in suis Epistolis. Exponendæ igi-tur sunt scripturæ, & applicandæ locis, tem-poribus nostris, prout res postulat. IV. Reg.Tametsi verò sunt interpretandæ, non sunt tamen corrumpendæ, nostris interpretationibus scripturæ, sicut faciebant Doctores populi apud Ezechielem, contra quos ait Dominus Ezech.18. An leue vobis est, quòd pascua bona depascitis, nisi residua pascuorum vestrorum, pedibus vestris conculcetis? & bibentes limpidiores aquas, residuas pedibus vestris conturbetis? & oues meæ conculcatum pedibus depascunt, & coturbatum pedibus vestris bibunt. Igitur adhibendus est modus interpretandis scripturis, qui modus in his 7. consistit.
units.tr: The Apostle Paul always interprets the Scriptures in his Epistles. The Scriptures must therefore be expounded and applied to our places and times, as the matter requires. IV. Rule. Although they are to be interpreted, the Scriptures are nevertheless not to be corrupted by our interpretations, as the teachers of the people did in Ezekiel, against whom the Lord says in Ezekiel 34: Is it a small thing for you that you feed on the good pastures, but you must trample the rest of your pastures with your feet? And drinking the clearer waters, you must muddy the rest with your feet? And my sheep feed on what you have trampled with your feet, and drink what you have muddied with your feet. Therefore a method must be applied in interpreting the Scriptures, and this method consists of seven parts.

units.la: 1. Illa quæ ita clara sunt per se, vt interpretationem non requirant, sicuti multa sunt, non debemus peregrinis nostris interpretationibus obscurare, sed ita clara vt sunt, populo proponere. Est enim hoc vel Solem exorientem, tædis adiuuare, quò orbi clarius illucescat, vel potius obscurare, sicut multi Sophistæ fecerunt.
units.tr: 1. Those things which are so clear in themselves that they do not require interpretation, as many are, we must not obscure with our own foreign interpretations, but must set them before the people just as clear as they are. For to help the rising sun with torches is either to make it shine more brightly on the world, or rather to obscure it, as many sophists have done.

units.la: 2. Illa verò, quæ ita posita sunt, vt nostram expositionem requirant, non debemus pro nostro arbitrio interpretari, sed pro eius ingenio & sensu, qui scripturas reuelauit. Sic enim ait 2.Pet.1. Omnis prophetica scriptura non est priuatæ interpretationis. Non enim voluntate humana allata est aliquando Prophetia, sed à Spiritu sancto inspirati, locuti sunt sancti Dei homines. Igitur sensus sacræ Scripturæ, siue verbi Dei, ex ipsa Scriptura sacra petendus est, non autem ex nostro arbitrio inferendus in ipsas scripturas. Ut autem hoc commodius fiat, observandae sunt etiam hæ regulæ quæ se-quuntur.
units.tr: 2. Those things, however, which are so put that they require our exposition, we must not interpret according to our own judgment, but according to the mind and sense of him who revealed the Scriptures. For thus says 2 Peter 1: No prophecy of Scripture is of private interpretation. For prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke, moved by the Holy Spirit. Therefore the sense of Holy Scripture, or of the word of God, is to be sought from Holy Scripture itself, and not to be imported into the Scriptures themselves from our own judgment. And so that this may be done more conveniently, the following rules also are to be observed.

units.la: 3. Expositio scripturæ, non adversetur articulis fidei. Ratio prima. Paulus vult Prophetiam respondere analogiæ fidei Rom ii.[?] Prophetia vero est interpretatio scripturæ. Ratio secunda 1. Corinth.4. Habentes ergo eundem spiritum fidei, sicut scriptum est, Credidi, propter quod locutus sum, & nos credimus, quapropter & loquimur. Ergo nihil est loquendum, dicendum, nisi iuxta regulam fidei, quæ in symbolo Apostolorum, & aliis antiquissimis continetur symbolis. Verbi gratia, Iohan.14. Pater maior me est. Primo spectandus est articulus fidei in symbolo, qui ait de Christo, Filius Dei, nempe consubstantialis. Ergo non est minor Patre, quod ad Divinitatem, & substantiam attinet. Aliud igitur intelligit Christus, quam verba ipsa prima fronte offerant, & quam Ariani exponant. Tunc quærendus est sensus verus. Ita de illo, Hoc est corpus meum. Primo credimus, Christum esse in cœlis, ergo non est in pane. Hinc facile eruendus verus horum verborum sensus.
units.tr: 3. The exposition of Scripture must not be opposed to the articles of faith. First reason: Paul wills prophecy to correspond to the analogy of faith (Rom. 12). But prophecy is the interpretation of Scripture. Second reason: 1 Cor. 4: "Having therefore the same spirit of faith, as it is written, I believed, and therefore I spoke; we also believe, and therefore we speak." Therefore nothing is to be said or taught except according to the rule of faith, which is contained in the Apostles' Creed and in the other most ancient creeds. For example, John 14: "The Father is greater than I." First, the article of faith in the creed must be considered, which says of Christ that he is the Son of God, namely consubstantial. Therefore he is not less than the Father, as regards the Godhead and substance. Christ therefore means something other than the words themselves offer at first sight, and than what the Arians expound. Then the true sense must be sought. So too concerning that, "This is my body." First we believe that Christ is in heaven, therefore he is not in the bread. From this the true sense of these words is easily drawn out.

units.la: 4. Expositio non repugnet charitati Dei & proximi. Ratio: Summa enim scripturæ in iis duobus præceptis continetur, Diliges Dominum Deum tuum, &c. & proximum sicut teipsum. Matth.22. In iis duobus mandatis, pendet lex & Prophetæ. Ideo Augustinus de doctrina Christiana, lib.1.cap.36.
units.tr: 4. The exposition must not conflict with the love of God and of neighbour. Reason: the sum of Scripture is contained in those two precepts, "You shall love the Lord your God," etc., and "your neighbour as yourself." Matt. 22: "On these two commandments hang all the law and the Prophets." Therefore Augustine, On Christian Doctrine, book 1, chapter 36:

units.la: Quisquis scripturas diuinas, vel quamlibet earum partem intellexisse sibi videtur, ita vt eo intellectu non adificet ista geminam charitatem Dei & proximi, nondum intellexit. Quisquis vero inde talem sententiam duxerit, vt huic adi-ficandæ charitati sit vtilis: nec tamen hoc dixe-rit, quod ille, quem legit, eo loco sensisse[?] proba-tur: nō perniciosè fallitur, nec omnino mentitur.
units.tr: Whoever believes that he has understood the divine Scriptures, or any part of them, but does not by that understanding build up this twofold love of God and neighbour, has not yet understood. Whoever, however, draws from them such a meaning as is useful for building up this love, and yet does not say that the one whom he reads is shown to have meant that in that place, is not perniciously deceived, nor does he lie at all.

units.la: Ergo cauendum, ne nostra interpretatio charitatem lædat. Verbi gratia. Ne resistatis malo, si etiam Magistratui hæc dicta esse interpretetur, lædimus charitatem proximi, salutem periclitantium, offensorum defen-sionem. Tunc enim latrones contumeliosi opprimunt viduas, pupillos, &c. & regnabit omnis iniquitas.
units.tr: Therefore we must take care that our interpretation does not harm charity. For example: "Do not resist evil"; if this is interpreted as also said to the magistrate, we harm the love of neighbour, the safety of those in danger, and the defence of the wronged. For then abusive robbers oppress widows, orphans, etc., and all iniquity will reign.

units.la: 5. Expositio excutiat præcedentia & consequentia, & omnes circumstantias. 1. ex-pendendum qua occasione quid dicatur, quid præcedat, quid sequatur, quo tempo-re aut modo, aut de qua persona aliquid di-ctum sit. Verbi gratia. Roman.4.& Galat.3. Paulus obseruauit circumstantiam tempo-ris, quando scilicet Abrahæ facta fuerit pro-missio, & ipse crediderit: & tunc conclusit, neque circumcisione, neque lege fuisse iu-stificatum. Item Petro dicitur Luc.22. Con-verte gladium in vaginam. Consideranda est persona, cui dicitur, Qui gladio ferit, gladio peribit. Erat priuata persona, non Magistratus. Ergo locus iste non est Inter-pretandus de Magistratu.
units.tr: 5. The exposition must examine what goes before and what follows, and all the circumstances. 1. We must weigh on what occasion something is said, what precedes it, what follows, at what time or in what manner, and about what person something has been said. For example, Rom. 4 and Gal. 3: Paul observed the circumstance of time, namely when the promise was made to Abraham and he himself believed, and then he concluded that he was justified neither by circumcision nor by the law. Likewise it is said to Peter, Luke 22: "Put your sword back into its sheath." The person to whom it is said must be considered: "He who strikes with the sword shall perish by the sword." He was a private person, not a magistrate. Therefore that passage is not to be interpreted of the magistrate.

units.la: 6. Expositio fiat per collat'onem aliorum locorum scripturae: obscuriores, per clariores: pauciores, per plures sunt exponendi. Verbi gratia. Johan. 14 .Pater maior me est, cogitandum, quod alibi dictum, Ego & Pater unum sumus.
units.tr: 6. The exposition should be made by collating other passages of Scripture: the more obscure passages by the clearer ones, the fewer by the more numerous. For example, John 14: "The Father is greater than I" should be considered together with what is said elsewhere: "I and the Father are one."

units.la: Jacobi 2. Abraham pater ille noster, non-ne ex operibus iustificatus est, cum obtulis[?]-set filium suum Isaac super altare? Cogitandum, quòd Paulus saepe dixit, Abrahamum ex fide, sine operibus iustificatum esse. Idem etiam Jacobus ipse. Hanc interpretandi rationem approbat Petrus, 2. epist. cap 1. dicendo: Et habemus firmiorem Propheti-cum sermonem, cui recte facitis quòd atten-datis, velut lucernae splendenti in obscuro loco, donec dies illucesceat, & lucifer exo-riatur in cordibus vestris.
units.tr: James 2: "Was not our father Abraham justified by works, when he offered his son Isaac upon the altar?" It should be considered that Paul often said that Abraham was justified by faith without works. James himself says the same. Peter approves this method of interpreting, 2 Peter ch. 1, saying: "And we have a more sure word of prophecy, to which you do well to take heed, as to a light shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts."

units.la: Item Tertullianus ait, Haereticos consue-uisse quaedam ex scripturis ad suam sententiam decerpere, non intueri cetera.
units.tr: Likewise Tertullian says that heretics have been accustomed to pick out certain things from Scripture for their own opinion, without looking at the rest.

units.la: 7. Expositio fiat ex pectore religioso, & cum orationibus: sit animus interpretetis, gloriae Dei, & salutis proximi amans, non ambitiosus, non prauis corruptus affectibus: ardeat studio prouehendi virtutes, & odio scelerum omnium: ne admittat prudentiam humanam in consilium, aut sophistam, oret autem Deum, ut Spiritum sanctum sibi det, quò possit interpretari iuxta genuinum sensum ipsius Dei. Nam ab unoquovis fideli interprete, cui hoc curæ est, ne verbum Dei adulteretur aut corrumpatur, hæc tria requiruntur. 1. Rectus Dei Zelus, 2. Ut meminerit, se negotium Dei agere: ideo nil proferendum, nisi quod est ex Deo, 3. Ut cogitet, nil nisi spectatore Deo se agere, ut omnia ad eius iudicium referat.
units.tr: 7. The exposition should be made from a religious heart, and with prayers. The mind of the interpreter should love the glory of God and the salvation of his neighbour; it should not be ambitious, nor corrupted by wicked affections. It should burn with zeal to advance virtues and with hatred of all sins. Let him not admit human prudence as counsellor, or a sophist, but let him pray God to give him the Holy Spirit, so that he may interpret according to the genuine sense of God himself. For from every faithful interpreter who takes care that the Word of God not be adulterated or corrupted, these three things are required: (1) a right zeal for God; (2) that he remember he is doing God's business, and therefore put forward nothing except what is from God; (3) that he think he does nothing except with God as witness, and so refer everything to his judgment.

units.la: Hæc tria Paulus habet 2. Corinth. 2. di-cendo: Non sumus sicut multi adulterantes verbum Dei: sed tanquam ex sinceritate, tanquam ex Deo, in conspectu Dei, de Chri-sto loquimur.
units.tr: Paul has these three things in 2 Corinthians 2, saying: "We are not, like many, adulterating the Word of God; but as of sincerity, as from God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ."

units.la: Summa. Ad veram scripturarum intelli-gentiam consequendam, tria pernecessaria sunt.
units.tr: Summary. To attain a true understanding of the Scriptures, three things are most necessary.

units.la: Primò, Animus humilis atque docilis, hoc est, ut in hanc scholam Spiritus S. in-grediamur animo ab omni superbia suique fiducia, atque ab omnibus præiudiciis vacuo:& ut quæ Spiritus sanctus docet, disca-mus, non autem, ut dictis aliquot ipsius præ-ceptoris, ad nostra abutamur somnia.
units.tr: First, a humble and teachable mind; that is, that we enter this school of the Holy Spirit with a mind free from all pride and self-confidence, and from all prejudices; and that we learn what the Holy Spirit teaches, and do not misuse the sayings of some teacher to fit our own dreams.

units.la: Deinde, diligens scripturarum inter se collatio, & ad regulam fidei examinatio. Sunt enim scripturæ per scripturas inter-pretandæ, ita ut nullum admittamus sensum, qui cum aliis scripturis, & cum principiis fidei non sit consentaneus.
units.tr: Next, a careful comparison of Scripture with Scripture, and examination by the rule of faith. For Scriptures are to be interpreted by Scriptures, so that we admit no sense which is not consistent with other Scriptures and with the principles of faith.

units.la: Postremò in scripturis semper quæra-mus Christum, eiusque gloriam tanquam scopum & finem scripturarum omnium. Qui enim habet Filium, habet & Patrem, & u-triusque Spiritum. Quifecus fecerit, is in multos labatur errores, necesse est, quia nunquam intelliget scripturas. Et sic videmus usu venisse omnibus haereticis. Unde enim tanta scripturarum ignoratio, & dein-detot errores & blasphemiae in Mundo, quâ ex hoc fonte & orti sunt, & aucti in immen-sum?nempe, quòd aut scripturas non legerint, aut si legant, primùm non adferunt animum docilem: nec conferunt scripturas cum scripturis: nec denique quaerunt Christum, & gloriam eius, sed potius scripturis abutun-tur, contra Christum. Ne igitur id ipsum et-iam nobis usu veniat, danda nobis est opera, ut contrà quàm isti faciunt, nos geramus, atque inprimis, ut adferamus animum hu-milem, docilem, Christi amantem, gloriae illius cupidum, & veritatis sitientem.
units.tr: Finally, in the Scriptures we should always seek Christ and his glory, as the aim and end of all Scripture. For he who has the Son has the Father also, and the Spirit of both. Whoever seeks otherwise will necessarily fall into many errors, because he will never understand the Scriptures. And so we see that this has happened to all heretics. For whence came such great ignorance of the Scriptures, and then such errors and blasphemies in the world, which arose from this source and have grown immensely? Namely, because they either did not read the Scriptures, or if they read them, first did not bring a teachable mind, nor compared Scripture with Scripture, nor finally sought Christ and his glory, but rather misused the Scriptures against Christ. Therefore, lest the same thing happen to us, we must take pains to act contrary to what they do, and above all to bring a humble, teachable mind, which loves Christ, desires his glory, and thirsts for truth.

units.la: V. Reg. Ius interpretandi scripturas, non est penes solum Pontificem Romanum, aut Concilia ab ipso congregata: sed penes totam Ecclesiam, & eos inprimis, quibus datum est hoc donum 1. Corinth. 12. Alij datur interpretatio sermonum. Alij Prophetia, hoc est, (ut Ambrosius interpretatur) donum interpretandi scripturas. Rom. 12. Habentes autem diuersa dona, pro gratia, quae nobis data est, siue Prophetiam (prophete-mus) secundùm analogiam fidei. Num.11.[?] Utinâ universus populus Iehouae Prophetae essent, & daret Iehoua spiritum suû super eos.
units.tr: V. Rule. The right to interpret the Scriptures does not belong only to the Roman Pontiff, or to councils convened by him; but it belongs to the whole Church, and especially to those to whom this gift has been given: 1 Corinthians 12: "To another is given the interpretation of speeches; to another prophecy, that is (as Ambrose interprets it) the gift of interpreting Scripture." Romans 12: "Having different gifts according to the grace given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the analogy of faith." Numbers 11: "Would that all the people of the LORD were prophets, and that the LORD would put his Spirit upon them!"

units.la: Iud. 4. Debbora mulier excitatur in Prophetam.
units.tr: Judges 4: Deborah, a woman, is raised up as a prophetess.

units.la: Amos.7. Non sum Propheta,neque filius Prophetæ: & tamen datum ei donum prophetandi & interpretandi Mosen.
units.tr: Amos 7: "I am not a prophet, nor the son of a prophet"; yet the gift of prophesying and interpreting was given to him, as to Moses.

units.la: 1. Thessal.5. Omnia probate,quod bonum est, tenete. Scribit autem ad totam Ecclesiam.
units.tr: 1 Thessalonians 5: "Prove all things; hold fast what is good." He writes to the whole Church.

units.la: 1. Iohan.4. Nolite omni Spiritui credere, sed probate spiritus utrum ex Deo sint. Ad omnes fideles scribit. Iudicium igitur de scripturis, & de doctrinis, non est penes unum Pontificem Romanum: sed penes illos in Ecclesia, qui hoc donum acceperunt.
units.tr: 1 John 4: "Do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are from God." He writes to all the faithful. Judgment concerning Scriptures and doctrines therefore does not belong to the one Roman Pontiff, but to those in the Church who have received this gift.

units.la: Nam in interpretatione scripturæ Papa Romanus non tantum errare potest: sed etiam sæpe erravit: si quidem multa[?] scripturarum loca partim impiè, partim inepte explicavit.
units.tr: For in the interpretation of Scripture the Roman Pope not only can err, but has often erred; indeed he has explained many passages of Scripture, partly impiously and partly foolishly.

units.la: 1. Corinth. 3. Quòd si quis super ædificet super fundamentum hoc aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos, ligna, fœnum, stipulam, cuiusque opus manifestum fiet. Dies enim declarabit. Nam per ignem revelabitur, & cuiusque opus quale sit, ignis probabit: Papa Gregorius & alij exponunt de peccatis venialibus fidelium & de igne purgatorio. Secus tamen Hieronymus, Ambrosius Augustinus, Chrysostomus. Vide in suis locis.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 3: "But if anyone builds on this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw, his work will be made manifest. For the day will declare it, because it will be revealed by fire, and the fire will test what sort of work each one's is." Pope Gregory and others explain this of the venial sins of the faithful and of purgatorial fire. Hieronymus, Ambrose, Augustine and Chrysostom, however, explain it otherwise. See them in their places.

units.la: Rom. 8. Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt: Siricius Papa Tom. 1. Concil. interpretatur de illis, qui sunt in matrimonio.
units.tr: Romans 8: "Those who are in the flesh cannot please God." Pope Siricius, in the first volume of the Councils, interprets it of those who are in marriage.

units.la: 1. Corinth. 7. Ne fraudetis vos invicem, nisi si quid ex consensu ad tempus, ut vacetis ieiunio & precationi, Siricius Papa Tom.1. Concil. inter decreta Siricij, hoc loco abutitur, imò corrumpit dicendo: Praeterea quod dignum, & pudicum, & honestum est, suademus, ut Sacerdotes & Levitae cum uxoribus non coëant, quia in Ministerio Ministri quotidianis necessitatibus occupantur. Ad Co-rinthios namque Apostolus scribens, ait: Abstinete, ut vacetis orationi. Siigitur Laicis abstinentia imperatur, ut possint deprecantes audiri: quanto magis Sacerdos utique omni momento paratus esse debet, munditiae puritate securus, ne aut sacrificium offerat, &c. qui si contaminatus est carnali concupiscentia, quid faciet?
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 7: "Do not defraud one another, except perhaps by consent for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to fasting and prayer." Pope Siricius, in the first volume of the Councils, among the decrees of Siricius, misuses this passage here, or rather corrupts it, saying: "Moreover, we advise what is worthy, chaste and honourable, that priests and Levites should not cohabit with their wives, because in the ministry ministers are occupied with daily necessities. For the Apostle, writing to the Corinthians, says: 'Abstain, that you may devote yourselves to prayer.' If abstinence is therefore enjoined on the laity, that they may be heard when they pray, how much more ought a priest to be ready at every moment, secure in the purity of chastity, lest he offer sacrifice, etc. If he is polluted by carnal lust, what will he do?"

units.la: Primò falsum est, quod ait, à Paulo imperari abstinentiam à congressu cum uxoribus: imò aperte contrarium demonstrat Apostolus. Hoc autem dico (inquit) κατὰ συγγνώ-μην, οὐ κατ' ἐπιταγὴν[?].
units.tr: First, it is false that he says abstinence from intercourse with wives is commanded by Paul; indeed the Apostle clearly shows the opposite. "But this I say" (he says) "by way of concession, not by way of command" [κατὰ συγγνώμην, οὐ κατ' ἐπιταγήν].

units.la: Secundò, falsum quod ait, ideo hanc praecipi Laicis, ut possint deprecantes audiri: quasi vero Coniuges non possint exaudiri, nisi abstineant à coitu.
units.tr: Second, it is false that he says this is commanded to the laity so that they may be heard when they pray; as if married people could not be heard unless they abstained from coition.

units.la: Tertiò, quod infert, sacerdoti non licere ministrare sacris, nisi abstineat ab uxore, damnatum fuit in Concilio Niceno: quòd congressus legitimus coniugum, castitas sit, non immundicia.
units.tr: Third, what he infers, that it is not lawful for a priest to minister in sacred things unless he abstains from his wife, was condemned at the Council of Nicaea, which held that the lawful intercourse of spouses is chastity, not uncleanness.

units.la: Item in Concilio Gangrensi cap. 4. damnatur, qui coniugem Sacerdotem discernit, tanquam propter nuptias offerre non debeat.
units.tr: Likewise, in the Council of Gangra, canon 4, one is condemned who separates from a priest's wife, as if, on account of marriage, he ought not to offer.

units.la: Tit.1. Omnia munda mundis: coinquinatis autem omnia sunt immunda: Siricius Papa Tomo 1. Concil. inter decreta Siricij, cap.7. sic interpretatur: Quaecunque administrant Sacerdotes in Ecclesia, immunda esse, nisi abstineant à congressu vxorum, quòd ille congressus faciat illos immundos.
units.tr: Titus 1: "To the pure all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure." Pope Siricius, in the first volume of the Councils, among the decrees of Siricius, chapter 7, interprets it thus: whatever priests administer in the Church is unclean, unless they abstain from intercourse with their wives, because that intercourse makes them unclean.

units.la: 1.Corinth. 7. Propter fornicationem, quisque habeat suam vxorem, &c. Gregorius Papa primus in Moralibus parte 6. lib.32. cap. 55 [?]. & 56. & citatur in Decret. dist.13. ait hic Apostolum cōcessisse minimum peccatum, vt euitentur maiora: id est, matrimonium, vt euitetur fornicatio, & adulterium.
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 7: "Because of fornication, let each man have his own wife, etc." Pope Gregory the First, in the Moralia, part 6, book 32, chapters 55 and 56, and cited in the Decretum, distinction 13, says here that the Apostle has granted the lesser sin so that greater sins may be avoided: that is, marriage, so that fornication and adultery may be avoided.

units.la: Concilia etiam errare possunt, & multa errarunt, quoties scilicet à verbo Dei defle-xerunt.
units.tr: Councils too can err, and have often erred, whenever they have departed from the Word of God.

units.la: Ephesina secunda Synodus, Eutychetis errorem probauit, eumque absoluit, quem postea Chalcedonensis damnauit. Fuit autem illa synodus conuocata, legitima, sicut & Nicena, per Imperatorem. Aderant legati Romanae etiam Ecclesiae. Praerat, suo iure, Antiochenus Episcopus.
units.tr: The Second Council of Ephesus approved the error of Eutyches and acquitted him, whom the later Council of Chalcedon condemned. That synod was convened lawfully, as the Council of Nicaea was, by the Emperor. Legates of the Roman Church were present. The bishop of Antioch presided, by his own right.

units.la: Chalcedonensis reprehenditur à Leone Episcopo Romano, quòd locum secundum dederint Constantinopolitanæ Ecclesiæ, postposita Alexandrina, decretumque Concilij Niceni resciderint. Constantinopolitana septima, quæ sub Irene fuit, imagines earumque cultum probat, quas tamen & quem damnarat Constantinopolitana, quæ sub Leone coacta fuerat.
units.tr: The Council of Chalcedon is rebuked by Leo, bishop of Rome, because they gave second place to the Church of Constantinople, placing it before Alexandria, and annulled the decree of the Council of Nicaea. The seventh Council of Constantinople, which was held under Irene, approves images and their worship, though Constantinople, which met under Leo, had condemned them and the worship of them.

units.la: VI. Reg. Patrum scripta, ad verbum Dei sunt examinanda, & quatenus ei sunt conformia, recipienda sunt: quatenus non conformia, respuenda. Augustinus Tom.7. contra Cresconium Grammaticum, lib. 2. cap. 32. nitentem authoritate Epistolæ Cypriani, ait: Ego huius Epistolæ authoritate non teneor: quia literas Cypriani non vt Canonicas habeo, sed eas ex Canonicis considero: & quod in eis diuinarum scripturarum authoritati congruit, cum laude eius accipio: quod autem non congruit, cum pace eius respuo. Nam etiam Patres quædam scripturarum loca ineptè sunt interpretati.
units.tr: The writings of the Fathers, Rule 6: they must be examined by the Word of God, and received insofar as they agree with it, and rejected insofar as they do not. Augustine, in volume 7 against Cresconius the grammarian, book 2, chapter 32, when he relies on the authority of an epistle of Cyprian, says: "I am not bound by the authority of this epistle, because I do not hold the letters of Cyprian as canonical, but I weigh them by the canonical books; and whatever in them agrees with the authority of the divine Scriptures, I accept with praise; whatever does not agree, I reject with due respect. For even the Fathers interpreted some passages of Scripture inaptly."

units.la: 1.Cor.7. Quòd si nupserit virgo, non peccauit, &c.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7. "But if a virgin marry, she has not sinned," etc.

units.la: Theophylactus excipit virgines Deo dicatas, & ait illas peccare, si nubant, quia nuptæ sunt Christo. Ideo adulterium committunt, si nubant viris. Sic etiam Romani Pontifices exponunt. Quasi verò non omnes Christiani sint Sponsæ, nuptæ Christo, vt ait idem Apostolus. Et spirituale illud connubium cum Christo, non maculatur connubio corporali cum viris. Apostolus etiam ostendit, se loqui de omnibus virginibus promiscuè, cum ait: De virginibus autem præceptum Domini non habeo. De omni igitur virgine etiam loquitur, cùm ait: Quòd si nupserit virgo, non peccauit. Et Cyprianus ad Pomp. lib.1.cap.11. iubet virgines Deo dicatas, si non velint, aut non possint se continere, viris nubere. Melius enim esse vt nubant, quàm vt in ignem suis deliciis cadant.
units.tr: Theophylact excepts virgins dedicated to God, and says they sin if they marry, because they are wedded to Christ; therefore they commit adultery if they marry men. The Roman Pontiffs also explain it this way. As though all Christians were not brides, wedded to Christ, as the same Apostle says! That spiritual marriage with Christ is not defiled by a bodily marriage with men. The Apostle also shows that he speaks of all virgins without distinction, when he says: "Concerning virgins I have no command of the Lord." Therefore he speaks of every virgin when he says: "But if a virgin marry, she has not sinned." And Cyprian, to Pomponius, book 1, chapter 11, bids virgins dedicated to God, if they do not wish or are not able to contain themselves, to marry men. For it is better that they marry than that they fall into the fire through their pleasures.

units.la: 1.Corinth.7. Qui habent vxores, sint tanquam non habentes, &c. Hieronymus ita interpretatur, quòd Apostolus hortetur coniuges ad continentiam: sint tanquam non habentes, id est, ne illis vtantur, sed ab eis abstineant. Quid igitur est, quòd Apostolus supra iussit, dicendo: Vir debitam reuerentiam exhibeat vxori, & vxor viro? Non est autem contrarius sibi Apostolus. Non igitur hic hortatur ad continentiam ab vsu vxoris.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7. "Those who have wives should be as though they had none," etc. Jerome interprets this to mean that the Apostle exhorts married persons to continence: "should be as though they had none," that is, they should not use them, but abstain from them. What then is the meaning of the Apostle's command above, when he says: "Let the husband render to his wife her due benevolence, and the wife to her husband"? The Apostle is not contrary to himself. Therefore he does not here exhort to continence from the use of a wife.

units.la: Ambrosius melius: Non debere Christianum ad generandum esse solicitum, neque ad ipsum vsum debitum. Iuxta Ambrosium igitur Paulus non dehortatur à generatione & vsu vxoris: sed tantùm docet, non debere Christianum hominem plus æquo propensum esse ad vxoris vsum, & ad generandum. Quare non abstinentiam, sed temperatum vxoris vsum requirit à viro Christiano. Verus autem sensus est, non debere hominem corde & amore nimium affici ergavxorem, ita vt ille nimius amor impedimento illi fit,nę[?] Christum constanter in tri-bulatione & persecutionibus confiteatur & sequatur.
units.tr: Ambrose interprets better: that a Christian ought not to be anxious about begetting children, nor about the due use of marriage itself. According to Ambrose, then, Paul does not dissuade from begetting and from the use of a wife, but only teaches that a Christian man ought not to be inclined to his wife's use and to begetting more than is fitting. Therefore he requires of a Christian husband not abstinence but a moderate use of his wife. The true sense, however, is that a man ought not to be too greatly affected in heart and love towards his wife, so that such excessive love becomes a hindrance to him from constantly confessing and following Christ in tribulation and persecutions.

units.la: 1. Corinth. 9. Annon habemus, potestatem circumducendi ἀδελφὴν[?] γυναῖκα ? Ἀδελφὸν, id est, sororem in Christo, Christianam. γυναῖκα vxorem. γυνὴ enim vxorem significat 1.Corinth.7. Hieronymus interpretatur de quibusdam matronis opulentis, quas Apostoli circumducebant, vt ab eis sibi victus suppeditaretur. Paulum vero noluisse vti hoc iure, cum posset: & hoc totum facit, vt concludat, Apostolos non habuisse vxores.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 9. "Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife?" The Greek word ἀδελφὴν is "sister," that is, a sister in Christ, a Christian woman; γυναῖκα is "wife," for γυνὴ signifies a wife, 1 Cor. 7. Jerome interprets this of certain wealthy matrons whom the Apostles led about, so that sustenance might be supplied to them by them. But Paul would not use this right, although he could; and this whole passage serves to conclude that the Apostles did not have wives.

units.la: Hæc expositio pugnat cum verbis Apostoli: item cum historiis, & Patribus vetustioribus Hieronymo, Ignatio scilicet & Clemente, & Eusebio Cæsar. Vide Muscu-lum in locis Communibus pag. 263. ex professo hoc argumentum tractantem.
units.tr: This explanation conflicts with the words of the Apostle, and likewise with the histories and the older Fathers, namely Jerome, Ignatius, Clement, and Eusebius of Caesarea. See Musculus in his Common Places, page 263, where he treats this argument expressly.
